t: Permit-to-Work (PTW) System
purpose: Control non-routine, high-risk work by making hazards, precautions, isolations and authorisations explicit and signed before work starts, and by formally handing the area back afterwards.
scope: Hot work, confined space entry, work at height, excavation, electrical (energised/HT), lifting with cranes, radiography, working on pressurised/chemical systems, roof work, demolition, vehicle entry to process areas, night work in restricted areas.
roles: Permit Issuer / Area Authority (operations owner of the area)
Permit Receiver / Performing Authority (supervisor of the work party)
Fire Watch / Standby person where required
hazards: Undetected residual energy or pressure
Simultaneous operations (SIMOPS) interacting
Unclear boundaries or expiry leading to work continuing in changed conditions
Permit treated as paperwork rather than control
pre: Written PTW procedure approved by site management; permit types and forms defined (OISD-STD-105 / HSG250 as model)
Trained and authorised issuers/receivers (register of signatories with validity)
Permit board or e-PTW register visible at control point
Risk assessment / JSA attached for the task
Isolation certificates (electrical, process) and gas test where applicable
steps: Define the job: location (tag/grid), equipment ID, description, duration, number of persons.
Identify hazards with the receiver on site (walk-down), referencing the JSA/HIRA.
Specify precautions: isolations (lock/tag numbers), draining/purging, gas test limits, barricading, fire watch, rescue arrangements, PPE.
Check SIMOPS: cross-reference other live permits in the area; attach interlocks (e.g. no hot work while confined-space entry open below).
Issuer and receiver sign; display original at worksite, copy at control point/permit board.
Validity: typically one shift (max 8–12 h); extension only by re-verification and re-signature; gas test repeated at intervals and after breaks.
Supervisor carries out toolbox talk on permit conditions with the crew; crew signs attendance.
During work: receiver stays on site; stop work if conditions change (alarm, weather, new work nearby); issuer or safety officer audit a sample of permits daily.
Suspend permit for emergencies/alarms; re-validate before resumption.
Close-out: receiver confirms area clean, tools removed, guards/covers refitted; issuer inspects and signs close; de-isolation only after closure of all permits on that isolation.
File permits for the retention period (typically ≥ 1 year; 3 years for MAH units) and trend audit findings.
ppe: As specified per permit type
stop: Gas reading beyond limits
Fire/gas alarm or site emergency
Permit expired or signatory absent
Unexpected energy source found
records: Permit forms (numbered), isolation register, gas-test log, permit audit sheet

t: Hot Work (Welding, Cutting, Grinding, Brazing)
purpose: Prevent fires, explosions and burns from sparks, open flame, hot surfaces and fumes.
scope: Any work producing flame, sparks or temperatures able to ignite materials: arc/gas welding, oxy-fuel cutting, grinding, brazing, soldering, heat-gun bitumen work, thermite, powder-actuated tools.
hazards: Ignition of combustibles within 11 m (35 ft) incl. hidden voids, floors below, ducts
Flammable vapour/gas (tanks, drums, drains, sewers)
Welding fumes (manganese, chromium VI, ozone), UV radiation, electric shock from welding sets
Cylinder incidents (acetylene flashback, oxygen enrichment)
Falls when welding at height; dropping hot slag on people below
pre: Hot-work permit issued (except in designated welding shops)
Gas test where any flammable may be present: 0% LEL for hot work in/near process plant (OISD); < 10% LEL general sites never acceptable for hot work — aim 0%
Fire extinguishers (min 2 × 9 kg DCP / CO2, or as permit) within reach; fire blanket; water supply
Combustibles removed to 11 m or covered with fire-resistant blankets; floor openings sealed; drains covered
Equipment inspected: cables, earth clamp, regulators, flashback arrestors (both ends), hoses, gauges
steps: Inspect area with issuer; identify combustibles, openings and adjacent work (SIMOPS).
Isolate/clean equipment to be welded: drain, purge, gas-free certificate for tanks/vessels (API 2015/2016 or OISD).
Establish exclusion/screens; post warning signs; protect people below with spark containment (fire blanket, sheeting).
Position fire watch with extinguisher; fire watch has no other duties during hot work and for ≥ 30 min after (NFPA 51B: 60 min typical in process areas; monitor up to 3 h).
Verify welder competence (IS 817 / structural code / IBR for pressure parts) and equipment earthing; welding return cable clamped close to the work.
Oxy-fuel: open cylinder valves slowly, acetylene ≤ 1 bar (15 psi), check leaks with soap solution, never oil on oxygen fittings, cylinders upright and secured, flashback arrestors fitted.
Perform work; re-test gas at intervals specified (typically every 2 h and after any break).
Local exhaust ventilation or fume extraction for stainless, galvanised, coated steel; respirator where LEV not feasible.
Stop at expiry; cool/quench slag; inspect area including below/behind; fire watch continues; sign permit close.
Report any flash fire or near miss; review JSA.
ppe: Welding helmet (auto-darkening shade 9–13) / cutting goggles shade 5
Leather gauntlets, apron/jacket, FR coveralls
Safety boots, helmet (welding helmet compatible), ear plugs
Respirator (P2/P3 or PAPR for Cr VI) where needed
stop: LEL reading above 0% in process area / any detectable flammable gas
Fire watch unavailable
Combustibles cannot be removed or protected
Wet conditions with electric welding without protection
records: Hot-work permit, gas-test log, fire-watch log, welder certificates, equipment inspection tag

t: Confined Space Entry
purpose: Prevent asphyxiation, poisoning, fire/explosion, engulfment and entrapment in spaces not designed for continuous occupancy.
scope: Tanks, vessels, silos, pits, manholes, sewers, pipelines, ducts, excavations deeper than 1.2 m with poor ventilation, boilers, tunnels, lift shafts, STP chambers, large-diameter piles.
roles: Rescue team (trained, equipment at point of entry)
hazards: Oxygen deficiency (< 19.5%) or enrichment (> 23.5%)
Toxic gases: H2S, CO, CO2, solvent vapours; flammable gas
Engulfment by solids/liquids; moving parts; heat; noise; limited egress
Hazards introduced by the work (welding fumes, coatings, inert gas purging)
pre: Confined-space register and signage at site; spaces classified (permit-required vs non-permit)
Written permit; isolation of inlets/outlets (blind/spade, lock, disconnect — not just valve closure)
Calibrated 4-gas detector (bump test same day); continuous monitoring
Forced ventilation (fresh air, not pure oxygen); lighting (24 V or intrinsically safe)
Rescue plan tested; retrieval system (tripod/winch) for vertical entry; communication method
steps: Identify and isolate all sources: energy (LOTO), process lines (blind), gravity/engulfment; drain, clean, purge and ventilate.
Gas-test from outside at top/middle/bottom before entry: O2 19.5–23.5%, LEL < 10% (0% for hot work), H2S < 10 ppm (TWA), CO < 25 ppm (ACGIH TLV; OSHA PEL 50 ppm). Record readings and time.
Entry supervisor issues permit listing hazards, limits, ventilation, PPE, rescue, duration.
Attendant posted at entrance with entrant log, communication (radio/voice/line), means to summon rescue; attendant never enters.
Entrants wear harness with lifeline attached to retrieval where feasible; carry personal gas monitor with alarm.
Continue ventilation; monitor continuously; re-test after breaks and at least every 2 h or as permit states.
No cylinders of compressed gas inside the space (except SCBA); torch hoses removed during breaks; no solvent use without respirator plan.
Evacuate immediately on alarm, ventilation failure, unusual odour/dizziness, or external emergency; never attempt rescue without SCBA/retrieval — most multiple fatalities are would-be rescuers.
On completion: head-count entrants out, remove tools, close permit, reinstate isolations only after permit closure, replace covers/guards.
Medical: workers fit for confined space (no claustrophobia, cardio-respiratory fitness).
ppe: Full-body harness with retrieval line
Personal 4-gas monitor
Helmet, boots, gloves, eye protection, coveralls
Respirator: SCBA/airline if atmosphere cannot be made safe (never a filter mask for O2 deficiency)
stop: Any gas reading outside limits
Attendant leaves post
Ventilation fails
Rescue team/equipment unavailable
records: Entry permit, gas-test log, entrant/attendant log, rescue drill records, detector calibration

t: Lockout / Tagout – Control of Hazardous Energy
purpose: Prevent unexpected start-up or release of stored energy (electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, chemical, thermal, gravity) during servicing and maintenance.
scope: All maintenance, cleaning, un-jamming, inspection and set-up where a person could be injured by energisation or movement; includes process isolation (valves, blinds) and temporary site power.
hazards: Electrocution; crushing; entanglement; release of pressure/chemicals; falling parts
Stored energy: capacitors, springs, raised loads, flywheels, pressurised accumulators
Remote/auto restart via PLC, timers, interlocks
Multiple crews on one isolation (group lockout failures)
pre: Equipment-specific energy control procedures (ECP) written for each machine/system
Personal locks (one key), tags, hasps, lock boxes; isolation points labelled
Training: authorised, affected, other; annual periodic inspection of each ECP (OSHA 1910.147(c)(6))
Voltage tester (proved before/after on known live source); pressure gauge; blinding register
steps: Prepare: identify all energy sources from drawings/ECP; notify affected employees.
Shut down equipment using normal stop controls.
Isolate every energy source: open breakers/disconnects (not just pushbutton/emergency stop), close & lock valves, insert blinds, disconnect links.
Apply lock and tag at each isolation point; each worker applies own lock (group: lock box with master key).
Release/restrain stored energy: bleed pressure, discharge capacitors, block raised parts, let hot parts cool, restrain springs.
Verify zero energy: attempt start (then return control to OFF), test with proved voltage tester on all phases, check gauges/vents.
Perform work; if shifts change, outgoing lock removed only after incoming lock applied.
Restore: remove tools, reinstall guards, head-count, notify affected employees, remove locks (own only), re-energise with controlled start.
Lost key/absent worker: only supervisor per written procedure after verifying the person is not exposed and attempts to contact.
Review ECPs annually or on equipment change.
ppe: Electrical: arc-rated clothing per incident energy (NFPA 70E), insulated gloves (IS 4770/EN 60903) with leather protectors, face shield
Standard site PPE
stop: Isolation cannot be verified
Lock/tag missing or tampered
Energy source not on drawings found
records: Isolation certificate, lock register, ECP documents, periodic inspection record, training

t: Work at Height & Fall Protection
purpose: Prevent falls of persons and objects from any height where a fall could cause injury (edges, openings, roofs, ladders, MEWPs, scaffolds, fragile surfaces).
scope: All work where a person could fall from one level to another. Triggers: India BOCW/state rules & site practice commonly 1.8–2 m (verify state rule); OSHA construction 6 ft (1.8 m), general industry 4 ft (1.2 m); UK no minimum height.
roles: Workers trained in WAH & harness use
hazards: Fall from unprotected edge, opening, fragile roof (AC sheets, skylights)
Ladder misuse; overreaching
MEWP tip-over, entrapment, catapult
Falling tools/materials onto people below
Suspension trauma after fall arrest
pre: Hierarchy applied: avoid WAH (prefab at ground) → collective protection (guardrails, nets, covers) → work-positioning/restraint → fall arrest (last resort)
Fall-protection plan with anchor points (≥ 22 kN / 5,000 lb or engineered), clearance calculation (free-fall + deceleration + harness stretch + safety ≈ 6 m for 1.8 m lanyard)
Harness (IS 3521 / EN 361), energy-absorbing lanyard (EN 355) or SRL (EN 360), inspected pre-use and 6-monthly by competent person; tagged
Rescue plan: retrieve suspended worker within 10–15 min (MEWP, rescue kit)
Weather check: no WAH in winds > 40 km/h (MEWP/crane limits per manufacturer), lightning, heavy rain
steps: Plan the task at ground level; select the safest access (mobile scaffold/MEWP preferred over ladders for prolonged work).
Install edge protection: top rail 0.95–1.1 m (OSHA 1.07 m ± 0.08), mid-rail, toe board ≥ 150 mm; cover and label floor openings (secured, load-rated); nets within 6 m below work surface.
Ladders: 4:1 angle, extend 1 m above landing, tied/footed, 3-point contact, no work from top 3 rungs; prohibit metal ladders near electricity.

Harness: 100% tie-off above shoulder where possible, twin-tail lanyards for moving, connect to rated anchor/lifeline — never to scaffold tubes without rated couplers or to rebar without engineered anchor.
MEWP: trained/licensed operator, daily check, outriggers on firm ground, harness with short restraint lanyard in boom-type, no climbing on rails, ground-rescue controls known.
Roof work: fragile-roof survey, crawling boards, edge protection, staging; no work on wet AC sheets.
Control dropped objects: tool lanyards, debris netting, exclusion zone below with barricade and signage.
Supervisor monitors; stop work if weather changes.
Rescue drill at project start and quarterly.
Daily visual check of harness/lanyard; remove from service after any fall arrest.
ppe: Full-body harness with dorsal D-ring
Energy-absorbing lanyard/SRL
Chin-strapped helmet (EN 397 with chin strap / IS 2925)
Non-slip boots; gloves; hi-vis
stop: No rated anchor available
Wind/lightning
Harness damaged or uninspected
Rescue plan not in place
records: WAH permit, harness inspection register (6-monthly), scaffold tags, MEWP daily checks, training & rescue drill records

t: Scaffolding – Erection, Inspection, Use & Dismantling
purpose: Provide a safe working platform and prevent scaffold collapse, falls and falling objects.
scope: Tube-and-coupler, cuplock/system, mobile tower, cantilever, suspended (swing-stage) and bamboo scaffolds (bamboo discouraged; if used, per IS 3696 with competent supervision).
roles: Scaffold inspector (competent person, independent of erector where possible)
hazards: Collapse: inadequate ties, foundations, bracing, overloading
Falls during erection/dismantling (no guardrails yet)
Incomplete platforms, gaps, missing toe boards
Proximity to overhead lines; mobile tower movement with persons aboard
pre: Design drawing or standard configuration (manufacturer/IS 4014/BS EN 12811); load class defined (light 1.5 kN/m², medium 2.0, heavy 3.0 — verify)
Materials inspected: tubes straight (no corrosion/dents), couplers tested, boards sound, base plates/sole boards
Ground bearing assessed; sole boards on soft ground
Tie pattern (typically every 4 m vertically × 6 m horizontally for sheeted less) and bracing
Scaffold tag system (Green = safe, Red = do not use) at each access
steps: Erect progressively with scaffolders tied off (advanced guardrail or harness to independent anchor); use ladder access bays.
Standards plumb on base plates; ledgers level; transoms at lift height; lift height ≤ 2 m; bay width adequate (boards ≥ 600 mm for working platform, 5 boards for material).
Fit ties as erection proceeds (through ties/box ties/anchor ties); never remove ties for façade work without replacing.
Platform: close-boarded, boards overhang supports 50–150 mm, no trip gaps; guardrails (top 0.95–1.0 m, mid), toe boards; brick guards where material stacked.
Access: internal ladders through trapdoors, or stair towers; no climbing frames.
Inspect before first use, after any alteration, after adverse weather, and at least every 7 days; record on tag and register.
Load control: posted SWL; no accumulation of debris; distribute materials over standards.
Mobile towers: height ≤ 3× base (outdoor) / 3.5× (indoor) unless outriggers; lock castors; never move with people/materials aloft; check overhead lines.
Suspended scaffolds: secondary safety line per worker, independent of suspension rope; daily rope/hoist check.
Dismantle in reverse order, lowering components (no throwing); keep ties until last; barricade below.
ppe: Harness & lanyard (scaffolders), helmet with chin strap, gloves, boots, hi-vis
stop: Red tag / no tag
Missing ties/bracing or guardrails
Wind > 40 km/h or lightning
Overhead line within 3 m (LV) / 6 m+ (HT) without authority
records: Scaffold design, inspection register (7-day), tags, scaffolder competence certificates, material inspection

t: Excavation, Trenching & Underground Utilities
purpose: Prevent cave-ins, utility strikes, falls into excavations, flooding, hazardous atmospheres and struck-by incidents from plant.
scope: All excavations, trenches, pits, shafts, basements; manual and machine digging; working near underground services (power, gas, water, telecom, sewer) and overhead lines.
roles: Competent person (daily inspection, soil classification, protective system)
hazards: Collapse of sides (1 m³ of soil ≈ 1.5–2 t); undermining of adjacent structures/roads
Striking live cables/gas mains; overhead line contact by excavator boom
Falls into excavation; persons struck by bucket/reversing plant
Water ingress, hazardous gases (sewer/landfill), falling spoil/materials
Excavation collapse during monsoon (Karnataka/TN June–Dec rains)
pre: Permit-to-dig after utility survey: drawings from BESCOM/TANGEDCO, gas (GAIL/IGL/AG&P), water boards, telecom; cable locator scan (CAT & Genny) and trial pits by hand

Soil classification by competent person; protective system chosen: sloping/benching (angle per soil, 1:1 for Type B equivalent; 1.5:1 for sand), shoring, trench box; design by engineer for depth > 6 m (OSHA > 20 ft)
Protective system required for depth ≥ 1.5 m (India BOCW/IS 3764) / ≥ 5 ft (OSHA) unless solid rock
Dewatering plan; discharge consent; edge protection and access ladders (within 7.5 m / 25 ft travel)
Spoil and plant kept ≥ 1 m (OSHA 2 ft min; good practice ≥ depth of trench) from edge; stop blocks for vehicles
steps: Mark services on ground (paint/flags); hand-dig within 0.5–1 m of marked services; treat all cables as live.
Set exclusion zone; hard barricade (not tape alone) ≥ 1.2 m high around open excavation, lighting at night, signage; cover small pits.

Excavate with banksman controlling plant; no one in bucket swing radius; machine at least 1 m from edge, on firm ground; overhead-line clearance maintained (≥ 3 m LT, ≥ 6 m HT — per CEA/Reg; use goal posts).
Install shoring/box progressively — never enter unprotected trench > 1.5 m; trench box top ≥ 0.45 m above trench bottom for sloped portion.
Daily inspection by competent person before each shift, after rain, blasting, vibration or any change; record (Form/register).
Provide ladders every 7.5 m, extending 1 m above surface, secured; separate pedestrian walkways with handrails for crossings.
Test atmosphere in excavations > 1.2 m deep where gases possible (near sewers, landfills, fuel tanks) — treat as confined space if criteria met.
Monsoon controls: pumps on standby, berms to divert runoff, re-inspect after every rain, stop work and evacuate in heavy rain.
Backfill in layers; compaction with plant kept clear of persons; reinstate surfaces.
Near existing structures: underpinning design, settlement monitoring, no excavation below foundation influence line without engineer's approval.
ppe: Helmet, boots, hi-vis, gloves, eye protection; harness for shaft work; gas monitor where required
stop: Unprotected trench > 1.5 m with persons inside
Water accumulating; cracks or tension cracks on surface
Unexpected service found
Spoil within 1 m of edge or plant near edge on soft ground
records: Permit-to-dig, utility clearance, daily excavation inspection register, soil classification, shoring design

t: Lifting Operations, Cranes & Rigging
purpose: Prevent dropped loads, crane overturning/collapse, contact with power lines, crushing and struck-by incidents.
scope: Mobile/crawler/tower cranes, EOT cranes, hydra (pick-and-carry), hoists, winches, chain blocks, forklifts used for lifting, material and passenger hoists, lifting gear (slings, shackles, eyebolts, spreader beams).
roles: Crane operator (licensed/competent; HMV licence for mobile crane)
hazards: Overload, out-of-radius, ground failure under outriggers, wind
Rigging failure, uncontrolled load swing, tag-line absence
Contact with overhead lines (fatal common cause in India)
Hydra cranes used beyond capacity on slopes; persons riding loads/hooks
Falling objects from height; crushing in pinch points
pre: Lifting plan (routine or complex): load weight (verified, +10% rigging), radius, chart capacity (≤ 75–85% utilisation for critical lifts), ground bearing pressure, outrigger pads, exclusion zone
Crane: valid test certificate (12-monthly by competent person, India; 'thorough examination' LOLER), load chart in cab, LMI/ASLI functional, anemometer; daily pre-use check
Lifting gear: colour-coded, SWL marked, 6-monthly (accessories) / 12-monthly (appliances) examination; register
Permit for lifts near lines, over public areas, tandem lifts, > 75% capacity, personnel baskets (last resort, engineered)
Weather: stop at wind ≥ 9–10 m/s (manufacturer), lightning, poor visibility
steps: Appointed person surveys: ground, lines, obstructions, laydown; prepares lift plan and JSA; toolbox talk.
Position crane: level (≤ 1%), outriggers fully extended on pads/mats sized for bearing pressure; distance from excavation edge ≥ 1.5 × depth or shored.
Rig load: correct sling angle (≤ 90° included; capacity reduces as angle widens), edge protectors, shackles pinned, hooks with latches, tag lines (2 for long loads).
Signaller only person giving signals (standard hand signals IS 13367 / ASME B30.5); radio for blind lifts.
Trial lift: raise 100–200 mm, check balance, brakes, LMI; then lift smoothly; no load over persons; nobody under suspended load.
Exclusion zone barricaded; load landed on stable dunnage; slings released only when load stable.
Power lines: maintain ≥ 3 m (up to 11 kV) / 6 m (above 11 kV) or per CEA table; use dedicated spotter; de-energise where possible (OSHA Table A: 10 ft to 50 kV, +0.4 in per kV).
Hydra/pick-and-carry: only on firm level ground, boom retracted, load close to ground, no persons within 5 m, never exceed chart; banned for lifts near lines.
Material/passenger hoists: licensed where state lifts act applies; gates interlocked, SWL posted, daily checks, no persons on material hoist.
Record lift, incidents and near misses; review plan for repeat lifts.

t: Demolition & Dismantling
purpose: Prevent premature collapse, falls, falling debris, utility incidents, asbestos/lead exposure and harm to the public during demolition.
scope: Partial/total demolition of buildings, structures, chimneys, tanks; mechanical, manual, cut-and-lift, deconstruction; excludes blasting (see explosives).
hazards: Unplanned collapse, loss of stability as members removed
Falls through openings/weakened floors
Dust (silica), asbestos (AC sheets, pipe lagging, gaskets), lead paint, PCBs
Live services, gas, chemical residues in tanks
Public and adjacent property; traffic; noise/vibration
pre: Structural survey & demolition method statement (sequence, props, exclusion zones) by competent engineer; local-body demolition permission
Pre-demolition hazardous materials survey (asbestos, lead, PCBs, residual chemicals, UST); removal before demolition by licensed agency; asbestos waste to authorised TSDF
All services disconnected and capped (electricity, gas, water, sewer, telecom); temporary supply for site separately
Hoarding/scaffold with debris netting, fans/catch platforms; pedestrian diversion; dust suppression; C&D waste plan (2025 Rules) with destination facility
Notify neighbours; vibration/noise monitoring near sensitive structures
steps: Establish exclusion zone ≥ 1.5 × height of structure for mechanical demolition (or as engineer specifies); gates manned.
Remove salvageable/hazardous items first; strip top-down for manual demolition; never undermine or remove load-bearing elements before upper loads removed.
Mechanical demolition: high-reach/excavator with operator cab FOPS, water spray for dust, no one within reach radius; drop zones planned.
Floors: do not overload with debris; use chutes (enclosed) for debris; openings guarded.
Monitor stability continuously; stop if unexpected movement, cracks; props as per plan.
Hot cutting of tanks/vessels only after gas-free certificate.

Handle asbestos-cement sheets whole (no breaking), wet, double-bagged, labelled, PPE (P3 respirator, disposable coveralls), decontamination; medical surveillance per state rules Schedule (TN Sch. XX asbestos 2025).
Debris transport covered; weighbridge/manifest for C&D waste; concrete to recycler.
End of day: secure site, fencing, lighting, no partially demolished unstable elements left.
Final: inspect, remove props safely, clear site, close permits.
ppe: Helmet, boots, gloves, eye protection, hi-vis, P2/P3 dust respirator; harness for edge work; hearing protection
stop: Unexpected movement/cracking
Asbestos found unplanned
Service found live
Dust escaping site / public exposure
records: Structural survey, method statement, hazardous-materials survey, asbestos removal records, C&D waste manifests, demolition permission

t: Electrical Safety – Site Temporary Power, LV/HT Work & Overhead Lines
purpose: Prevent electrocution, arc flash, electrical fires and contact with overhead/underground lines.
scope: Temporary site distribution (DBs, generators, cables), portable tools, lighting, welding sets; maintenance on LV/HT systems; work near live overhead lines; substations.
roles: Competent person for HT (authorised by CEIG/utility)
hazards: Shock/electrocution from damaged cables, improper joints, no RCD, wet conditions
Arc flash during switching/testing on energised boards
Overhead line contact by cranes, concrete pump booms, tipper bodies, scaffold tubes, ladders
Fire from overloaded temporary wiring; DG set hazards (fuel, CO, noise)
pre: Temporary electrical layout approved; all circuits protected by 30 mA RCD (ELCB) at DB; earthing per IS 3043 tested (< 1 Ω typical site target) and re-tested quarterly
Industrial plugs/sockets (IS/IEC 60309), armoured/ double-insulated cables, cables overhead or protected, no joints by taping
DBs lockable, labelled, IP rated, accessible, with fire extinguisher (CO2) nearby; monthly inspection tag
Portable tools 110 V CTE or double-insulated 230 V with RCD; inspection/test (PAT) 3-monthly; register
Overhead lines surveyed; goal posts/barriers at crossings; clearance per CEA regulations; shutdown/shrouding arranged with utility where needed
steps: Energise only through approved DBs by licensed electrician; no direct connection to live terminals.
Daily visual check of cables, plugs, RCD test button weekly (record).
Work on electrical equipment dead: isolate, lock, test dead with proved tester, earth where HT; permit-to-work for HT (utility/CEIG format).
Energised work only where unavoidable, by qualified person under energised-work permit with arc-flash PPE and boundaries (NFPA 70E) – never alone.
Keep plant, scaffold, ladders and materials outside line-clearance zones; crane operators briefed; spotter assigned; use insulated link stick where authorised.
Wet weather: suspend outdoor electrical work; protect DBs; raise cables.

DG sets: earthed (2 earth pits), acoustic enclosure (75 dB(A) @ 1 m), exhaust away from work areas, fuel in bunded tank (PESO licence if > 2,500 L Class B), no refuelling while running, fire extinguishers.
Lighting: 24 V in confined/wet areas; task lighting ≥ 100 lux general, 200 lux work areas (IS 3646).
Report every shock/arc-flash as incident; notify Electrical Inspector within 48 h for reportable electrical accidents (fatal immediately).
Lightning: suspend WAH/crane work; LPS on tall structures (IS/IEC 62305).
ppe: Insulated gloves (class per voltage) with leather over-gloves, arc-rated FR clothing, face shield/hood, insulated tools, safety boots (electrical hazard rated), helmet (non-metallic)
stop: Missing/failed RCD
Damaged cable or exposed conductors
Plant within line-clearance zone
Rain on exposed temporary installation
records: Temporary electrical layout, earth-test records, RCD test log, PAT register, HT permits, electrician licences, DG set consent

t: Hazardous Chemical Handling, Storage & SDS Management
purpose: Prevent exposure, fire/explosion, spills and environmental release from hazardous chemicals (solvents, acids/alkalis, gases, fuels, admixtures, epoxies, pesticides, cement).
scope: Receipt, storage, transfer, use, waste and emergency handling of all hazardous chemicals; threshold-quantity screening against MSIHC Schedules; dangerous-goods transport.
hazards: Inhalation/skin/eye exposure; chronic effects (CMR, sensitisers – isocyanates, chromates)
Fire/explosion of flammables; incompatibles (oxidisers + flammables, acids + cyanides/hypochlorite)
Spills to drains/soil; toxic gas release (chlorine, ammonia, H2S)
Pressure/temperature runaway; static ignition during transfer
pre: Chemical inventory with GHS classification, quantities, locations; screened against MSIHC Sch. 1/2/3 thresholds (MAH status → site notification, safety report, on-site plan)
16-section SDS (ISO 11014/UN GHS) for every chemical, available at point of use in local language (Kannada/Tamil summaries); MSDS per MSIHC Rule 17 format

Storage design: segregation matrix, bunding (110% of largest container), ventilation, flameproof electricals in Zone 1/2 (IEC 60079), earthing/bonding for Class A/B liquids, eyewash/shower within 10 s / 15 m
PESO licence for petroleum Class A/B above thresholds; gas cylinders store; SPCB consent/HW authorisation
Spill kits, PPE matrix, exposure monitoring plan (PELs per Factories Act Sch. II / OSH rules; TLVs)
steps: Receipt: verify label, SDS, container integrity; reject damaged; TREM card for transport; unloading with bonding and bunded area.

Store by compatibility class, not alphabetically; flammables in cabinets (NFPA 30/IS) ≤ 250 L per cabinet (verify) or dedicated store; cylinders upright, chained, caps on, oxidisers 6 m from fuel gases.
Label all secondary containers (name, hazard, date); never use food/water containers.
Transfer: closed systems/pumps where possible; grounding clips; drum pump; no siphoning by mouth; LEV for solvents; work-area monitoring (PID/detector tubes) for high-risk tasks.
Use: follow SDS Sec. 7/8; PPE per matrix (chemical-resistant gloves with breakthrough time, goggles/face shield, apron, respirator cartridge type); hygiene – no eating/smoking, wash before breaks.
Health surveillance: pre-employment & periodic medicals for dangerous operations (lead, chrome, solvents, isocyanates, asbestos, silica) by certifying surgeon; records.
Waste: segregate hazardous waste (used oil, solvent, contaminated PPE, empty drums) → labelled, ≤ 90 days storage, manifest to authorised recycler/TSDF; Form 4 annual return.
Spill: evacuate, isolate ignition, PPE, contain (booms/absorbent), collect, report to SPCB if beyond site/ significant (HOWM Rule 23 Form 11); EPA s.9 duty to report forthwith.

MAH units: on-site emergency plan rehearsed every 6 months; off-site plan with District Collector; mock drill with District Crisis Group yearly; safety audit annually; safety report update every 3 years.
Management of change for any new chemical/process (see MoC procedure).
ppe: Per SDS Sec. 8: chemical goggles, face shield, nitrile/butyl/viton gloves, chemical apron/suit, respirator (OV/AG cartridges or SCBA), safety boots
stop: Unlabelled container
Incompatible storage found
Leak/odour beyond control
Missing SDS for new chemical
records: Chemical inventory, SDS register, MSIHC site notification/safety report, exposure-monitoring results, medical records (retained ≥ 30–40 yrs for carcinogens – verify), HW manifests & returns, spill reports, drill records

t: Fire Prevention, Protection & Evacuation
purpose: Prevent fires, limit spread, and ensure everyone can evacuate safely; meet Fire NOC conditions.
scope: Factories, warehouses, construction sites (incl. labour colonies), site offices, fuel stores, hot-work areas, electrical rooms.
roles: Fire safety officer / fire warden per floor/zone
hazards: Electrical faults, hot work, smoking, cooking in labour camps, LPG, flammable storage, combustible waste accumulation, arson
Blocked exits, locked doors, storage in staircases
Construction sites: formwork timber, shuttering oil, bitumen, cylinders, temporary wiring
High-rise under construction without fire-fighting infrastructure
pre: Fire risk assessment; fire plan with zoning, exits, assembly points; Fire NOC (KSFES/TNFRS) where applicable
Extinguishers selected and placed per IS 2190 (travel ≤ 15 m Class A / ≤ 10–15 m Class B; 1 per 100–200 m²), inspected monthly, serviced annually, hydrostatic test per schedule
Hydrant/sprinkler/alarm systems maintained (NFPA 25 / IS 13039, IS 15105, IS 2189); fire pump weekly test
Emergency lighting, exit signs, clear escape routes ≥ 1 m, doors opening outward; no locks during occupancy
Trained fire wardens; evacuation drill every 6 months (every 3 months for hazardous units); mutual-aid agreements
steps: Housekeeping daily: combustible waste removed, no accumulation under stairs/near exits; oily rags in metal bins with lids.
Control ignition: smoking only in designated areas; hot-work permit; electrical inspections; no open fires in labour camps – provide LPG cooking areas with extinguishers.
Flammables: minimum quantities at point of use, in approved cabinets; cylinders stored outdoors in cages, segregated; fuel in bunded tanks away from buildings (≥ 6 m).

Construction: progressive installation of fire standpipe/risers as floors rise (NBC/NFPA 241 – wet riser charged within 2 floors of top), temporary extinguishers each floor, access for fire tender maintained, no storage blocking stairs.
Detection/alarm tested weekly; manual call points; PA system; alarm sound known to all.

On alarm: raise alarm (shout/manual call point), call 101/112, attempt first-aid firefighting only if trained and safe (PASS), evacuate via nearest exit, never use lifts, close doors, go to assembly point, head count by wardens, report missing persons to incident controller, nobody re-enters until all-clear.
Incident controller liaises with fire brigade; provide site plan, chemical inventory, isolation points.
After fire: preserve scene for investigation; report per OSH Code s.11 (dangerous occurrence) within 12 h; MSIHC major accident 48 h; insurance.
Review drill performance (evacuation time, head-count accuracy) and update plan.
Labour colonies: fire-resistant materials for huts, spacing, extinguishers, water drums, no electrical hazards, exits.
ppe: ERT: fire-retardant suit, helmet, gloves, boots, SCBA for interior attack
stop: Exits blocked
Hydrant system out of service without compensatory measures
Fire detected – evacuate
records: Fire NOC, extinguisher register, hydrant/pump tests, alarm tests, drill records, warden training, fire incident reports

t: Emergency Response & On-Site Emergency Plan
purpose: Ensure a prepared, rehearsed response to fire, explosion, toxic release, structural collapse, medical emergency, flood/cyclone, earthquake, bomb threat, and civil disturbance; integrate with district off-site plans.
scope: All sites; mandatory written on-site emergency plan for MAH units (MSIHC Rule 13) and hazardous-process factories; construction sites per BOCW rules (emergency action plan).
roles: Emergency Response Team leader; fire team; rescue team; first-aid team
Communications officer; security; liaison with police/fire/district authority
hazards: Delayed alarm; unclear command; unprepared responders become casualties
Loss of utilities; inaccessible roads; monsoon flooding/cyclone (TN coast); Karnataka/TN heat waves
Media/public panic; secondary incidents
pre: Written plan: hazard inventory, scenarios (worst credible), roles, alarm codes, assembly points (upwind alternatives), emergency control centre with phones/radios/drawings/SDS/wind sock, shelter-in-place rooms for toxic release

Emergency contacts board at gate and ECC: 112, 101, 108/102, nearest hospital(s) with burn/trauma capability, police, District Collector/ DEOC 1077, SPCB, Factory Inspector/ICF, utility helplines, poison centre
Equipment: fire systems, breathing apparatus, spill kits, gas detectors, stretchers, ambulance (own or tie-up within 15 min), first-aid room (≥ 500 workers), AEDs
Training: ERT quarterly; all staff induction; drills: fire 6-monthly, toxic release/chemical mock drill annual with District Crisis Group (MAH), evening/night-shift drill
Business continuity & crisis communication plan
steps: Detection & alarm: anyone can raise alarm; codes for fire/gas/evacuation/shelter-in-place; siren patterns displayed.
Activation: SMC declares level (1 = local, 2 = site, 3 = off-site); ECC activated; head counts at assembly points.
Response: ERT tackles incident within competence; isolate utilities (power, gas) as directed; account for contractors/visitors via gate register.
Medical: first-aiders stabilise; ambulance dispatch; hospital notified (nature – chemical burn, crush); casualty log.
Communication: single spokesperson; inform family of injured; notify authorities per statutory timelines (see Reporting view).
External: receive fire brigade/police at gate with site plan and chemical inventory; District Collector for off-site; inform neighbours if release.
Shelter-in-place for toxic gas: close doors/windows, stop AC, move to upper floors/designated rooms, monitor.
Natural hazard: cyclone/flood warning (IMD) – secure cranes (free slew), lower loads, stop WAH, move workers to safe shelters; heat wave – stop outdoor work at peak hours.
Stand-down only by SMC; scene preserved for investigation; debrief within 24 h.
Review plan annually and after every drill/incident; update contacts quarterly.
ppe: ERT kit as per scenario (SCBA, chemical suits, fire kit)
stop: Responder without correct PPE
Unknown chemical involved
Structural instability
records: On-site emergency plan (approved by Chief Inspector for MAH), drill reports, ERT training, casualty logs, notification records, off-site plan correspondence

t: Incident Reporting, Investigation & Statutory Notification
purpose: Capture every injury, illness, dangerous occurrence, near miss and environmental release; meet statutory notification deadlines; find root causes and prevent recurrence.
scope: All work-related incidents involving employees, contractors, visitors and the public; property damage; environmental releases; security events.
roles: Investigation team (lead trained in RCA; worker rep; engineer)
hazards: Late or missed statutory notice (penalties, loss of insurance)
Scene disturbed; evidence lost
Blame culture suppressing near-miss reporting
pre: Incident classification matrix (fatal, lost-time, restricted, medical treatment, first aid, near miss, dangerous occurrence, occupational disease, environmental, property)

Notification flowchart with deadlines by jurisdiction (see Reporting view); pre-filled Form XI / state accident forms; contacts of ICF, police, DM/SDO, Electrical Inspector, Boiler Inspector, SPCB, PESO, ESIC
RCA methodology (5-Why, fishbone, TapRooT, ICAM); investigation kit (camera, tape, cones, witness forms)
KPI definitions: LTIFR, TRIR, severity rate (IS 3786 / OSHA 1904 method)
steps: Make area safe; rescue and first aid; call 108/112; isolate hazard; prevent secondary incidents.
Report immediately to supervisor and safety officer (within 1 h internal); log in incident register with unique number.
Preserve scene (do not disturb until inspector permits for fatal/serious – legal requirement); photographs, measurements, witness names.

Statutory notification: death – forthwith to ICF (electronically + written), police and family (OSH Central Rules Rule 7; state rules); injury ≥ 48 h absence / dangerous occurrence – within 12 h in Form XI (central sphere) or per state rule (often 4–24 h); MSIHC major accident – 48 h (Schedule 6); electrical accident – 48 h to Electrical Inspector; boiler – 24 h; ESIC accident report – 24 h; Employee's Compensation Commissioner – fatal within 7 days; SPCB – environmental release forthwith/Form 11; PESO – forthwith; OSHA (US sites) – fatality 8 h, hospitalisation/amputation/eye loss 24 h.
Investigation within 24–72 h: sequence of events, immediate causes (unsafe acts/conditions), underlying causes (management system), root causes; use hierarchy of controls for actions.
Corrective & preventive actions with owner and due date; tracked to closure; verify effectiveness.
Communicate lessons (safety alert, toolbox talk); share with corporate/client.
Occupational disease: medical practitioner reports (OSH Code s.12 / Factories Act s.89 Third Schedule) to ICF; employer notice.
Maintain registers: accident register, dangerous-occurrence log, first-aid register, near-miss log; annual return.
Monthly KPI review at safety committee; trend analysis.
ppe: As required for scene access
stop: Scene unsafe
Attempting to move fatal/serious casualty before medical advice (unless further danger)
records: Incident register, statutory notices with acknowledgements, investigation reports, CAPA tracker, medical records, annual return

t: Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA) / Job Safety Analysis (JSA)
purpose: Systematically identify hazards, evaluate risk and define controls before work, and keep assessments live as conditions change.
scope: Baseline site/plant HIRA; activity-based JSA/method statements; task-specific dynamic risk assessment; process hazard analysis (HAZOP/What-if/LOPA) for process plants; environmental aspect-impact register.
hazards: Generic copy-paste assessments; controls not implemented; no review after change
pre: Risk matrix (likelihood × severity, e.g. 5×5) with acceptance criteria; legal register linked
Templates: HIRA register, JSA (steps-hazards-controls), method statement, PHA worksheets
Legal and standard requirements identified (OSH Code s.6; ISO 45001 cl. 6.1.2)
steps: Break the job into steps (observe or walk-through with the crew).
For each step list hazards: physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic, psychosocial, environmental, and energy sources (gravity, electricity, pressure, motion, chemical, thermal, radiation).
Rate risk (unmitigated) with matrix; identify who is harmed (workers, contractors, public).
Apply hierarchy of controls: eliminate → substitute → engineering → administrative (procedures, permits, training) → PPE.
Rate residual risk; if above acceptance, add controls or escalate; obtain approvals (high-risk = site head).
Convert into method statement/toolbox-talk content; communicate to crew in local language; crew signs.
Implement; supervisor verifies controls in place before start (pre-task briefing).
Review: on change of scope/equipment/people, after incident/near miss, at fixed interval (annually; monthly for high-risk sites), at monsoon start.
Process plants: HAZOP at design and every 5 years / on MoC; LOPA/SIL for safeguards; bow-tie for MAH scenarios.
Maintain risk register; feed into safety committee, objectives and training plan.
ppe: Determined by assessment
stop: No assessment for new/high-risk task
Controls not available at site
records: HIRA register, JSAs/method statements, PHA reports & action close-out, legal register, review log

t: Personal Protective Equipment Programme
purpose: Select, issue, use, maintain and replace PPE correctly as the last line of defence after higher-order controls.
scope: Head, eye/face, hearing, respiratory, hand, foot, body, fall protection and hi-vis PPE for employees, contractors and visitors.
hazards: Wrong PPE for hazard (e.g. dust mask for solvent vapour), counterfeit/uncertified PPE, poor fit, non-use due to heat/discomfort
pre: Written PPE hazard assessment per area/task (OSHA 1910.132(d); OSH Code s.6)

Free issue to workers (employer cost – statutory), replacement schedule, sizes stocked
Fit testing for tight-fitting respirators; medical evaluation
Training on donning/doffing, limitations, inspection, storage
steps: Issue PPE on induction against signed register; record sizes and dates.
Mandatory minimum on site: helmet, safety boots, hi-vis; task PPE per matrix and permit.
Daily pre-use inspection by wearer; damaged PPE replaced immediately (no cost to worker).
Respirators: clean-shaven for tight-fit; cartridge change schedule; store sealed; disposable FFP replaced each shift.
Hearing: ear plugs/muffs where ≥ 85 dB(A); signage; audiometry for exposed workers annually.
Fall protection: 6-monthly competent inspection; retire after fall or per manufacturer life (typically 5 years from first use).
Heat: breathable FR/cotton, cooling vests, shaded rest; schedule heavy work out of peak heat.
Visitors: PPE at gate with escort.
Enforcement: supervisors stop non-compliant work; progressive discipline; recognise good practice.
Review matrix on new hazards, incidents, and PPE standard changes (e.g. new QCOs).
ppe: Programme defines all

Uncertified/counterfeit PPE in use

t: Contractor & Subcontractor Safety Management
purpose: Ensure contractors work to the same standard as the principal employer; discharge principal-employer liability under OSH Code Ch. XI.
scope: Pre-qualification, contract clauses, mobilisation, supervision, performance monitoring and close-out for all contractors (civil, mechanical, electrical, scaffolding, crane hire, labour supply, cleaning, security).
hazards: Unlicensed contractors; untrained migrant workers; wage/welfare defaults attributed to principal employer
Interface hazards between contractors (SIMOPS)
pre: Pre-qualification: OSH Code contractor licence (50+ workers), safety statistics (LTIFR), ISO 45001/competence, insurance (EC/WC policy, PLI), past prosecutions

Contract HSE clauses: site rules, PTW, PPE, penalties/incentives, reporting, right to stop work, safety officer requirement by headcount, medical fitness, age proof (no child/adolescent in hazardous work)
Mobilisation checklist: worker registration (BOCW board, ESI/EPF), induction, medical, tool/equipment inspection, lifting gear certificates, electrician licences
Interface/SIMOPS matrix and coordination meetings
steps: Issue site HSE plan and rules with contract; kick-off HSE meeting before mobilisation.
Verify licences, registrations (contract labour licence, BOCW), insurance, competence certificates; approve contractor's method statements and HIRA.
Induct every worker (ID card with photo, blood group, emergency contact, induction date); maintain gate register; daily toolbox talks by contractor supervisors.
Joint weekly inspections; score cards (leading indicators: toolbox talks, inspections, near-miss reports; lagging: injuries).
Enforce PTW and stop-work authority; non-conformance notices; escalating sanctions.
Welfare: verify wages paid, PF/ESI, drinking water, latrines, rest sheds, crèche, canteen, accommodation standards (labour camps) — principal employer liable on default.
Inter-state migrant workers: journey allowance, helpline, portability; language-appropriate training.
Incident reporting by contractor within 1 h; principal employer files statutory notices where it is the 'employer' under the Code.
Monthly HSE performance review; quarterly audit; demobilisation close-out (clearance only after safe removal of equipment, waste, scaffolds).
Keep records for statutory period.
ppe: Per site matrix
stop: Contractor without valid licence/insurance
Unregistered/under-age worker
Repeated serious non-conformance
records: Pre-qualification files, licences, contractor HSE plans, induction registers, inspection scorecards, NCRs, performance reviews

t: Safety Induction, Training, Competence & Toolbox Talks
purpose: Ensure every person has the knowledge and competence for their task and hazards, in a language they understand.
scope: Site induction (all persons), job-specific training, statutory certifications (competent persons, operators, electricians, first-aiders, fire wardens, scaffolders, riggers), refresher, toolbox talks, visitor briefings.
hazards: New workers (first 30 days) have highest injury rates; language barriers (Kannada/Tamil/Hindi/Odia/Bengali migrant mix)
pre: Training needs matrix by role; statutory list (e.g. crane operator licence, scaffold inspector, electrical supervisor licence, first-aid certificate from St John/approved centre, fire warden, confined-space, radiography RSO)
Induction content: site hazards, rules, PTW, PPE, emergency, reporting, welfare, rights (no retaliation), POSH; audio-visual in local languages; test
Training records with validity; ID card colour/sticker shows induction & skills
steps: Induct before first entry (2–4 h); issue ID; buddy for first week; mark 'new worker' helmet sticker for 30 days.
Job-specific training with practical assessment (e.g. harness donning, extinguisher use, gas detector).
Statutory refreshers: induction annually; WAH/confined/LOTO every 2 years or on change; first aid 3-yearly; operators per licence.
Daily toolbox talk (10–15 min) by supervisor on the day's tasks and permit conditions; attendance signed; topic library (see Toolbox Talks view).
Mock drills count as training; record participation.
Supervisor/line-manager training: legal duties, incident investigation, behaviour-based safety.
Evaluate effectiveness: observations, audit findings, quiz scores; retrain where gaps.
Keep training records ≥ 3 years (longer for statutory certificates).
ppe: N/A
stop: Untrained person on high-risk task
No induction
records: Training matrix, attendance, certificates, toolbox talk sheets, competence assessments

t: Manual Handling & Ergonomics
purpose: Prevent musculoskeletal injuries from lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling and repetitive or awkward work.
scope: Cement bags (50 kg), rebar, blocks, pipes, drums, formwork panels, equipment; repetitive bar bending, tiling, plastering, overhead work; workstation ergonomics.
hazards: Loads > guideline weights; twisting; above-shoulder/below-knee lifts; long carries; team lifts uncoordinated; heat compounding fatigue
pre: Mechanical aids: trolleys, pallet trucks, hoists, vacuum lifters, conveyors; design-out (25 kg cement bags, pre-cut rebar)

Statutory maximum weights (state Factories Rules, Rule on 'maximum permissible loads' — commonly adult male 50 kg, adult female 30 kg, adolescent 30/20, child not permitted — verify; good practice ≤ 25 kg single-person lift, NIOSH 23 kg)
TILE assessment (Task, Individual, Load, Environment); ISO 11228
steps: Avoid: deliver materials close to point of use; use plant; reduce load size.
Assess remaining manual tasks (TILE/NIOSH equation); set team-lift rules (2 persons for 25–50 kg).
Train lifting technique: plan route, stable base, bend knees, keep load close, no twisting, smooth movement; team lifts with one leader.
Rotate repetitive tasks; micro-breaks; adjustable workstations for bar bending/pipe fitting.
Provide gloves with grip, shoulder pads, and handles/hooks for blocks and rebar.
Heat: more rest in hot hours; hydration (see heat stress).
Early reporting of pain; medical review; modified duties.
Review incidents and MSD symptoms at safety committee.
ppe: Gloves, safety boots, shoulder pads, back support only where prescribed
stop: Single-person lift beyond limit
Unsafe route/footing
records: Manual handling assessments, training, MSD reports

t: Heat Stress Management (Outdoor & Hot-Process Work)
purpose: Prevent heat exhaustion, heat stroke and heat-related accidents in Karnataka/Tamil Nadu summers (Mar–Jun; Chennai humid heat) and hot processes (foundries, boilers, kilns, bitumen).
scope: All outdoor work, roof/ height work, confined spaces, hot plants; new and returning workers; PPE-heavy tasks (FR suits, respirators).
hazards: Heat stroke (core > 40 °C; confusion; can be fatal), heat exhaustion, cramps, syncope, dehydration-related falls and errors
Risk amplified by humidity, no acclimatisation, illness, medication, impermeable PPE
pre: Heat illness prevention plan triggered by IMD heat-wave alerts / State Heat Action Plan; WBGT monitor or heat-index chart; ACGIH TLV WBGT action limits by workload
Water: ≥ 1 cup (250 ml) every 15–20 min; cool potable water within 100 m; ORS available; shaded rest areas with fans/misting; cooling vests for FR work
Acclimatisation: new/returning workers 20% workload day 1, +20%/day over 5–7 days (OSHA NEP focus)
Buddy system; emergency plan for heat stroke (cool first – ice water immersion/cold wet sheets – then transport)
steps: Check forecast daily; post heat level (green/amber/red) at gate.
Schedule heavy work early morning/evening; red level: no heavy outdoor work 12–3 pm (or per state advisory); shift adjustments.
Work/rest cycles per WBGT and workload (e.g. heavy work at WBGT 30 °C: 25% work/75% rest for unacclimatised).
Supervisors observe for symptoms (headache, dizziness, cramps, confusion, cessation of sweating); never leave symptomatic worker alone.
Encourage drinking before thirst; avoid caffeinated/sugary drinks; monitor urine colour chart in toilets.
Clothing: light, loose, cotton; helmet with brim/neck flap; sunscreen.
Confined/hot spaces: ventilation, shorter rotations, physiological monitoring where WBGT > TLV.
Heat stroke response: call 108, move to shade, remove excess clothing, aggressive cooling (immerse/douse with cold water, fan), do not give fluids if unconscious.
Record heat illness as incident; review schedule.
Training in local language before summer each year.
ppe: Light cotton clothing, helmet neck flap, cooling vest, sunglasses (where no eye hazard conflict)
stop: Worker shows confusion/collapse
WBGT above ceiling for workload with no engineering control
No water/shade available
records: WBGT/heat-index log, acclimatisation schedules, heat illness incidents, training

t: Noise & Vibration Control
purpose: Prevent noise-induced hearing loss and hand-arm/whole-body vibration syndrome; comply with ambient noise limits for neighbours.
scope: Breakers, compressors, DG sets, piling, grinders, cutting, concrete pumps, compaction plant, process plant (compressors, mills), vehicles.
hazards: Occupational exposure ≥ 85 dB(A) 8-h TWA; impulse noise; HAV from breakers/grinders; WBV from plant seats
Community complaints; night-work restrictions
pre: Noise survey (sound level meter, dosimetry) and HAV exposure estimates (manufacturer vibration data, trigger times)
Hearing conservation programme where ≥ 85 dB(A): audiometry baseline & annual, hearing protection, training
Ambient limits: industrial area 75/70 dB(A) day/night at boundary; no night construction noise without permission (Noise Rules 2000); DG sets with acoustic enclosures
steps: Eliminate/substitute: hydraulic breakers with silenced tips, electric over diesel, rubber lining chutes.
Engineering: enclosures, screens, silencers, anti-vibration mounts; maintain equipment (worn bearings raise noise).
Zoning: mark hearing-protection zones ≥ 85 dB(A) with signs.
Admin: rotate workers; limit HAV trigger time (EAV 2.5 m/s² A(8), ELV 5 m/s²); job rotation; warm hands/gloves.
PPE: plugs/muffs rated for level (SNR), fit-trained; double protection > 105 dB(A).
Monitor boundary noise near residences/schools/hospitals; adjust timing (no piling at night).
Audiometry annually for exposed workers; refer standard threshold shifts.
Record exposures; review when plant changes.
ppe: Ear plugs/muffs (IS 9167/EN 352), anti-vibration gloves (limited benefit)
stop: Exposure > 90 dB(A) without protection
Complaint of tingling/numbness from vibrating tools
records: Noise survey, dosimetry, audiometry, HAV exposure log, community monitoring

t: Respiratory Protection, Dust, Silica & Asbestos
purpose: Prevent silicosis, asbestosis, COPD, lung cancer and acute poisoning from airborne contaminants.
scope: Concrete/stone cutting and grinding, drilling, sandblasting (prohibited in many rules – use wet/grit alternatives), demolition, cement handling, welding fumes, paint spraying, insulation, asbestos-cement work, solvents, confined spaces.
hazards: Respirable crystalline silica (RCS) – PEL 0.05 mg/m³ (OSHA; India Sch. II lower?), asbestos (0.1 f/cc OSHA), cement dust, wood dust, welding fumes (Mn, Cr VI), isocyanates, solvents; O2 deficiency; CO from engines
pre: Exposure assessment; control plan per task (OSHA Table 1 style: wet cutting, LEV with HEPA, enclosed cabs)
Respiratory protection programme: selection by assigned protection factor, fit test (qualitative/quantitative) annually, medical evaluation, cleaning, cartridge change-out, training
Medical surveillance: chest X-ray (ILO classification), spirometry for silica/asbestos-exposed (state rules dangerous-operations schedules); records retained long-term
steps: Eliminate: pre-cast, prefabricated, non-silica abrasives; prohibit dry sweeping — use vacuum/wet.
Engineering: water suppression on saws/drills, LEV with HEPA on grinders, enclosed cabs with filtered air, downdraft tables, ventilation.
Admin: restricted zones, rotation, signage, hygiene (no eating in dusty areas, laundering of contaminated clothing on site — not taken home).
PPE: FFP2 (N95) minimum for nuisance/cement dust; FFP3/P100 or half-mask P3 for silica/asbestos; PAPR/airline for high exposures; organic-vapour cartridges for solvents; SCBA for IDLH/unknown.

Asbestos: survey before work; only licensed agency for friable; AC sheets removed whole, wetted, no power tools; waste double-bagged to TSDF; air monitoring; medical surveillance per TN Factories Rules Sch. XX / KA rules.
Welding: LEV at arc; low-fume consumables; respirator for stainless/galvanised.
Monitor: personal sampling for silica/asbestos per plan; compare with PEL/TLV.
Medical: baseline and periodic; refer abnormal findings; report notifiable diseases (silicosis, asbestosis, byssinosis) under OSH Code s.12.
Record keeping for exposure and medical (≥ 30–40 years for carcinogens – verify).
ppe: Respirators per programme; eye protection; coveralls (disposable for asbestos)
stop: Dry cutting of concrete/stone without control
Suspected asbestos disturbed
Respirator not fit-tested for silica/asbestos work
records: Exposure assessments, sampling, fit tests, medical surveillance, asbestos survey/removal, training

t: Machine Guarding & Safe Use of Plant/Power Tools
purpose: Prevent entanglement, crushing, shearing, cutting and ejection injuries from machinery and tools.
scope: Bar-bending/cutting machines, concrete mixers, batching plants, compressors, conveyors, presses, lathes, grinders, saws, woodworking, pumps, drive belts; portable tools (angle grinders, drills, nail guns).
hazards: Unguarded nip points/belts; missing emergency stops; bypassed interlocks; grinder disc burst (wrong RPM/size), kickback; loose clothing
pre: Machinery risk assessment (ISO 12100); guards (fixed, interlocked, adjustable), light curtains, two-hand controls per IS 9474/ISO 14120
Emergency stops accessible; isolation switches; pre-start alarm for conveyors
Operator authorisation; young persons (< 18) barred from dangerous machines (Factories Act s.23 / OSH Code)
Tool register with inspection colour-code (quarterly)
steps: Inspect guards daily; never operate with guards removed; report defects; tag out defective machines.
Grinders: disc RPM ≥ tool RPM, correct size, guard fitted, side handle, face shield + goggles, no cutting with grinding disc; 9-inch grinders restricted to trained users.
Mixers/batching plants: isolate before cleaning drum; interlocked hopper; no entry under raised skip.
Bar bending/cutting: foot pedal guard, no loose rebar ends, keep hands clear, ear/eye protection.
Conveyors: pull-cord stops, guards at nip points, no crossing except bridges, lockout for un-jamming.
Compressed air: never for cleaning clothing; whip checks on hose couplings; pressure relief.
Nail guns/powder-actuated tools: licensed operators, sequential trigger, exclusion zone, PPE.
Maintenance under LOTO; test guards after maintenance before release.
Keep machines in register with inspection dates; competent-person examinations per rules (e.g. pressure vessels, lifting).
ppe: Eye/face protection, gloves (not near rotating parts), hearing protection, no loose clothing/jewellery, hair tied
stop: Guard missing/bypassed
E-stop not working
Wrong abrasive disc
records: Machine register, guard inspection, tool inspection colour-code log, operator authorisation

t: Compressed Gas Cylinders – Storage, Handling & Use
purpose: Prevent cylinder explosions, fires, oxygen enrichment, asphyxiation and crushing injuries.
scope: Oxygen, acetylene, LPG, argon, CO2, nitrogen, hydrogen, chlorine cylinders at sites and plants; manifolds; cryogenic dewars.
hazards: Acetylene decomposition/flashback; oxygen with oil/grease; LPG leaks (heavier than air); valve shear on falling cylinder (projectile); inert gas asphyxiation in enclosed spaces
pre: Store outdoors/ventilated cage, shaded, on level ground, upright, chained, caps on; full/empty segregated; oxidisers ≥ 6 m or 1.5 m fire wall (30 min) from fuel gases; no sources of ignition within 3 m
PESO licence if quantities exceed thresholds; supplier test dates (hydro test within validity — 5/10 yrs by gas)
Colour coding per IS 4379; leak detection (soap solution); flashback arrestors; regulators matched to gas
steps: Receive: check test date, valve, cap, leaks; reject damaged; record.
Transport on cylinder trolley, secured upright; never roll on side, drag, lift by cap/valve, or use crane slings (use cage).

Use: open valve slowly standing to side; acetylene valve ≤ 1.5 turns, key left in place; regulator pressures (acetylene ≤ 1 bar); flashback arrestors both ends; hoses colour-coded, clamped, free of oil.
LPG: never in basements/pits/confined spaces; detect leaks with soap; hoses BIS-marked, replaced 2-yearly; regulators with pressure relief.
Inert gases: ventilation/oxygen monitoring in enclosed areas (purging, argon welding in tanks).
Close valves when not in use and at end of shift; remove regulators for transport; return empties marked 'MT'.
Fire involving cylinder: evacuate 100+ m, cool with water from behind cover, call fire service; acetylene cylinder that has been heated must be cooled 24 h (fire service).
Monthly storage inspection; quarterly hose/regulator inspection.
ppe: Gloves, eye protection, safety boots; face shield for connecting
stop: Cylinder without cap/chain
Leak detected
Oil/grease on oxygen fittings
Past test date
records: Cylinder register, PESO licence, inspection logs

t: Site Traffic, Mobile Plant & Pedestrian Segregation
purpose: Prevent persons being struck or run over by vehicles and plant (leading cause of construction fatalities with falls and electrocution).
scope: Tippers, transit mixers, excavators, loaders, forklifts, cranes, hydras, rollers, dumpers, site cars; public road interface; loading/unloading; reversing.
hazards: Reversing without banksman/alarm; blind spots; speeding; pedestrians in haul routes; unsecured loads; overturn on slopes/edges; refuelling fires
pre: Traffic management plan: one-way routes, speed limits (10–20 km/h), segregated pedestrian walkways with barriers, crossing points, parking, turning areas, lighting
Vehicle/plant: registration, fitness, insurance, reversing alarm/camera, beacon, seatbelt, ROPS/FOPS, mirrors; daily pre-start check; defect register
Operators: valid licence (HMV/CEV), site authorisation, medical fitness, no phone use; banksman trained
Public road: IRC:SP:55 signage, flagmen, wheel wash, no mud on road, covered loads
steps: Induct drivers/operators to the traffic plan; display plan at gate.
Keep pedestrians out of plant zones; where interaction unavoidable, banksman controls with radio; stop plant when pedestrian within swing/travel zone.
Reversing minimised (drive-through, turning circles); banksman always for reversing in congested areas; stand clear of path.
Loads secured/covered; height limits at overhead lines (goal posts); tippers: never travel with body raised; check overhead before tipping; stable level ground for tipping; stop blocks at edges.
Slopes/edges: plant kept away ≥ 1 m per 1 m depth from excavation edges; no operation across steep slopes.
Refuelling: engine off, no smoking, spill kit, bunded area; fuel bowser licensed.
Night: lighting, hi-vis class 3, reflective barriers.
Vehicle/plant inspection daily; maintenance records; tyre/brake checks.
Report near misses; review plan on layout change.
ppe: Hi-vis (class 2/3), helmet, boots; seatbelt in plant
stop: No banksman for reversing in congested area
Pedestrian in exclusion zone
Alarm/camera not working
Tipping near edge without stop block
records: Traffic management plan, operator licences/authorisations, vehicle inspection logs, incident reports

t: Concrete, Formwork & Falsework (Temporary Works)
purpose: Prevent formwork/falsework collapse, falls, concrete burns and pump/boom incidents.
scope: Slab/column/wall formwork, shoring towers, props, scaffold-based falsework, slipform, precast erection, concrete pumping, rebar work.
hazards: Collapse during pouring (overload, premature striking, inadequate bracing/foundation); boom contact with lines; hose whip; impalement on rebar; cement dermatitis/burns; falls from deck edges
pre: Temporary works design (loads, bracing, foundations) and checked drawings (BS 5975 TWC model); shoring tower load tables; props at correct extension
Formwork inspection and sign-off before pour (permit to pour); striking times per IS 456 (e.g. vertical forms 16–24 h; slab props 7–14 days depending on span) or cube results
Rebar caps/covers on protruding bars; edge protection on decks; access stairs/ladders
Pump: inspection certificate, outriggers, line clearance, hose restraints; washout area
steps: Install falsework per drawing on firm bearing (sole plates); plumb and brace; check prop pins/extensions.
Pre-pour inspection by engineer: supports, ties, bracing, cleanliness; issue pour permit.
Pour sequence controlled to avoid overloading; monitor for movement; stop pour if deflection/sound of distress.
Concrete pump: operator competent; boom clear of lines; nobody under boom; hose end held by two with restraint; pressure release before uncoupling; no hands near hopper agitator (interlock).
Skin protection: cement is alkaline — gloves, long sleeves, boots; wash splashes immediately; eye wash available.
Strike only on engineer's approval after required strength; re-prop as designed; never remove props prematurely for reuse.
Precast: lifting points designed; temporary propping until connections complete; exclusion zone.
Deck edges: guardrails before rebar fixing; openings covered; rebar caps.
Housekeeping: tie wire offcuts, nails in timber removed; slip/trip prevention; night lighting for pours.
Monsoon: drainage of formwork, ground softening checks for falsework foundations.

t: Structural Steel Erection & Pre-Engineered Buildings
purpose: Prevent falls, structural collapse during erection, dropped members and crane incidents.
scope: Columns, beams, trusses, purlins, roof sheeting, PEB panels, bolting/welding at height, decking.
hazards: Member falling before bolted (minimum 2 bolts rule); collapse without temporary bracing; walking on unsecured purlins/sheeting; fragile roof lights; wind
pre: Erection method statement with stability sequence and temporary bracing/guying; anchor bolts verified before column erection
Fall protection: lifelines/beam anchors designed; safety nets below steel; MEWPs for connections
Lifting plan; tag lines; pre-slung bundles (no loose purlins); weather limits
steps: Install anchor bolts and verify grout/levelling; columns erected with minimum 4 anchor bolts (OSHA) and temporary guys.
Beams landed and secured with at least two bolts wrench-tight at each connection before release from crane.
Connectors tie off 100% (SRL to beam anchor); use MEWP/scaffold where feasible; no 'beam walking' without lifeline.
Temporary bracing installed progressively; no bay left unbraced at end of day; check stability for wind.
Purlins/sheeting: install from secure platform/netting; crawl boards; roof-edge protection; no stepping on sheeting between purlins or on roof lights.
Dropped-object control: tool lanyards, exclusion zone below, no stacking loose bolts on beams.
Bolting: torque per design; welding at height with fire blankets below.
Decking: perimeter protection, controlled decking zone, cover openings immediately.
Stop at wind > 40 km/h (sheeting), lightning, poor visibility.
ppe: Harness + SRL, helmet with chin strap, gloves, boots, eye protection
stop: Member not bolted before release
Missing bracing
High wind
records: Erection method statement, bracing sign-offs, lifting plans, net inspection

t: Housekeeping, Waste Management & Environmental Controls
purpose: Prevent slips/trips/falls, fire, pollution and penalties; comply with waste rules and consent conditions.
scope: General housekeeping, material storage, C&D waste, hazardous waste, e-waste, batteries, plastic, bio-medical (first-aid room), used oil; dust, noise, water, dewatering discharge; labour camp sanitation.
hazards: Trips on debris/cables; falling stacked materials; fire from waste; vector-borne disease in camps; SPCB directions/closure
pre: Waste management plan: segregation points (concrete/soil/steel/wood/plastic/hazardous), authorised vendors (SPCB-registered), manifests; C&D plan for ≥ 20,000 m² (2025 Rules)
CTE/CTO conditions understood (dust, noise, STP, DG); HW authorisation; e-waste/battery producer/bulk-consumer obligations
Dust control: barricade ≥ 3 m sheet, sprinkling, wheel wash, covered trucks, no burning
Camp: potable water testing, toilets (1 per 20), bathing, drainage, waste bins, fogging
steps: Daily clean-as-you-go; designated laydown areas; stacks ≤ 1.5 m (manual) with stable bases; walkways ≥ 1 m clear.
Cables/hoses routed overhead or protected; no trailing leads in walkways.
Segregate waste at source; label bins; hazardous waste in bunded, roofed store ≤ 90 days; manifest Form 10 to TSDF/recycler; Form 4 return by 30 June.
Used oil/oily rags/paint cans: hazardous; batteries to registered recycler (Battery Waste Rules 2022); e-waste to registered dismantler.
C&D waste: on-site segregation, reuse, transport to authorised processing facility with records; no dumping in lakes/drains/roadside (heavy fines in Bengaluru/Chennai).
Dust: suppression on roads/stockpiles, cover fine materials, speed limits, enclosures for cutting; AQ monitoring if required by EC.
Water: dewatering discharge through settlement; no silt to storm drains; rainwater harvesting; STP for camps.
Noise: timings, enclosures; community notice for night work with permission.
Sanitation: clean toilets daily, soap/water, waste collection, pest control; malaria/dengue prevention (no stagnant water).
Monthly environmental inspection; six-monthly EC compliance; Form V environmental statement by 30 Sept (where applicable).

Discharge of silt/oil to drain

t: Occupational Health Surveillance, First Aid & Welfare
purpose: Detect and prevent work-related ill health early; provide statutory medical, first-aid and welfare facilities.
scope: Pre-employment and periodic medical examinations, dangerous-operations surveillance, first-aid boxes/rooms, ambulance, occupational health centre, drinking water, sanitation, canteen, crèche, rest rooms, labour accommodation, mental health.
hazards: Undetected occupational disease (silicosis, NIHL, dermatitis, lead/solvent toxicity); heat illness; infectious disease in camps; fatigue; psychosocial stress
pre: Medical examination schedule per state rules dangerous-operations schedules and OSH Code (annual health examination for prescribed classes); Form numbers per state rules
First-aid: 1 box per 150 workers (verify state rule), contents per rule, trained first-aider per shift (≥ 1 per 150), ambulance room/OHC for 500+ workers (factory) or as rules; AED recommended

Welfare: drinking water (cool, potable, 1 point per 150), latrines/urinals (1 per 20–25 workers; separate for women), washing, rest shelter, canteen (100+ under OSH Code; 250+ under some state rules – verify), crèche (50+ workers under OSH Code), lunch room
Occupational health centre: part-time/full-time medical officer thresholds per state rules for hazardous units
steps: Pre-employment medical for all; fitness for specific tasks (height, confined space, crane, driver – vision/epilepsy screen).
Periodic exams per exposure (lead: blood lead 6-monthly; noise: audiometry annual; silica: CXR/spirometry per schedule); records in prescribed register.
Notify occupational diseases (OSH Code s.12; Third Schedule) by medical practitioner and employer.
First-aid boxes inspected weekly; register of treatments; first-aider list displayed.
Emergency medical: ambulance or vehicle on call 24×7; hospital tie-ups (trauma, burns, poison); transport time < 30 min.
Welfare inspections weekly (water quality tests monthly; toilets cleaned daily; camp hygiene).
Heat/cold/monsoon health advisories; vaccination drives where relevant (tetanus for injuries).
Mental health: fatigue management (hours, rest days), grievance channel, POSH committee, counselling access (ISO 45003).
Return-to-work after injury with modified duties; compensation coordination (ESI/EC).
Annual health report to safety committee; OHC statistics in annual return.

No first-aider on shift
records: Medical examination registers/certificates, first-aid register, OHC records, disease notifications, water tests, welfare inspection

t: Safety Governance – Safety Officer, Safety Committee, Audits & Legal Register
purpose: Establish statutory governance: appointments, committee, audits, legal compliance monitoring and management review.
scope: Factories, construction sites, MAH units, mines; corporate HSE management system (ISO 45001/14001).
roles: Safety officer(s) – qualified per rules (degree/diploma in industrial safety; thresholds by headcount)
Safety committee (equal employer/worker representation; chaired by senior manager; meets at least quarterly – monthly on many sites)
hazards: Governance gaps found in audits/inspections; prosecutions of occupier/manager
pre: Appointment letters & notification to ICF (safety officer, manager/occupier particulars); qualification evidence
Safety committee constitution notified; minutes system

Legal register listing every applicable act/rule/consent/licence with renewal dates (Factories/OSH registration, fire NOC, CTE/CTO, HW authorisation, PESO licences, boiler certificates, lift licences, competent-person certificates, BOCW registration/cess, contractor licences, EC)
Audit plan: internal (ISO 45001 cl. 9.2), statutory safety audit (Karnataka Safety Audit Rules 2024; MSIHC Rule 12 annual for MAH; IS 14489), external certification
steps: Set OHS policy signed by top management; objectives & KPIs (leading/lagging).
Appoint safety officer(s) per threshold (OSH Code s.23: factory 500+, hazardous factory 250+, construction 250+ — verify rules) and welfare officer (250+); medical officer for hazardous units.
Constitute safety committee (OSH Code s.22) with worker representatives; meet quarterly minimum; track actions.

Maintain legal register; compliance evaluation quarterly; calendar of renewals, returns (annual return, Form V, HW Form 4, cess), and statutory tests (lifting 12 m, pressure vessels, hoists 6 m, extinguishers, earth pits, electrical inspection).
Inspections: daily supervisor, weekly safety officer, monthly management walk; findings tracked.
Audits: internal annually; statutory safety audit by recognised auditor as per rules; close findings with evidence.
Management review (ISO 45001 cl. 9.3) at least annually: performance, incidents, audits, legal changes (e.g. OSH state rules notification), resources.
Consultation & participation: safety committee, toolbox feedback, suggestion scheme, worker right to refuse unsafe work (OSH Code).
Document control: procedures, forms, records retention.
Report to board/corporate; benchmark with IS 3786 rates.

Expired statutory certificate affecting safety (e.g. crane test)
records: Policy, appointments, committee minutes, legal register, audit reports, management review, inspection logs, statutory registers

t: Management of Change (MoC)
purpose: Ensure changes to process, equipment, chemicals, procedures, organisation or site layout are risk-assessed and communicated before implementation.
scope: Permanent, temporary and emergency changes; 'replacement in kind' excluded; includes design changes on construction projects and temporary works alterations.
hazards: Unreviewed changes causing incidents (e.g. bypassed trip, new solvent, altered scaffold); temporary changes becoming permanent
pre: MoC form and register; classification (minor/major); PHA trigger criteria; PSSR (pre-start-up safety review) checklist
steps: Describe change, technical basis, duration (temporary ≤ 90 days with removal date).
Risk assess: HAZOP/What-if as appropriate; environmental aspects; legal implications (consents, licences, MSIHC thresholds).
Update documents: P&IDs, procedures, SDS, training, emergency plan, drawings.
Approve at defined level; communicate to affected persons (training/toolbox).
PSSR before start-up: construction per design, procedures in place, training done, permits.
Close MoC after verification; temporary changes reverted or converted via new MoC.
Audit MoC compliance quarterly.

t: Pressure Systems, Boilers & Steam/Air Lines
purpose: Prevent boiler/vessel explosions, steam burns and compressed-air injuries.
scope: IBR boilers, steam pipelines, air receivers, autoclaves, heat exchangers, pressure vessels, compressors, hydro-testing, pneumatic testing.
hazards: Low-water explosion; safety-valve failure; corrosion/thinning; pneumatic test energy; steam leaks; blowdown hazards
pre: Boiler registered; current certificate of inspection; IBR-approved repairs; attendant certificates; log sheets
Pressure vessels: examined by competent person (external every 6 months, internal 12 months, hydraulic test every 4 years – per state Factories Rules, verify); safety valves tested; gauges calibrated
Pneumatic testing only with written procedure, exclusion zone, and approval; hydro-test preferred
steps: Daily boiler checks: water level (gauge glass blowdown), safety valve lift test weekly, low-water cut-off test, flame failure, feedwater treatment.
Start-up/shutdown per written procedure; purge before ignition; no bypassing of interlocks.
Blowdown to blowdown vessel; valves operated in sequence; PPE for steam.
Isolate steam lines for maintenance by double block & bleed; drain condensate; lock; test cold.
Air receivers: drain daily, safety valve test, inspection per rules; never use air for cleaning body.
Record all tests in boiler log and vessel register; renew certificates before expiry.
Accident/explosion: stop, isolate, report to Chief Inspector of Boilers within 24 h; preserve scene.
ppe: Face shield, heat-resistant gloves, FR clothing near steam; hearing protection
stop: Certificate expired
Safety valve inoperative
Water level not visible
records: Boiler certificates, log sheets, vessel examination reports, safety valve tests, operator certificates
