t: Laboratory Safety (QC/R&D/Microbiology)
purpose: Protect laboratory staff from chemical, biological, physical and fire hazards in plant QC, R&D and testing labs.
scope: Analytical/QC labs in chemical, pharma, food, cement, steel and construction-material testing; microbiology labs (BSL-1/2); pilot plants by analogy.
hazards: Chemical exposure (solvents, acids, HF, cyanides, carcinogens), splashes to eyes, peroxide-formers, incompatible storage
Fire from solvents/heating mantles; pressure/vacuum glassware implosion; compressed gases; cryogenics (asphyxiation, cold burns)
Biological agents, sharps, aerosols; autoclave burns
Ergonomics (pipetting), electrical, heavy equipment (presses, ovens, muffle furnaces in material-testing labs)
pre: Chemical hygiene plan; SDS library; chemical inventory with max quantities; segregated storage (acids/bases/oxidisers/flammables); flammables ≤ 10 L on bench, cabinets for more; peroxide-former dating/testing
Fume hoods (face velocity 0.4–0.5 m/s, annual test), biosafety cabinets (annual certification), LEV at instruments; eyewash and safety shower within 10 s, tested weekly
Gas cylinders secured, regulators matched, leak checks; cryogen handling PPE and O2 monitors in storage rooms
Waste: segregated solvent/halogenated/aqueous/sharps/bio streams, labelled, manifested (HW/BMW rules); autoclave validation
Training (incl. HF first aid – calcium gluconate gel), emergency procedures, lab access control, no lone working with hazardous procedures
steps: Plan experiments/tests with risk assessment; use smallest quantities; prefer closed systems.
Wear lab coat, goggles, gloves per SDS; no food/drink; tie hair; closed shoes; wash hands.
Work in hood with sash low; keep hood uncluttered; never store chemicals in hood.
Heating: mantles/water baths over open flames; no unattended heating; use pressure-rated vessels; shield vacuum glassware.
Label all containers (name, hazard, date, owner); date peroxide-formers (ethers) and discard per policy.
Spills: small – trained staff with kit; large/toxic – evacuate, ventilate, call ERT; mercury spills with specific kit.
Biological: BSL-2 practices, biosafety cabinet for aerosols, autoclave waste, disinfect surfaces, sharps containers, immunisations/medical surveillance.
Material-testing labs: guard presses/compression machines, hot-sample handling from ovens/furnaces with tongs/gloves, silica dust from grinding (LEV), noise.
Housekeeping, weekly safety inspection, chemical inventory review quarterly, equipment electrical safety (PAT), emergency drills.
ppe: Lab coat (FR for flammable work), chemical splash goggles, face shield for acids/HF, nitrile/neoprene gloves, cryogenic gloves/face shield, respirator for specific tasks, closed-toe shoes
stop: Fume hood failed/flow alarm
Eyewash/shower inoperative
Unlabelled or peroxide-crystallised chemical
Lone working on hazardous procedure
Cylinder unsecured/leaking
records: Chemical inventory, SDS register, hood/BSC tests, eyewash tests, waste manifests, training, incident/near-miss, medical surveillance (bio)

india: IS 4209 code of safety in chemical laboratories and plants

Factories Act via state rules (laboratories within factories – hazardous process provisions, Sch. II PELs); OSH Code s.6; HOWM Rules 2016; Bio-Medical Waste Rules 2016; DBT biosafety guidelines; Gas Cylinders Rules 2016; MSIHC (quantities rarely exceed thresholds); IS 15656
ka: DFBISH; KSPCB (lab waste); Karnataka Bio-medical waste authorisation
tn: DISH TN; TNPCB; TN BMW authorisation
osha: 1910.1450 (Laboratory Standard – Chemical Hygiene Plan); 1910.1200; 1910.1030; 1910.134; 1910.151; NFPA 45 (fire protection for laboratories using chemicals)
intl: ISO/IEC 17025 (safety clauses); OECD GLP; WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual; UK COSHH/ CLEAPSS; ACS lab safety

t: Biological Hazards, Vector Control, Water Hygiene & Pandemic Readiness
purpose: Prevent infectious disease outbreaks (vector-, water- and air-borne), animal bites and bloodborne exposures at sites, factories and labour camps.
scope: Construction camps and canteens, factory OHCs, cooling towers/water systems, STP/ETP operators, waste handlers, security/first-aiders; pandemic/epidemic response.
hazards: Dengue/malaria/chikungunya (stagnant water), leptospirosis (flood water), typhoid/cholera/hepatitis A (water/food), TB/influenza/COVID-type outbreaks in dense camps
Snake/scorpion/dog bites (rabies), tetanus from injuries
Bloodborne pathogens for first-aiders, sharps in waste, legionella from cooling towers/showers, H2S/biological at STPs
pre: Camp/site standards: potable water (IS 10500; tested monthly; chlorination), food safety (FSSAI-registered canteens, hygiene training), toilets/bathing, drainage, waste collection, bedding spacing/ventilation, isolation room
Vector control plan: weekly source reduction (no stagnant water in tyres, drums, excavations), larvicide, fogging in season, nets/repellents, ULB coordination; monsoon campaign

Medical: pre-employment screening, vaccinations as advised (tetanus, hepatitis B for first-aiders/waste handlers, typhoid), antivenom/rabies PEP availability mapped to hospitals, first-aid kits with bite protocol
Water systems: legionella risk assessment of cooling towers/hot water (temperature control, biocide dosing, cleaning quarterly/6-monthly, sampling), drift eliminators, records

Outbreak plan: case definition, reporting to District Health Officer (notifiable diseases), isolation, contact tracing, PPE stocks (masks, gloves, sanitiser), remote-work/shift segregation, communication in local languages
steps: Daily camp inspection: water, toilets, waste, drainage; weekly larval survey; act on findings within 24 h.
Food: canteen hygiene audit monthly; food handlers' medical certificates; safe storage temperatures.

Bites: snake — immobilise limb, no cutting/sucking/tourniquet, hospital with antivenom within 1 h; dog/animal — wash wound 15 min with soap, rabies PEP; scorpion — hospital (prazosin where indicated); record and remove attractants (rodents, debris piles).
Injuries: tetanus prophylaxis per vaccination status; first-aiders use gloves, sharps containers, disinfect; post-exposure protocol for needle-stick (OHC/hospital).
STP/ETP: PPE (gloves, boots, goggles), H2S monitoring, hand hygiene, vaccination (hepatitis), confined-space procedure for sumps.

Cooling towers: monthly inspection, biocide/scale control, cleaning and disinfection per schedule, Legionella sampling where risk assessment requires; shut down and clean after any positive result; shower heads descaled.
Respiratory outbreaks: screening at gate, masks, ventilation, isolation, report cluster to health authority, stagger shifts; follow MoHFW/State advisories.
Records: water tests, vector control log, medical cases/outbreak reports, vaccination, cooling-tower maintenance.
ppe: Gloves, masks (as per risk), boots, goggles for waste/STP; repellents/nets for camps
stop: Water test failing bacteriological standard
Confirmed cluster of infectious disease
Antivenom/rabies PEP access not confirmed for remote site
Cooling tower positive Legionella without action
records: Water quality tests, vector control & larval survey logs, canteen audits, vaccination records, bite/injury register, outbreak reports to health authority, cooling-tower logs

intl: WHO guidance; ILO; ASHRAE 188 (legionellosis); UK HSE L8/HSG274 (legionella)

t: Site Security, Workplace Violence & Public Safety
purpose: Protect people, assets and the public from unauthorised access, theft, violence, harassment, civil disturbance and threats, and ensure security measures never compromise emergency egress.
scope: Perimeter and access control, visitor/contractor management, materials control, CCTV, guarding, cash/explosives/fuel/chemical security, hoardings and public walkways, labour unrest, harassment (POSH), threats and bomb calls.
hazards: Theft of scaffold/formwork components (collapse risk), cable theft (electrical hazards), fuel/explosives diversion
Unauthorised entry into hazardous areas; trespass by children into excavations/water bodies
Violence/harassment; crowd events during unrest; vehicle ramming at gates
Security measures that lock fire exits or block emergency access
pre: Risk-based security plan; licensed guards with verified antecedents; shift rosters; training in emergency response and first aid
Access control: ID cards/biometric, visitor register and escorts, vehicle gate passes, material in/out registers, key control; hazardous stores (explosives, chemicals, fuel) with locks/CCTV/logs
Perimeter: fencing/hoarding ≥ 2 m, lighting, CCTV with 30-day retention, signage; public walkways with overhead protection where work above; excavations fenced at night
Policies: POSH (ICC constituted, displayed), anti-violence, grievance redressal (IR Code committees), drug/alcohol, weapons prohibition; threat/bomb-call procedure; media policy
Coordination with police (beat officer contacts), fire service; emergency egress must never be locked — security checks exits daily
steps: Gate: verify ID/induction before entry; log visitors; issue PPE; vehicles inspected; hazardous materials checked against manifests.
Patrols: perimeter and hazardous stores every shift; night checks of cranes/hoists isolation, fuel bunds, excavation fencing; report defects.
Public safety: maintain hoardings, covered walkways, debris nets; no material stored on public footpath; traffic marshals at site exits; night lighting.

Incidents: theft/trespass — secure, record, report to police; violence/harassment — immediate safety, medical aid, report via ICC/HR, no retaliation; unrest — de-escalate, protect lives, inform police, safe shutdown of plant (process isolation) if needed.
Threats/bomb calls: record details, inform site head/police, evacuate per plan without panic, do not touch suspicious objects.
Workplace violence prevention: training for supervisors, lone-worker protection, cash handling controls, exit interviews for grievances.
Drills: security breach and threat scenarios annually with emergency plan.
Audit quarterly: access logs, CCTV function, guard training, exit integrity; review after incidents.
ppe: Guards: hi-vis, helmet/boots where on site, torches, radios
stop: Fire exit found locked
Hazardous store unsecured
Credible threat received
Violent incident in progress
records: Security plan, guard licences, access/visitor logs, material registers, CCTV logs, incident reports (police FIR copies), ICC records, drills, audits

tn: TN PSARA licensing; GCC norms; Greater Chennai Police

t: Drone Operations for Inspection & Survey
purpose: Use drones safely and lawfully for progress surveys, structural/roof/stack/flare inspections and confined-area reconnaissance, reducing work at height and confined-space entry.
scope: Nano/micro/small drones for photogrammetry, thermal inspection of roofs/solar/substations, chimney/flare inspection, tank internal inspection (caged drones), site security.
roles: Remote pilot (DGCA Remote Pilot Certificate for applicable classes)
hazards: Drone strike on persons/plant/lines; loss of control/fly-away; Li-Po battery fire; propeller injuries
Flying in restricted zones (airport, defence) – legal violations; privacy; distraction of crane operators
pre: DGCA compliance: type-certified drone with UIN; remote pilot certificate; Digital Sky zone check (green zone or permission); ≤ 120 m AGL; VLOS; insurance; no flight over crowds or near cranes in operation without coordination

Site SOP: flight plan, exclusion of persons under flight path, coordination with crane/lifting operations (no simultaneous), weather limits (wind, rain), battery management (fire-safe charging bags/cabinet), emergency landing areas
Industrial sites: hazardous-area check (no non-Ex drones in Zone 1/2 during operation), permits from plant control room, EMI near substations
steps: Pre-flight: zone check, NOTAM/airspace, weather, battery/propeller/firmware check, geofence set, return-to-home altitude above obstacles.
Brief site: announce flight, cordon take-off/landing area, spotter assigned, crane operators informed (stop lifts in overlap).
Fly within VLOS; avoid people, lines and structures by safe margins; abort on control/signal loss warnings.
Internal tank/duct inspections: caged drone, confined-space hazards still apply to any human entry; atmosphere test for ignition risk if flammable vapours.
Post-flight: logs, battery storage at 40–60% charge, data secured (privacy), defects reported; incidents/near-misses reported (and to DGCA where required).
Maintenance per OEM; propeller replacement; annual review of SOP and certificates.
ppe: Standard; safety glasses for pilots near take-off; gloves for battery handling
stop: Zone not permitted / no permission
Wind above limit, rain, low visibility
Persons under flight path cannot be cleared
Crane operating in overlap
Battery swollen/damaged
records: Pilot certificates, UIN, flight logs, zone permissions, battery logs, incident reports

t: Carbon Accounting – GHG Inventory (Scope 1/2/3), CCTS Compliance & Verification
purpose: Produce an auditable organisational GHG inventory aligned with GHG Protocol/ISO 14064-1, meet CCTS obligations where the site is an obligated entity, and supply CBAM data to EU customers.
scope: All sites: stationary combustion (boilers, furnaces, DG sets, kilns), mobile combustion (fleet, site plant), process emissions (cement calcination, steel, chemicals), fugitive (refrigerants, SF6, methane), purchased electricity/steam, and Scope 3 categories material to the business (purchased goods, fuel & energy, upstream transport, waste, business travel, commuting, use of sold products).
roles: Sustainability/energy manager (BEE-certified energy manager where designated consumer)
Site data owners (utilities, stores, fleet, maintenance)
Internal auditor; Accredited Carbon Verification Agency (ACVA) / assurance provider
hazards: Data gaps and double counting; wrong emission factors; unverifiable claims (greenwashing liability under SEBI/ASCI/EU rules)
Missing CCTS deadlines → CCC purchase/penalty; CBAM default-value mark-ups
pre: Boundary: operational control; list of sites and sources; base year (CCTS: FY2023-24); materiality thresholds

Emission factors: IPCC 2006 for fuels (diesel ≈ 2.68 kg CO2/L, petrol ≈ 2.3, LPG ≈ 3.0 kg/kg, natural gas ≈ 1.9 kg/SCM, furnace oil ≈ 3.1 kg/kg, Indian non-coking coal ≈ 1.6–1.9 t CO2/t by grade), CEA grid factor (v20: 0.727 tCO2/MWh FY2023-24), GWPs (IPCC AR5/AR6 as required by the scheme), process factors (e.g. clinker 0.52 tCO2/t); BEE-specified factors override for CCTS
Data systems: metered fuel/electricity, stores issue records, refrigerant purchase/leak logs, production data; monthly data close; QA/QC checks
CCTS (obligated entities): monitoring plan submitted/approved by BEE; monthly monitoring; registry account (Grid-India); ACVA appointed; GEI target known
CBAM (exporters): product–CN code mapping; installation-level direct/indirect emissions; precursor data; verifier; CBAM registry access via EU customer
steps: Collect monthly activity data by source; reconcile with finance (fuel invoices, electricity bills) and production.

Calculate Scope 1 by source (fuel × NCV × EF; process; fugitive = purchases − returns ± inventory change × GWP); Scope 2 location-based (kWh × grid factor) and market-based (contracts/RECs where allowed); Scope 3 by category with documented methods.
Compute intensity: tCO2e per tonne product (GEI for CCTS), per ₹ crore turnover (BRSR), per unit floor area for buildings.
Quality: uncertainty assessment, completeness check, documentation of assumptions; internal review; management sign-off.

CCTS: submit verified GHG emission report within 4 months of FY end (31 July); respond to ACVA findings; receive/surrender CCCs via registry; plan abatement (energy efficiency, fuel switch, RE PPAs, process changes) to meet next year's GEI.

CBAM: compile installation data per EU template (direct emissions by production process, electricity consumption with factor, precursors), get verification, share with EU importer before their 30 Sep annual declaration; record carbon price paid in India for deduction claims.
Disclosure: BRSR Principle 6 (Scope 1/2 totals, intensity, Scope 3 leadership), CDP/GRI as applicable; maintain evidence files for assurance.
Improvement: set targets (SBTi-aligned where chosen), energy audits (EC Act), project pipeline, annual recalculation of base year on structural change.

Deadline risk for CCTS/BRSR

t: ESG Reporting (BRSR), Energy Management & EPR Compliance
purpose: Run a defensible ESG programme: BRSR/BRSR Core disclosures with assurance, energy management under the EC Act, EPR obligations, and integration of safety KPIs into ESG reporting.
scope: Listed entities (top 1,000) and their suppliers facing value-chain requests; designated consumers under the EC Act; producers/bulk consumers under EPR; companies supplying EU customers (CSRD/CBAM data requests).
hazards: Inconsistent OSH data between statutory registers and BRSR (assurance findings); misstatements (SEBI action)
Missed EPR registration/targets (environmental compensation); EC Act penalties for energy audit/return defaults
pre: Materiality assessment; ESG governance (board committee), policies (NGRBC nine principles), data owners and controls; ESG data platform or controlled spreadsheets

BRSR Core KPI definitions: LTIFR (per million hours), fatalities, high-consequence injuries, recordable injuries, safety-related complaints; energy intensity; water intensity; waste; GHG; wages/gender; customer complaints; openness of business (trade payables concentration)

EC Act: check designated-consumer status (thresholds by sector), appoint energy manager, energy audit by accredited auditor (periodicity per notification), annual energy return (Form 1/2) to SDA/BEE; ISO 50001 recommended

EPR: register as producer/importer/brand owner/bulk consumer/generator on CPCB portals (plastic, e-waste, battery, tyre, used oil); set up collection/hand-over contracts with registered recyclers; annual returns
Supplier code of conduct and value-chain data collection (≥ 2% partners for BRSR assurance); human-rights/labour due diligence (child/forced labour, wages, OSH)

Collect and reconcile OSH data from incident registers, OSH Code annual return, ESI records; hours worked from attendance systems; ensure the same numbers appear in BRSR, annual return and insurance filings.

Environmental data: GHG (from inventory), energy (bills/meters), water (withdrawal/discharge by source), waste by type and disposal (manifests), air emissions (stack results); recycled inputs; EPR fulfilment.

Assurance: engage practitioner; evidence packs per KPI; walkthroughs; close findings; management representation.

EPR operations: tagging of e-waste/battery/used-oil generation, storage limits, hand-over to registered recyclers with certificates, portal returns; plastic packaging accounting.
Review annually with board; update materiality; align with ISSB/CSRD as customer demands evolve.

t: Fire Protection Systems – Design Basis, Testing, Maintenance & Impairment Control
purpose: Keep fire-water, sprinkler, hydrant, detection, alarm, suppression and passive fire-protection systems reliable, and control periods when they are impaired.
scope: Factories, warehouses, high-rise construction (progressive installation), tank farms (foam/cooling), data/control rooms (clean agent), battery rooms, kitchens (wet chemical), substations (CO2/water mist), labour camps (extinguishers/water).
hazards: Systems that fail on demand: dry pumps, closed valves, low water, dead batteries, blocked hydrants, painted sprinklers, impaired detectors
Unmanaged impairments during maintenance/construction → uncontrolled fire; hot work during impairment
pre: Design basis per NBC Part 4/IS/TAC/NFPA: hazard classification, water reserve (typically 2–4 h), pump set (electric + diesel + jockey), hydrant spacing, sprinkler density, detection type by area, foam for Class B, clean agent for electronics, Class D for metals; drawings and hydraulic calculations
Fire NOC and insurer requirements documented; AMC with competent agency; spares; ITM schedule (NFPA 25 / IS 15105 / IS 13039 / IS 2189 / IS 2190)

Impairment procedure: pre-planned vs emergency impairment; tags on valves/panels; notification list (fire brigade where required, insurer, site head); compensating measures (fire watch, hot-work ban, extra extinguishers, hose lines charged); restoration test
Water supply security: tank level monitoring, alternative supply/tanker tie-up; power supply to pumps on dedicated feeder/DG
steps: Weekly: diesel pump 30-min run, electric pump churn test, jockey pressure, control valve supervision (open and locked/sealed), alarm panel healthy, water level, hydrant cabinet contents.

Monthly: extinguisher visual (pressure, seal, tag), emergency lighting flick test, fire doors/closers, hydrant valve exercise sample, foam system visual, detector cleanliness, sprinkler heads not obstructed/painted/storage ≥ 450 mm below.

Quarterly: hydrant flow at remote points, main drain test (sprinklers), alarm devices audibility test, fire door inspection, gas-suppression pressure/weight check, duct/kitchen hood cleaning as needed.

Annual: pump performance (flow/pressure curve), full sprinkler/hydrant test including deluge trip, detection loop test 100% of devices, foam concentrate lab test, extinguisher service, emergency lighting 3-h duration, passive fire-stopping survey, fire-drill with system use; 5-yearly: internal pipe inspection, pressure gauge calibration, hydrostatic test of hoses; 10-yearly CO2/clean-agent cylinder hydro test; extinguisher hydro test 3–5 years.

Construction sites: install standpipe/riser as floors rise (charged within two floors of work), temporary hydrants, extinguishers per floor and at hot-work; maintain fire tender access roads; protect systems from construction damage.
Impairment: authorise on tag/log; implement compensating measures; limit duration (same shift where possible); restore and test; close log; notify.
Keep records (ITM logs) for Fire Service/insurer; trend defects; replace obsolete components; update design basis on occupancy/process change.
Train ERT on hydrant/hose drill, pump operation, panel reset, foam branch use; monthly drills.
ppe: ERT: fire kit, helmet, gloves, boots; SCBA
stop: Fire pump failed test/ unavailable without compensating measures
Water reserve below minimum
Main control valve found closed/unsupervised
Hot work planned during impairment without controls
records: Design basis & drawings, Fire NOC/insurer surveys, ITM logs (weekly/monthly/quarterly/annual/5-yr), impairment log, AMC reports, drill records, defect trend

Karnataka Fire Force Act 1964; KSFES NOC renewal inspections; BBMP high-rise fire conditions

TN Fire Service Act 1985; TNFRS fire licence/NOC; TN CDBR 2019 fire provisions

t: Cooling Towers, Water Systems & Legionella Control
purpose: Prevent Legionnaires' disease and water-system hazards (chemical dosing, drift, confined spaces) in cooling towers, evaporative condensers, hot and cold water systems and spray systems.
scope: Industrial cooling towers, HVAC towers, evaporative condensers, hot-water systems, showers in camps/plants, humidifiers, water features, firewater tanks (stagnation).
hazards: Legionella growth 20–45 °C in stagnant/biofilm water; aerosol from drift and showers; immunocompromised/older workers at risk
Biocide/acid/alkali dosing chemicals (chlorine, bromine, hypochlorite); confined-space entry into basins/tanks; falls on wet tower decks/ladders
pre: Written scheme/risk assessment: schematic of systems, dead legs identified, control measures, monitoring, roles; records for 5 years

Cooling towers: drift eliminators, accessible basins, biocide programme (oxidising + non-oxidising), corrosion/scale control, bleed-off, cleaning/disinfection at least 6-monthly (quarterly in heavy fouling), microbiological testing (TVC monthly, Legionella quarterly), action levels (Legionella ≥ 100 cfu/L review; ≥ 1,000 cfu/L immediate disinfection)
Hot/cold water: hot stored ≥ 60 °C, distributed ≥ 50 °C, cold < 20 °C; flush little-used outlets weekly; descale shower heads quarterly; TMVs maintained
Chemical dosing: bunded, labelled, SDS, PPE, eyewash; automated dosing with interlocks; no mixing of acids with hypochlorite
Confined-space procedures for basins/tanks; WAH for tower access
steps: Weekly: check tower operation, water treatment parameters (conductivity, pH, biocide residual), bleed, drift eliminators; flush infrequently used outlets.
Monthly: TVC sampling; temperature checks at sentinel taps (hot/cold); inspect tanks/tower condition; dosing equipment calibration.
Quarterly: Legionella sampling (towers; hot/cold where risk), shower-head cleaning, tower pack/basin inspection.
Six-monthly: tower cleaning & disinfection (chlorination ≥ 5–50 mg/L per method, contact time, neutralise before discharge to drain – SPCB limits), tank cleaning where sediment; review scheme.
Positive results: ≥ 1,000 cfu/L — immediate shock disinfection, re-sample, investigate; cluster of pneumonia cases — inform health authority, isolate system.
Shutdown/stagnation: drain or maintain circulation and biocide; before restart after > 1 week idle, clean/disinfect; firewater tanks on recirculation/chlorination schedule.
Chemical handling: PPE, spill kits, segregated storage; dosing room ventilation; never mix.
Records of all checks, results and actions; annual review of risk assessment; training for operators.
ppe: Gloves, goggles/face shield for chemicals, respirator (FFP3) when cleaning towers/aerosol work, harness for tower access, boots
stop: Legionella ≥ 1,000 cfu/L untreated
Dosing failure/biocide residual absent for > 48 h
Entry into basin without confined-space controls
Discharge of disinfectant without neutralisation
records: Water-system schematics & risk assessment, treatment logs, sampling results, cleaning/disinfection certificates, dosing chemical SDS/inventory, incident/outbreak reports

india: OSH Code s.6 & s.24 (welfare water); Factories Act s.11/s.18 via state rules; Water Act (cooling tower blowdown/ disinfectant discharge consent); IS 10500 (drinking water); MoHFW guidance; HOWM (spent chemicals)
ka: KSPCB discharge consent for cooling tower blowdown; BBMP water supply standards
tn: TNPCB; CMWSSB; TN Public Health Act notification of disease clusters
osha: General Duty Clause; OSHA Technical Manual Section III Ch. 7 (Legionnaires' disease); 1910.146 for basins
intl: UK HSE L8 ACOP & HSG274 Parts 1–3; ASHRAE 188 & Guideline 12; EU Technical Guidelines for Legionella; WHO

t: Power Presses & Press Shop (Mechanical, Hydraulic, Servo)
purpose: Prevent hand and finger amputations, crush injuries and die-ejection incidents on power presses, press brakes and transfer lines in press shops and component units.
scope: Mechanical (clutch/brake), hydraulic and servo presses 10–2,500 t; press brakes; tandem and transfer lines; die setting and try-out; coil/blank feeding; scrap handling; die storage and maintenance.
roles: Press shop head (authorises operators and die-setters)
hazards: Hands in point of operation: clutch failure, double stroke, repeat, unexpected descent; crush between ram and bolster
Die ejection, slug/scrap fly-out, broken punch fragments; coil whip when cutting bands; sharp blanks
Die setting: 1–20 t dies lifted by EOT/forklift, hands between die halves, ram creep with no safety blocks
Noise 95–110 dB(A) at impact; vibration; oil mist; back and shoulder strain from repetitive loading
pre: Each press risk-assessed per ISO 12100; safeguarding by fixed/interlocked guards, light curtains (ISO 13855: S = 1,600 mm/s × T + C), two-hand control (both within 0.5 s) or automatic feed with enclosure

Mechanical presses: part-revolution clutch with brake monitor, anti-repeat, stroke selector keyed; full-revolution (positive-clutch) presses only with fixed enclosure or hand-removal tools; no foot pedal without light curtain
Safety circuit designed and validated to ISO 13849-1 PL d/e (Cat 3/4) or IEC 62061 SIL 2/3; e-stops at every station; stop time measured and recorded at commissioning and after brake work
Die-setting: safety blocks (ram props) rated for ram weight, die clamps/lifting points inspected, EOT with rated slings, die carts; die height and shut height set under written procedure
Operators 18+, trained and authorised in writing; state dangerous-operations schedule for power presses complied (TN Rule 53 Schedule / KA Rule 56 Schedule — verify); hearing-conservation zone marked
steps: Shift start: operator checks guards, light curtain function (test piece at three heights), two-hand controls, e-stop, brake-monitor lamp, lubrication; records in press log; defects → tag out, inform supervisor.

Set-up by die setter only: press isolated (LOTO) before hands enter die space; ram at bottom or safety blocks in; die clamped at all designated points; guard re-fitted and verified before first stroke.
First-off inspection in inch/single-stroke mode with hands outside; verify stripper, slug chute, scrap exit, part ejection; approve run.
Production: feed/unload with hands outside the light-curtain plane or with tongs/magnets; never reach to clear a misfeed on a cycling press — stop, isolate, then clear.
Multi-operator presses: a two-hand station per operator, all required to initiate; supervisor keys stroke selector; no bypass keys left in machines.
Coil handling: cut bands from the side with band cutter, face shield, gloves; coil cars/decoilers interlocked; secure coil before releasing clamp.
Hydraulic presses: check pressure relief setting and hose condition; treat hydraulic leaks as injection-injury risk; isolate and bleed before work on cylinders.
Scrap: enclosed chutes and conveyors to bins; cut-resistant gloves for blank handling; no hand-trimming of burrs on moving line.
Maintenance: LOTO at main isolator plus pneumatic/hydraulic dump; brake lining, clutch air pressure and stop-time checked at defined intervals
Thorough examination of press and safety devices every 6 months (12 months if fixed guards only — PUWER benchmark, verify).
Record near misses (light-curtain trips, double strokes); investigate every double stroke as a dangerous occurrence; retrain and re-verify after any modification or relocation.
ppe: Safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves (not where entanglement risk), safety shoes with metatarsal guard at die-setting, hearing protection (SNR ≥ 25), no loose clothing or jewellery
stop: Light curtain or two-hand control fails test
Brake-monitor fault or stop time exceeds recorded value
Ram moves with hands in die space / safety blocks missing during set-up
Operator not authorised or under 18
Bypass key, jumper or taped sensor found
records: Press register with safeguarding type, stop-time and PL/SIL validation, shift checks, die-setting log, 6-monthly examinations, operator authorisations, audiometry, near-miss log

india: Factories Act ss.21–23, 26 (fencing, machinery in motion, young persons, casing of new machinery) via state rules / OSH Code s.6
IS 9474 (guarding); IS 16819 / ISO 12100; Sch. II noise limit 90 dB(A); Third Schedule (noise-induced hearing loss notifiable)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 Rule 56 Schedule (power presses — verify number); DFBISH; Karnataka Safety Audit Rules 2024
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rule 53 Schedule (power presses, shears, guillotines — verify); DISH TN
osha: 1910.217 (mechanical power presses, incl. brake monitors & PSDI), 1910.212, 1910.147; ANSI B11.1 (mechanical presses), B11.2 (hydraulic presses), B11.19 (safeguarding)
intl: ISO 16092-1/-2/-3 (presses safety); ISO 13855, ISO 13849-1, ISO 13857, ISO 14119 (interlocks); UK PUWER regs 32–35 & HSG236 (power presses)

t: Industrial Robot Cells, Interlocked Guarding & Collaborative Robots
purpose: Prevent crushing, striking and trapping of people inside robot cells during production, teaching, maintenance and recovery from faults.
scope: Welding, handling, painting, palletising and assembly robots; perimeter-guarded cells; multi-robot lines; AGV/AMR interfaces; collaborative robots (power-and-force limiting, speed and separation monitoring); cell integration and modification.
hazards: Unexpected motion from a stopped-looking robot (waiting for signal); reach beyond visible envelope; high speed (> 2 m/s) and payload inertia
Person inside cell unseen when cycle restarted from outside; muted or defeated interlocks; climbing over fences
Teach mode: pendant enabling device released late; wrong frame/speed; collision with fixtures; crush against fixed objects
Secondary hazards: weld spatter and fume, laser, pinch points of grippers, dropped parts, pneumatic/hydraulic stored energy, hot tooling
pre: Cell risk assessment to ISO 10218-2:2025 / ISO 12100 covering all task-based modes (production, teach, maintenance, cleaning, recovery); safeguarded space defined; restricted space limited by software and hard stops
Perimeter guard ≥ 1.4 m (ISO 13857 reach), interlocked gates with guard locking and trapped-key or request-to-enter
Presence sensing (laser scanners/light curtains) covering every hiding zone so restart is impossible while someone is inside
Safety functions (protective stop, speed monitoring, safe zones) on safety PLC validated to ISO 13849-1 PL d; stop performance (stopping distance/time) measured and used for safeguarding distances
Teach pendant with 3-position enabling device; T1 reduced speed ≤ 250 mm/s; T2/high-speed teaching only with written authorisation and second person at e-stop

Cobots: collision test on body regions against ISO 10218 (ex-ISO/TS 15066) force/pressure limits with calibrated measuring device; sharp tools and payload edges covered; hand-guiding only with enabling device
steps: Before entry for any reason: request access at gate, wait for 'safe to enter' (robot in protective stop, drives disabled), open gate, take gate key/lock with you — the key in your pocket keeps the cell from restarting.
Inside the cell: carry the pendant with e-stop; never trust a motionless robot — it may be waiting for a part present signal; stay out of pinch zones between robot and fixtures.
Teaching: T1 mode; enabling device held in middle position; check tool frame and speed override; second person outside at e-stop for complex paths; no production parts in cell unless needed.
Fault recovery (dropped part, weld stuck, gripper jam): follow the task-specific procedure; isolate pneumatics (dump valve) before freeing gripper; hot tooling cooled or gloves rated.
Leaving: confirm nobody else inside (visual sweep of every robot), tools removed, gate closed and reset by the same person who entered; cycle start from outside only.
Maintenance: LOTO of main disconnect, pneumatics and hydraulics; support arm before brake release; capacitor discharge time (per OEM, typically 5 min — verify) before touching drives.
Changes to program, tooling, fixtures or cell layout → management of change: re-run risk assessment, re-validate safeguarding distances, document, retrain.
Interlock audit monthly: test every gate switch, scanner zone, muting function and e-stop; any bypass found is a stop-work and investigation.
AGV/AMR interfaces: pedestrian lanes separated; AMR safety scanners validated; handover stations guarded.
Train all cell entrants (operators, cleaners, maintenance) on cell-specific hazards; record authorisation; refresher yearly.
ppe: Safety glasses, safety shoes, gloves as task requires, welding PPE where arc exposure, hearing protection; no loose clothing
stop: Any interlock, scanner or e-stop bypassed or faulty
Person can enter cell without robot going to protective stop
Teaching at high speed without authorisation and second person
Cell modified without MoC and re-validation
Cobot force/pressure test not done after tool/payload change
records: Cell risk assessment, safety validation report (stop times, PL), interlock test log, pendant/teach authorisations, MoC records, incident and near-miss log

india: Factories Act ss.21–22 via state rules / OSH Code s.6 (fencing, machinery in motion); IS 9474; IS 16819 / ISO 12100; IS 17893 (permits for cell maintenance); OSH Central Rules 2026 (machinery)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (fencing & maintenance of machinery); Karnataka Safety Audit Rules 2024
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 (fencing of machinery); DISH TN
osha: 1910.212, 1910.147 (incl. minor servicing exception limits); OSHA Technical Manual Sec. IV Ch. 4 (industrial robots); ANSI/RIA R15.06-2012; RIA TR R15.306/R15.806
intl: ISO 10218-1 & -2:2025 (robots and robot applications; incorporates ISO/TS 15066); ISO 13849-1; ISO 13855; ISO 13857; ISO 14119; ISO 3691-4 (AGVs); EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230

t: Paint Shop – Spray Booths, Solvents, Isocyanates & Ovens
purpose: Prevent fire and explosion from flammable solvents, occupational asthma from isocyanates, and burns, falls and chemical injuries in pre-treatment, e-coat, sealer, primer, top-coat and oven areas.
scope: Pre-treatment/phosphating, electro-deposition (ED) tanks, spray booths (manual, electrostatic, robotic), paint mix rooms, solvent and thinner storage, curing ovens, paint sludge and VOC abatement (RTO), repair/touch-up, booth maintenance.
roles: Maintenance (Ex equipment, oven burners, booth filters)
hazards: Flammable vapours (thinners, xylene, butyl acetate; flash points < 23 °C) — ignition by static, non-Ex electricals, hot work, electrostatic guns
Isocyanates (HDI/IPDI in 2K clear coats): respiratory sensitisation and asthma at µg/m³ levels; skin absorption; also solvents (neurotoxic), chromates in some primers, nickel/zinc phosphate
Ovens: gas explosion on light-off without purge; CO; burns; drying overspray self-heating in ducts; RTO flashback
ED tanks: 200–400 V DC in large tanks, drowning/chemical immersion; conveyors and skids overhead; falls from booth grids, pits and oven roofs; paint sludge pits (confined, H2S/solvent)
pre: Hazardous-area classification per IS 5572 / IEC 60079-10-1 (Zone 1 inside booths and mix rooms, Zone 2 around openings — verify extents)
Ex-rated electricals, lighting through sealed glass, intrinsically safe instruments; IS/IEC 60079-14/-17 inspections
Booths: downdraught/side-draught ventilation keeping vapour < 25% LEL and capture velocity ≈ 0.5 m/s at face (verify)
Overspray filters monitored by differential pressure; interlock: no spraying without airflow; sprinklers/deluge or CO2 flooding
Static: bonding and earthing of parts, conveyors, hoses and containers (< 10 Ω bonding, verify); conductive flooring and footwear; electrostatic guns interlocked with conveyor earth and ventilation
Isocyanate control: enclosed robotic application where possible; manual spraying only with supplied-air RPE (airline hood, APF 40 — verify) or PAPR with combined filters
Booth clearance time before entry; biological monitoring (urinary HDA) and annual lung-function tests for painters
Ovens per NFPA 86: pre-ignition purge ≥ 4 volume changes, flame safeguard, high-temperature limit, LEL control for solvent load, explosion relief
Solvent storage per Petroleum Rules 2002 (Class A), daily quantities only inside shop; spill kits, foam extinguishers
steps: Mix room: weigh and mix under LEV; containers earthed and bonded before pouring; lids closed; no electronic devices unless Ex; waste solvent to closed, earthed drums.
Before spraying: ventilation running and interlock proved, filters within DP limits, RPE fit and airline flow checked, no one else in booth during 2K application, warning light on.
Spraying: keep gun earthed; never point at people; stop if airflow alarm; clean guns in enclosed gun washers; dispose of rags in self-closing metal bins emptied each shift.
Booth exit: wait clearance time; remove coveralls and gloves before leaving; wash hands and face; no eating/smoking in paint areas.
Oven light-off: operator follows burner start-up sequence; never bypass purge or flame failure; check exhaust and LEL readings; keep oven doors interlocked; no entry until < 40 °C and gas-free.
ED/pre-treatment: isolate rectifier and verify dead before any work near the bath; guardrails and covers on tanks; acid/alkali handling with face shield, apron, gloves; eyewash within 10 s travel.
Booth and duct cleaning: hot work prohibited; remove overspray deposits per schedule (self-heating); confined-space permit for sludge pits and ducts; Ex-rated tools only.
Hot work or maintenance in paint shop: PTW with gas test (0% LEL), isolation of solvent lines, ventilation running; fire watch 60 min after.
Paint sludge, spent solvent, filters = hazardous waste (HOWM Sch. I); manifests; VOC emissions within SPCB consent; RTO maintained.
Health: pre-placement and annual surveillance (lung function, skin, urinary HDA where 2K used); remove sensitised workers from exposure; record and report occupational asthma as notifiable.
ppe: Supplied-air hood or PAPR with A2P3 filters for spraying, chemical splash goggles, nitrile gloves (change after contamination), antistatic FR coveralls (EN 1149/ISO 11612), conductive footwear in Zone 1
stop: Booth ventilation or LEL interlock bypassed
Non-Ex equipment or phone in Zone 1/2
Isocyanate spraying without supplied-air/PAPR or with others in booth
Oven purge or flame-failure defeated
Hot work in paint shop without permit and gas test
records: Area classification drawings, Ex inspection register, airflow and LEL records, RPE fit tests and airline checks, biological monitoring, oven safety-device tests, HW manifests, VOC monitoring, PTW records

india: Petroleum Act 1934 & Rules 2002 (Class A/B storage, licensing); Factories Act ss.37, 87 via state rules (explosive atmospheres
Dangerous operations incl. cellulose/paint spraying — verify schedule); IS 5572, IS/IEC 60079-14/-17; IS 7689 (static); IS 3103 (ventilation); HOWM Rules 2016; Air Act consent (VOC); Sch. II PELs
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 Rule 129 schedule (spray painting / cellulose — verify); KSPCB VOC conditions; KSFES
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rule 95 schedule (spray painting / cellulose solutions — verify); TNPCB; TNFRS

t: Body Shop – Resistance Spot Welding, MIG/Laser Welding & Weld Fume Control
purpose: Control welding fume (a Group 1 carcinogen), burns, crush and eye injuries, electrical and laser hazards in body-in-white shops and fabrication cells.
scope: Manual and robotic resistance spot welding (RSW), MIG/MAG and CuSi brazing, stud and projection welding, laser welding/brazing, hemming, sealing; weld guns, transformers, cooling water, fume extraction; galvanised, boron and stainless steels, aluminium.
hazards: Welding fume: Mn (TLV 0.02 mg/m³ respirable), ZnO from galvanised sheet (metal fume fever), Cr(VI)/Ni from stainless, ozone from MIG on aluminium; IARC Group 1 for all welding fume (2017)
RSW: crush between electrodes (3–6 kN force), spatter burns, hot tips, molten expulsion; magnetic fields near transformers (pacemakers); shock from primary 415 V and damaged cables
Laser: Class 4 — eye/skin injury from direct or reflected beam, fume with fine particles, fire; enclosure interlocks
Fire from spatter on sealers, cardboard, oils; cooling-water leaks onto electrics; manual handling of weld guns (balancers), awkward postures; noise and UV (arc eye) for MIG
pre: Fume control hierarchy: enclosed robotic welding with extraction; on-torch/on-gun LEV for manual MIG
General ventilation alone is not acceptable for indoor welding (HSE 2019 benchmark); RPE (FFP3/PAPR) where LEV cannot capture
Exposure monitoring for Mn, Zn, Cr(VI), Ni, total fume against Sch. II / ACGIH values; health surveillance (lung function, respiratory questionnaire, Cr(VI)/Ni skin checks)

RSW guns: insulated handles, two-hand or enabling initiation for manual guns, tip dressers guarded, balancers and rails inspected; transformer secondary earthed; cables inspected weekly; water-flow switches interlocked
Laser cells: Class 1 enclosure with interlocked access, beam stops, warning lamps, laser safety officer, eyewear for maintenance in Class 4 mode (IEC 60825-1/-4); fume extraction with HEPA
Fire: sealers/adhesives and packaging kept away from arc zones; spark screens; extinguishers (CO2/DCP) every 15 m; hot-work permit for any welding outside designated shop areas
steps: Shift start: check LEV airflow indicators, hood positions, gun insulation, cables, water hoses, balancers; defective items tagged out.
Manual RSW: position panel, keep fingers clear of electrode line, initiate with both hands/enable; dress tips only with guarded dresser; let tips cool before handling.
MIG/MAG: position extraction nozzle ≤ 150–300 mm from arc (verify by smoke test); use welding helmet with correct shade (9–13), leather gloves/jacket; screens for others.
Galvanised or coated parts: extra extraction; stop and report metal fume fever symptoms (chills, fever after shift); remove coating where practical before welding.
Aluminium MIG: ozone — extraction plus ventilation; check for 'sweet' smell; stainless: treat as Cr(VI) — LEV, RPE, health surveillance.
Laser cells: access only with interlock sequence; beam off and verified before entry; service in Class 4 with LSO present, eyewear rated for wavelength, exclusion zone.
Robotic weld cells: see robot-cell procedure; tip dressing and spatter cleaning under LOTO.
Cooling water: check for leaks every shift; isolate power before fixing hoses near transformers; conductivity controlled per OEM.
Housekeeping: spatter and dust vacuumed (no compressed air); fume filters changed per DP with RPE and bagged as hazardous waste.
Health: pre-placement and periodic surveillance; pacemaker wearers kept away from RSW transformers (sign); notify occupational diseases (metal fume fever clusters, asthma).
ppe: Welding helmet/shade, leather gauntlets and apron, FR cotton clothing, safety glasses under helmet, FFP3 or PAPR where LEV inadequate, hearing protection, laser eyewear (maintenance)
stop: LEV not running or airflow below set point
Gun insulation damaged or water leaking on live parts
Laser interlock bypassed or cell entered with beam enabled
Welding on coated parts without extraction
Combustibles or sealers within spatter range
records: LEV examination (14-monthly benchmark), airflow checks, exposure monitoring, health surveillance, gun/cable inspections, laser safety records, hot-work permits, incident log

india: Factories Act s.14 (dust & fume), s.36A, s.87 via state rules / OSH Code s.6; Sch. II PELs (welding fume, Mn, Zn oxide, Cr(VI))
IS 818 (electric & gas welding safety), IS 3016 (fire precautions), IS 3103 (ventilation), IS 7194 (noise); IS 15298 PPE; HOWM Rules (fume filters)

intl: IARC Monograph 118 (welding fume Group 1); UK HSE WL3 & COSHH welding fume guidance (2019); EN ISO 15012 (fume extraction); IEC 60825-1/-4 (lasers); EN ISO 11611 (welder's clothing); ACGIH TLVs

t: EV Traction Batteries – Pack Assembly, HV Work, Storage & Charging
purpose: Prevent electric shock, arc flash, thermal runaway fires and chemical exposure when assembling, testing, servicing, storing, charging and transporting lithium-ion traction batteries and high-voltage vehicles.
scope: Cell and module handling, pack assembly and end-of-line testing, HV system work on vehicles (48 V–800 V DC), battery storage and quarantine, charging bays (AC Mode 3 / DC Mode 4), damaged or crashed vehicle handling, battery waste.
roles: HV competent persons (Level 2/3 trained per OEM/DGUV 200-005 benchmark — verify)
hazards: HV DC 400–800 V: shock, arc flash with no current zero; stored energy in capacitors and contactors; insulation faults on chassis
Thermal runaway from internal short, over-charge, mechanical damage or heat: 600–1,000 °C, toxic/flammable gases (HF, CO, H2, electrolyte vapours), jet flames, re-ignition hours to days later
Cell handling: external short by tools/jewellery, dropped modules (20–60 kg), busbar laser welding fume, electrolyte (LiPF6 → HF with moisture), NMP in electrode coating
Charging: cable/connector damage, DC leakage without Type B RCD, vehicle fire in enclosed parking; transport: UN 38.3 untested or damaged cells
pre: HV work only by trained and authorised persons; HV areas marked
Insulated tools to IEC 60900 (1,000 V), Class 0 insulating gloves (EN 60903) with leather over-gloves, face shield (arc-rated), insulated mats (IS 15652), CAT III/IV meter with proven test leads
Vehicle/pack de-energising procedure per OEM: service disconnect removed and locked
Wait capacitor discharge time (typically 5–10 min — verify), measure HV bus < 60 V DC and insulation resistance before touching orange cables
Pack assembly: ESD and short-circuit control — insulated workbenches, covered busbars, torque tools with insulated shafts, no metal watches/rings
Module lifting aids; thermal cameras and gas (CO/VOC/H2) detection in formation/EOL test areas
Storage: SoC 30–50% for storage; temperature 15–25 °C; segregated fire-compartment or outdoor containers per NFPA 855 benchmark
Damaged/defective/returned (DDR) cells quarantined outdoors ≥ 15 m from buildings (verify) in metal containers with vermiculite/sand; off-gas/smoke detection and water-based suppression
Charging bays: CEA 2023 EV charging provisions; EVSE to IS 17017 series; Type B RCD or 6 mA DC detection; emergency stop
Fire detection in enclosed parking; no charging of visibly damaged vehicles; extinguishers and vehicle-fire plan
steps: Before HV work: PTW (Electrical), vehicle on insulated stand, 12 V battery disconnected, service plug removed and locked in worker's possession
Wait discharge time, verify 0 V with meter proven on live source before and after, barrier the bay with 'HV work' sign.
Work on HV components with insulated tools and gloves; one hand where possible; never work on HV alone; second HV-trained person within sight with rescue hook and AED.
Re-energising: remove tools, check insulation resistance (IMD), close service plug, verify interlock loop, log.
Cell/module handling: inspect for dents, swelling, leakage, odour; reject and quarantine suspect cells immediately; carry modules with lifting aids; cover terminals during moves.
Formation/ageing and EOL testing: fixtures with rated contactors; thermal monitoring per channel; alarm → isolate channel, remove cell to quench tank/sand if safe, evacuate area if venting.

Crashed or damaged vehicles/packs: treat as thermal-runaway risk for 48 h — isolate outdoors, thermal camera every hour, no charging, inform OEM; transport as damaged Li-ion (UN 3480/3481 special provisions — verify).
Fire response: raise alarm, isolate charger/vehicle HV if safe, evacuate, call fire service with 'lithium-ion vehicle/pack' information
Cool with large volumes of water (thousands of litres) or submerge pack; expect re-ignition — monitor 24 h; do not use Class D agents (for lithium metal only).
Charging operations: visual check of cable/connector each use; RCD test monthly; keep bays clear of combustibles; smoke detection linked to alarm; weekly thermal scan of high-use chargers.
Battery waste: Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 — hand over to registered recycler/refurbisher via producer EPR; discharged and terminals insulated; manifests kept.
Training and drills: HV authorisation renewal every 2 years (verify), Li-ion fire drill 6-monthly with fire service, first aid for electrical injury and HF burns (calcium gluconate gel available).
ppe: Class 0 insulating gloves with over-gloves, arc-rated face shield, insulated footwear, FR clothing, safety glasses, chemical gloves for electrolyte, FFP3/PAPR for venting or fume
stop: HV bus not proven dead before contact
Working alone on HV
Swollen, hot, hissing or leaking cell in production or storage
Charger RCD fails test or cable damaged
DDR cells stored inside building
records: HV authorisations, PTW/isolation records, discharge/verification logs, cell inspection and quarantine register, thermal monitoring logs, charger RCD tests, fire drill reports, BWMR manifests

india: CEA Safety Regulations 2023 (EV charging; electrical installations); AIS-156 & AIS-038 Rev 2 (EV battery safety); IS 17855 (traction battery packs), IS 16893 (Li-ion traction cells — verify), IS 17017 (EVSE)
IS 16046 / IEC 62619; Battery Waste Management Rules 2022; Factories Act via state rules / OSH Code; IS 15652 (insulating mats)

tn: CEIG Tamil Nadu; TNFRS; TNPCB; TN EV Policy 2023 charging safety conditions (verify)

intl: ISO 6469-1/-3 (EV electrical safety), ECE R100 (Class B voltage 60–1,500 V DC), UN 38.3 & UN Model Regulations SP 376/377; IEC 62660, IEC 62485; DGUV Information 200-005 (HV qualification — verify); UK HSE EV guidance

t: Vehicle Test Tracks, Proving Grounds & Dynamometer Testing
purpose: Prevent collisions, rollovers, run-off and struck-by incidents during vehicle development and end-of-line testing on tracks, high-speed ovals, off-road courses and chassis dynamometers.
scope: OEM and component test tracks, end-of-line test strips and roller brake testers, ARAI/NATRAX-type proving grounds, durability and brake testing, autonomous/ADAS testing, chassis and engine dynamometer cells, test vehicles with prototype systems.
roles: Track controller (radio dispatch, single point of control)
Test drivers (licensed, medically fit, track-certified by level)
hazards: Loss of control at speed (prototype brakes/tyres), rollover in handling/stability tests, run-off into barriers; collision with slower vehicles, pedestrians or maintenance crews on track
Multiple vehicles on one circuit without separation; wrong-way entry; poor visibility (rain, fog, night, dust); animals on perimeter
Dynamometer cells: vehicle restraint failure, rotating rollers, exhaust CO, hot brakes/tyres bursting, fuel leaks on hot exhaust; EV HV systems
Fatigue on long durability shifts; heat in cabins without AC; fire in prototype vehicles (fuel, HV battery)
pre: Track rules booklet: speed limits per zone, direction, entry/exit protocol, radio procedure, right-of-way, maximum vehicles per circuit, weather limits (wet grip, visibility < 200 m — verify)
Displayed and signed by every driver
Driver certification tiers (e.g. up to 80 km/h; high-speed; handling/limit testing) with practical assessment, medical fitness, annual re-check; zero alcohol; mobile phones off while driving
Vehicles: pre-run check (tyres, brakes, fluid leaks, HV status), roll cage/5-point harness and helmet for limit-handling and rollover-risk tests; fire extinguisher; prototype systems' kill switches
Track infrastructure: run-off areas and barriers (tyre walls/guardrail), marshal posts or CCTV, radio coverage, lighting
Drainage, fencing against animals and intruders, separate access for maintenance vehicles with flashing beacons

Emergency: ambulance or trained paramedic on site during high-speed/limit tests, hospital tie-up, recovery vehicle, fire response for fuel and HV fires, HV rescue hooks; incident reporting to MV Act/OSH Code as applicable
steps: Daily track inspection by controller: surface debris, oil, water, barriers, signage, radio check; track status board set (open/closed/wet).
Driver and vehicle sign-in with controller; test plan declared (speed band, manoeuvres, zone); controller allocates slot and confirms maximum vehicles on circuit.
Entry/exit only at designated points on controller's clearance; acceleration lanes used; indicate and look before merging; no stopping on racing line — pull to shoulder and radio.
During test: driver keeps radio on and reports faults or anomalies; observers belted; no passengers during limit-handling or brake-fade tests unless role-essential and protected.
Limit-handling, J-turn, rollover-propensity and ADAS tests on dedicated dynamic pad with outriggers/safety vehicles; exclusion zone; no other traffic.
Maintenance or pedestrians on track only after controller closes the zone, barriers/cones placed, hi-vis and radios carried; vehicles re-admitted only when crew confirms clear.
Weather: suspend high-speed runs in heavy rain, standing water, fog, lightning or dust storms; night tests only with lighting and reflective markers.

Dynamometer cells: vehicle restrained per OEM (chains/straps rated), wheel chocks on non-driven axle, exhaust extraction connected, CO monitor, cooling fan, no one in cell during test, e-stop at console
HV vehicles with IMD monitoring.
Incident: controller stops all traffic (red flag/radio), dispatches rescue, isolates HV if EV, preserves scene, notifies as per statutory requirements; restart only after investigation clearance.
Fatigue: driving blocks ≤ 2 h with breaks on durability runs (verify against site policy), hydration, shift limits; audit driver hours.
ppe: Helmet (ECE/FIA rated) and harness for high-speed/limit tests, hi-vis vest for anyone on foot, fire-retardant suit for fuel-system or HV prototype tests, safety shoes, hearing protection in dyno cells
stop: Controller or radio not available
Driver not certified for the test tier or unfit
Vehicle fault affecting brakes, steering, tyres or HV isolation
Pedestrians or maintenance on track without zone closure
Weather or visibility below limits
records: Driver certifications and medicals, daily track inspection, vehicle pre-run checks, test plans and track logs, incident reports, maintenance records, emergency drills

india: Motor Vehicles Act 1988 & CMV Rules 1989 (Rule 126 test agencies — ARAI, ICAT, NATRAX, GARC; registration/trade certificates for test vehicles); OSH Code s.6 (duty of care
Non-factory premises as establishment); Factories Act via state rules where track is within factory; CEA 2023 (EV HV); AIS standards for testing
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (where within licensed premises); RTO Karnataka trade certificates
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950; RTO TN; GARC/Oragadam & Sriperumbudur OEM test tracks local emergency tie-ups
osha: General Duty Clause; 1910.178 (industrial trucks), 1910.147 (dyno maintenance), 1910.1000 (CO); NFPA 30A (motor fuel), SAE J2990
intl: ISO 3888 (lane change), ISO 4138 (steady-state circular), ISO 17387 (ADAS test methods)
FIA/FIM circuit safety guidance (barriers, run-off) as benchmark; UK HSE guidance on proving grounds (MIRA); ISO 39001 (road traffic safety management)

t: Ammonia Refrigeration Plants – Machinery Rooms, Oil Draining & Leak Response
purpose: Prevent ammonia releases, cold burns, asphyxiation and fire/explosion in refrigeration plants of dairies, cold stores, breweries, meat and seafood processors and ice plants.
scope: Machinery rooms (compressors, receivers, oil pots), condensers, evaporators in cold rooms and freezers, pump recirculation, hot-gas defrost, charging and oil draining, maintenance, decommissioning; 50 kg to several tonnes of NH3.
roles: Operators trained in oil draining and leak response (minimum two per shift)
ERT with SCBA and ammonia suits
hazards: NH3: TLV 25 ppm, STEL 35 ppm, IDLH 300 ppm; flammable 15–28% v/v in confined machinery rooms; dense cold cloud on release; corrosive to eyes/lungs; frostbite from liquid (−33 °C)
Oil draining: liquid ammonia blow-out when valve left open or trapped liquid; hydraulic shock in hot-gas defrost; over-pressure from trapped liquid between closed valves
Machinery-room asphyxia/panic; single exit; corrosion under insulation causing pipe failure; relief valves vented inside; forklift strikes on evaporator pipes in cold rooms
Charging/decanting from cylinders or tankers; hose failure; contaminated oil; fire in compressor room oils
pre: Design per IS 660 / IS 4544 / IIAR 2 and EN 378 benchmark: machinery room with two exits (doors outward, panic bars), emergency ventilation, NH3 detection (alarm 25 ppm
Emergency ventilation and shutdown at 150–200 ppm — verify per IIAR 2), emergency stop outside door, eyewash/shower at exit, lighting Ex where required
Relief valves vented outdoors to safe height, replaced every 5 years (IIAR 6 benchmark)
Pressure vessels (receivers) registered and tested under state Factories Rules / SMPV(U) Rules 2016 where applicable; pipe labelling (IIAR Bulletin 114 style: physical state, pressure, direction)
Oil-draining: self-closing (dead-man) oil drain valves, two persons, written procedure, PPE; oil pots isolated and pumped down; never leave an open ammonia drain
Emergency: SCBA (≥ 2 sets) and Type B gas suits stored outside machinery room, escape respirators for all in NH3 areas
Wind sock, assembly points upwind/crosswind, water fog for vapour knock-down (not on liquid pool), hospital tie-up
MSIHC thresholds checked (site notification/on-site plan if exceeded — verify quantity)
Evaporators in cold rooms protected by bollards; NH3 detectors in rooms with evaporators; cold-room procedures (see cold-room entry)
steps: Shift round: compressor oil levels and pressures, receiver level, detector readings, ventilation, PRV discharge lines
Pipe insulation (wet/stained = inspect for corrosion), unusual smell (NH3 odour threshold 5–50 ppm — any smell is a leak).

Oil draining: two trained persons, full-face respirator with K filter and gloves, dead-man valve, pot isolated and warmed, drain slowly into closed container, close and verify; never leave a drain open.

Pump-down and isolation for maintenance: evacuate section to flare/absorption, confirm pressure ≤ 0 bar g, never trap liquid between closed valves without relief; LOTO; hot work only after nitrogen purge and NH3 < 25 ppm.
Hot-gas defrost: follow OEM sequence to avoid hydraulic shock; investigate any banging in lines.
Charging: tanker/cylinder earthed, hose rated and within test date, excess-flow protection, operator in full PPE, second person at emergency stop; stop at design charge.
Minor leak (< 25 ppm alarm): approach upwind with SCBA, isolate at source, ventilate, repair under PTW; log and investigate root cause.
Major leak: toxic-gas alarm, evacuate crosswind/upwind, headcount, shelter-in-place for non-ERT; ERT in SCBA/gas suits isolates compressors and king valve
Water fog to knock down vapour; call fire service, inform District authorities if off-site impact; MSIHC 48-h report and dangerous-occurrence notice (12 h).
First aid: flush eyes/skin with water 15–20 min; remove contaminated clothing; frostbite — warm slowly; inhalation — fresh air, oxygen, hospital.
Integrity programme: IIAR 6 benchmark — annual inspection of vessels, piping, valves, relief, insulation; 5-yearly thickness survey; replace PRVs; test detectors quarterly; calibrate yearly.
Training: operators certified (refrigeration trade); annual refresher and leak drill; records; review after any leak.
ppe: Escape respirator for all in NH3 areas; full-face respirator with K filter for routine; SCBA and Type B gas suit for ERT; chemical goggles, cold-insulating and chemical gloves, face shield for oil draining
stop: Detector alarm active or smell of ammonia without known source
Only one trained person available for oil draining or charging
Machinery-room ventilation or detector out of service
SCBA/suits missing or out of test
PRV vent line blocked or vented indoors
records: Charge inventory, operator certificates, shift logs, oil-draining log, detector tests, PRV register, vessel test certificates, maintenance/inspection reports (IIAR 6), leak and drill reports, MSIHC documents where applicable

india: IS 660 (safety code for mechanical refrigeration), IS 4544 (code of safety for ammonia); Factories Act s.31 pressure plant & s.41B–H hazardous processes via state rules / OSH Code Ch. XII
SMPV(U) Rules 2016 (receivers > 1,000 L — verify); Gas Cylinders Rules 2016; MSIHC Rules (ammonia thresholds — verify); Sch. II PEL 25 ppm; IS 10592 (showers/eyewash)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (pressure plant rule; verify number); MAH Control (Karnataka) Rules 1994 if threshold exceeded; KSFES
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rule 61 pressure plant (verify); TN CIMAH Rules 1994; DISH TN; TNFRS
intl: EN 378-1 to -4 (refrigeration safety); ISO 5149; UK IOR Ammonia Refrigeration Safety Guide; EIGA; EU Seveso III (ammonia thresholds)

t: CIP Systems & Food-Plant Chemicals (Caustic, Acid, Peracetic, Hypochlorite)
purpose: Prevent chemical burns, toxic gas generation, scalds and entrapment during clean-in-place, manual cleaning and sanitiser handling in food, beverage, dairy and brewery plants.
scope: CIP sets (caustic 1–3% at 70–85 °C, nitric/phosphoric acid 0.5–1.5%, peracetic acid 0.1–0.3%, hypochlorite), bulk and IBC chemical storage, dosing systems, manual foam cleaning, bottle washers, membrane cleaning, chemical deliveries.
roles: CIP operators and sanitation crew (contract and own)
First aiders trained for chemical burns
hazards: Concentrated NaOH 30–50% and nitric acid 55–60%: severe burns, blindness; exothermic dilution; hot CIP solutions 80 °C scald

Mixing errors: acid + hypochlorite → chlorine gas; peracetic acid (strong oxidiser, organic peroxide UN 3109, pungent vapour, STEL 0.4 ppm) decomposes with heat/contamination; hypochlorite + ammonia → chloramines
Cross-connection: CIP solution routed to a tank or line a person is inside or that holds product; opening a manway/clamp on a line under CIP pressure
Slips on wet floors, foam; manual handling of 25–35 kg jerry cans; splashes while dipping sample cups; inadequate eyewash response
pre: Chemical inventory with SDS (IS 17859/GHS), segregation (acids away from caustic and hypochlorite
PAA in its own cool, vented store), bunding 110%, vented IBCs, labelled lines and valves; delivery couplings unique per chemical (different sizes/colours) to prevent wrong-tank filling
CIP sets with automated dosing, concentration and temperature control, interlocks: mix-proof valves or physical breaks between CIP and product routes
Tanks under CIP have 'CIP in progress' lock-out on manways; conductivity return verified
Emergency showers/eyewash within 10 s travel (ANSI Z358.1 / IS 10592) tested weekly, tempered water; spill kits with neutraliser; chlorine gas awareness in sanitation areas
PPE standard per task: chemical goggles + face shield, nitrile/neoprene gloves (gauntlet), chemical apron, boots; respirators for PAA/hypochlorite fogging
Training in local language with pictograms; written cleaning cards (chemical, concentration, temperature, time, PPE, never-mix list); contractors inducted to same standard
steps: Deliveries: driver and operator confirm chemical, tank, coupling and level; bund drains closed; PPE worn; stand by throughout; sample and seal.
Making up solutions: add concentrate to water, never water to concentrate; use dosing pumps; no decanting by hand from 200 L drums without pump; label every container.

Before starting CIP: confirm route, tank empty of people (visual plus sign-off), manways locked, hoses connected to correct ports, drains free; start sequence and verify return temperature/conductivity.
During CIP: no opening of clamps, sight glasses or manways; treat all lines as hot and chemical-filled; investigate leaks only after stopping and draining.
Manual foam cleaning: apply at low pressure away from electrical panels; one chemical at a time with rinse between acid and chlorine products; ventilate rooms; keep others out.
PAA/hypochlorite sanitising: measure concentration; ventilate; avoid heat and contamination; store PAA away from caustic, metals and organics; never return unused PAA to drum.
Entering tanks after CIP: confined-space permit, rinse verified, isolate CIP supply with blinds/locks, gas test (chlorine, O2), cool below 40 °C.
Spills: evacuate, PPE, contain, neutralise (dilute acid for caustic; soda ash for acid), dispose via ETP within consent limits; report.
First aid: flush with water ≥ 20 min, remove clothing, eyes held open under eyewash, go to hospital for alkali eye splashes; keep SDS for doctor.
Audit monthly: showers, bunds, labels, couplings, PPE condition, concentration logs; review near misses (wrong-coupling, splash) and update cleaning cards.
ppe: Chemical goggles and face shield, gauntlet nitrile/neoprene gloves, chemical apron or suit, safety gumboots, respirator (ABEK/P3) for PAA or chlorine fogging
stop: Person inside tank or line not positively confirmed empty before CIP
Delivery coupling does not match tank or label missing
Shower/eyewash not working within 10 s travel
Mixing acid and chlorine products in same area/sequence
Opening equipment under CIP pressure or temperature
records: Chemical inventory and SDS, delivery and dosing logs, CIP cycle records (conc./temp.), shower/eyewash tests, PPE issue, training (language), spill and first-aid log, ETP discharge records

india: Factories Act s.41B/41C (hazardous substances information), s.36/36A via state rules / OSH Code s.6, s.11; MSIHC Rule 17 SDS
IS 17859 (GHS/SDS), IS 10592 (showers/eyewash), IS 4209 (chemical plant safety); FSSAI Schedule 4 (cleaning chemical control); Water Act consent for effluent; HOWM Rules

tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 (Rule 95 schedules; washing facilities Rule 42 — verify); TNPCB
osha: 1910.1200 HazCom, 1910.151(c) eyewash, 1910.132–138 PPE, 1910.146, 1910.1000 (chlorine ceiling 1 ppm); ANSI/ISEA Z358.1
intl: EHEDG hygienic design & CIP guidance; UK HSE Food Information Sheets (chemical burns, CIP); COSHH; EN ISO 374 (chemical gloves); EN 166 (eye protection)

t: Silos, Hoppers & Bulk Bins – Engulfment Prevention, Entry & Dust Explosion
purpose: Prevent engulfment, asphyxiation, falls and dust explosions in silos, flat stores, hoppers and bins holding grain, flour, sugar, feed, cement, fly ash and other bulk solids.
scope: Steel and concrete silos, hopper-bottom bins, flat storage with sweep augers, feed bins, cement/fly-ash silos, bucket elevators and conveyors feeding them; clearing of bridged or caked material; cleaning and inspection entries.
roles: Entry supervisor, attendant and entrants (confined-space trained)
hazards: Engulfment: flowing grain buries a person knee-deep in 4–5 s and fully in 20–30 s; bridged crust collapses; vertical wall avalanche; > 300 kg force needed to pull a buried person — recovery becomes a body recovery
Atmosphere: O2 depletion and CO2 from grain respiration/spoilage, CO from smouldering, phosphine from fumigation, dust > PEL; heat
Dust explosion in bucket elevators, dust collectors and silo headspace (flour/sugar/starch St 1; MIE 10–30 mJ); ignition from bearings, belt slip, static, hot work
Falls from silo roofs and internal ladders; moving augers/sweeps; roof collapse from vacuum/over-pressure; bin structural failure from off-centre discharge
pre: Zero-entry policy: design out entry with external poles, air cannons, vibrators, bin whips and cameras; entry only when no alternative and under permit
Permit-required confined-space programme: isolation and LOTO of all feed and discharge equipment (augers, sweeps, pneumatic lines, elevators)
Bridging/caking assessment, atmosphere testing (O2 19.5–23.5%, CO < 25 ppm, LEL < 10%, dust, PH3 < 0.3 ppm), continuous ventilation

Entrant on full-body harness with lifeline attached to a rated anchor and mechanical retrieval (winch/tripod) controlled by attendant; never attached to equipment; second lifeline where sweep auger present
Dust explosion controls: Dust Hazard Analysis (NFPA 652/61), explosion vents on elevators and collectors, bearing-temperature and belt-alignment switches
Magnets before mills, Ex-rated electricals in Zone 20/21/22, housekeeping limit, hot-work permit system
Roof access: fixed ladders with cages/fall-arrest rail, guardrails or anchor points at roof hatches, no walking on grain surface; weather limits; signage 'Engulfment hazard — no entry without permit'
steps: Try every non-entry method first: run discharge, use poles/air lances from outside hatch with harness tied off, use bin whip; schedule entry only if these fail.

Pre-entry: LOTO all equipment that moves material (verify by attempted start), check for bridging or wall build-up with camera/light from hatch; if material is caked above entrant's level — no entry; plan removal from above.
Test atmosphere from outside at several depths; ventilate; continue monitoring during entry; check fumigation records and PH3 reading before any entry to a treated bin.

Entrant in harness with lifeline on retrieval device; attendant in constant contact; no entry below the level of hanging material; never walk on grain to break crusts; use platform/boards from above where possible.
Work from the top down when clearing walls; keep lifeline taut; stop and exit if material starts to flow or shift.
Rescue plan: on-site team can reach and begin retrieval within minutes; grain rescue tube/cofferdam and vacuum where available; never jump in after a victim; call fire service with silo details.
Elevator/conveyor operation: respond to bearing and belt alarms; keep covers closed; clean dust layers daily; no compressed-air blow-down near ignition sources.
Hot work on silos, elevators or ducts: shut down and empty, clean to bare metal around the work, wet or inert, gas/dust test, fire watch 60 min; permit.
Inspection: annual structural inspection of silo walls, roofs, hoppers and anchors; explosion vents and sensors tested; records.
Training and drills: engulfment awareness for all, entry team competence yearly, rescue drill yearly with local fire service.
ppe: Full-body harness with retrieval lifeline, FFP3 dust respirator (or SCBA/airline where atmosphere not proven), goggles, helmet with chin strap, gloves, antistatic clothing, personal 4-gas monitor
stop: Feed/discharge not isolated and locked
Entrant without lifeline on retrieval device or attendant absent
Material bridged or caked above entrant level
Atmosphere outside limits or fumigant present
Hot work without emptying, cleaning and permit
records: Confined-space entry permits, isolation/LOTO records, gas-test logs, rescue plan and drill records, DHA and explosion-protection maintenance, bearing/belt alarm logs, structural inspections, fumigation records

Dust-codes (NFPA 652/61 as benchmark); FCI/CWC storage guidelines for bag/bulk stacks; Insecticides Act 1968 (fumigation operators)

t: Bakery & Hot-Process Food Lines – Gas Ovens, Fryers, Mixers & Hot Surfaces
purpose: Prevent burns, gas explosions, fires, entanglement and flour-dust asthma in bakeries, biscuit and snack plants, confectionery and frying lines.
scope: Deck, rack and tunnel ovens (LPG/PNG/electric), proofers, fryers (hot oil 170–190 °C), kettles and jacketed pans, spiral and planetary mixers, dividers, moulders, slicers, depositors, flour silos and sifters, cooling conveyors, packaging.
hazards: Gas: leaks and explosion on light-off without purge; flame failure; CO from poor combustion; LPG cylinder/bulk and PNG supply faults
Burns from oven surfaces > 200 °C, trays, steam injection, hot oil splash and fryer fires (Class F); scalds from kettles; thermal-fluid leaks
Entanglement in mixers (bowl/agitator), dividers, moulders, slicer blades, depositors; hands in conveyors; manual cleaning of running machines
Flour dust: baker's asthma (flour dust TLV 0.5 mg/m³ inhalable, ACGIH), explosion in silos/sifters; heat stress near ovens; slips on flour/oil; night shifts and fatigue
pre: Gas installation to IS 6044 (LPG) / PNGRB T4S (PNG): isolation valve at entry, double block-and-bleed and pressure switches on burners
Flame-failure devices, pre-purge ≥ 4 volume changes (NFPA 86 benchmark), gas detectors with auto shut-off in oven rooms and cylinder stores, CO detection

Fryers: high-temperature limit cut-out independent of thermostat, lid or fixed suppression (wet-chemical/Class F), oil-level interlocks, no water near fryer; kitchen-style exhaust hoods cleaned per schedule (grease fire)
Mixers and machines: interlocked bowl guards and covers (no run with guard open), e-stops, LOTO for cleaning; slicers with blade guards and push sticks; young persons excluded from dangerous machines

Flour dust: enclosed transfer, LEV at tipping/sifting, vacuum cleaning, no compressed air; silo/sifter dust-explosion controls; health surveillance questionnaire and lung function yearly for flour-exposed staff
Heat: oven-room ventilation, WBGT monitoring, water and rest breaks; burns first aid (cool running water 20 min, cling film, burn dressings) in every area
steps: Oven start-up: verify gas pressure, purge complete, ignition by sequence; never light manually with a flame; stop and ventilate on any gas smell; report flame-failure trips.
Loading/unloading ovens: heat-resistant gauntlets and sleeves, trolleys locked, clear path; steam-injection ovens opened from the side after venting.
Fryers: heat slowly, keep oil below max line, no wet product/ice into oil, skim from the side; fire — cover/suppression, isolate heat, never use water; cool below 50 °C before draining/cleaning.
Mixers and dividers: stop and isolate before scraping, adding by hand or clearing jams; test interlocks at start of shift; keep hair covered and no loose sleeves.
Slicers/cutters: blade guard in place, push stick, cut-resistant gloves for blade changes under LOTO.
Flour handling: tip under LEV, minimise dust clouds, wet-wipe or vacuum surfaces; sifters sealed; check silo controls; report chest tightness or rhinitis to OHC.
Cleaning: machines isolated and locked; hot-surface warning; non-slip footwear; chemicals per cleaning cards (see CIP/chemical procedure).
Gas cylinders/bulk: stored outdoors, upright, segregated; changeover by trained person with leak test; regulators and hoses within date.
Night/early shifts: minimum two persons; fatigue management; welfare; women's night-work conditions per state rules.
Maintenance: annual burner and safety-device service by licensed gas fitter; thermal-fluid systems inspected; exhaust duct cleaning records.
ppe: Heat-resistant gauntlets and sleeves, face shield at fryers, FFP2 for flour tipping, non-slip safety shoes, hairnet, cut-resistant gloves for blade work, apron
stop: Gas smell or detector alarm
Flame-failure or purge bypassed
Interlocked guard open with machine running
Fryer high-limit or suppression not functional
Flour LEV not running during tipping
records: Gas installation certificates and annual service, detector tests, oven/fryer safety-device checks, interlock tests, LEV checks, health surveillance (asthma), burn/first-aid log, cleaning and LOTO records

india: Factories Act ss.21–23 (fencing, young persons), s.14 (dust), s.13 (temperature), s.38 (fire) via state rules / OSH Code
Gas Cylinders Rules 2016 & IS 6044 Pt 1–2 (LPG installations); PNGRB T4S (PNG); IS 9474 (guarding); FSSAI Schedule 4; IS 2190 (extinguishers, Class F); Sch. II dust limits
