t: Bottling & Packaging Lines – Conveyors, Fillers, Glass & CO2
purpose: Prevent entanglement, crush, cuts from glass, CO2 asphyxiation, caustic burns, noise damage and slips on high-speed bottling, canning and packaging lines.
scope: Depalletisers, rinsers, fillers/cappers, pasteurisers, labellers, case packers, palletisers and stretch wrappers; conveyor systems; bottle washers (returnable glass); carbonation and CO2 storage; PET blow moulders; CIP of fillers.
hazards: Conveyor nip points, star wheels, infeed screws, transfer plates, palletiser hoists and cells; reaching in to clear jams on running lines (most common injury)
Glass: bottle bursts at filler/capper (2–4 bar carbonation), shards on conveyors, bottle-washer breakages; eye and hand lacerations
CO2: bulk tank and carbonators — leaks in enclosed rooms (TLV 5,000 ppm; STEL 30,000 ppm; IDLH 40,000 ppm), odourless; dry-ice; cold burns
Bottle washer caustic 2–3% at 60–80 °C; pasteuriser heat; noise 85–95 dB(A); slips on wet floors; manual handling of cases; PET blow-moulder hot moulds and high-pressure air (40 bar)
pre: Machines guarded to EN 415 benchmark: interlocked guards with guard locking where run-down > 1 s, e-stops every 10–15 m along conveyors, pull-wires, perimeter guarding on palletiser/depalletiser cells with presence sensing
Written jam-clearing procedure per machine: stop, isolate (or use inching/control-reliable hold-to-run with guards), clear with tools, restart; 'no hands in a running machine' rule
CO2: detectors with alarms at 5,000 ppm (action) and 15,000–30,000 ppm (evacuate) in carbonation rooms, cellars and tank enclosures
Ventilation; tank per SMPV(U) Rules 2016 (> 1,000 L) with PESO licence (verify); PRVs vented outdoors

Glass: polycarbonate guards at filler/capper, face shields in glass zones, cut-resistant gloves (EN 388 level C+), broken-glass procedure (stop, clear zone, brush/tongs, bin for sharps); eye-protection zones marked
Noise: hearing-conservation zones (≥ 85 dB(A)), audiometry yearly; anti-slip flooring and drainage; drip trays; chain-lube control
steps: Shift start: test e-stops and interlocks on each machine, check guards, CO2 detector status, floor condition, lighting; log.
Normal running: never reach over, under or through guards; remove fallen bottles with tools from outside; keep hair, lanyards and loose clothing secured.
Jam or fault: press stop, wait for run-down, open interlocked guard, clear with tool; if guard must be open with motion — only trained person using hold-to-run at reduced speed per machine procedure.
Glass breakage at filler: stop, purge affected containers (count per procedure), remove shards with tongs/brush, check conveyors downstream; never use bare hands; log breakage rate.
Palletiser/depalletiser cells: enter only via interlocked gate with key in pocket; see robot-cell procedure for hoist/stored-energy isolation.
Bottle washer: caustic handling PPE, lid interlocks, steam/hot-water isolation before entry for cleaning; confined-space permit for tanks.
CO2 handling: tanker fill by trained operator with PPE; never enter a CO2 alarm area without SCBA; dry ice only in ventilated areas; cold-protective gloves.
PET blow moulders: isolate high-pressure air and heaters; wait for mould cool-down; guard interlocks tested.
Changeovers and maintenance: LOTO at machine isolator; verify zero energy (air, electrical, gravity on palletiser hoists); test guards before handing back.
Noise and ergonomics: hearing protection in zones; rotate manual-case-handling roles; lifting aids; report MSD symptoms.
ppe: Safety glasses (face shield in glass zones), cut-resistant gloves, hearing protection, non-slip safety shoes, hairnet, caustic PPE at washer, cold gloves for CO2/dry ice
stop: Interlock or e-stop defeated or failed test
Hands in running machine / jam cleared without stopping
CO2 detector alarm or detector out of service
Caustic or hot-water line not isolated before entry
Glass breakage zone not cleared before restart
records: Interlock/e-stop test log, jam-clearing training and authorisations, CO2 detector calibration, SMPV licence and PRV tests, glass-breakage log, noise surveys and audiometry, LOTO records, injury and near-miss log

Gas Cylinders Rules 2016; Sch. II (CO2 5,000 ppm; noise 90 dB(A)); IS 7194 (noise); FSSAI Sch. 4; IS 15298 footwear

tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 (Rule 53 schedules; noise); DISH TN; PESO Chennai

t: Cold Rooms, Blast Freezers & Controlled-Atmosphere Stores – Entrapment & Cold Stress
purpose: Prevent entrapment, hypothermia, asphyxiation in controlled-atmosphere stores, ammonia exposure and forklift incidents in chillers (0–5 °C), freezers (−18 to −30 °C), blast freezers (−40 °C) and CA fruit stores.
scope: Cold stores and dark stores, blast and spiral freezers, ripening and CA rooms (O2 1–3%, CO2 up to 5%), refrigerated containers and reefer trucks, ice plants; work inside by pickers, forklift operators, hygiene and maintenance staff.
hazards: Entrapment: door latch frozen, interior release missing or frozen, lights off, phone no signal; hypothermia within hours at −25 °C; blast-freezer air flow (wind chill −60 °C)
CA/ripening rooms: oxygen 1–3% kills in seconds; CO2; ethylene (flammable) in ripening rooms; nitrogen generators; entering to retrieve fruit or a fallen colleague
Cold stress: frostbite (fingers, ears), reduced dexterity, slips on ice, fogged visors; dehydration; cardiovascular strain
Forklifts in freezers: fogging, icy floors, battery capacity drop, reduced visibility in fog at doors; rack collapse with frozen loads; ammonia or CO2 evaporators in rooms; falling frozen product
pre: Every cold room door openable from inside at all times, even when locked from outside — luminous internal release handle, tested weekly and kept ice-free
Trapped-person alarm (battery backed, audible outside and to control room) inside; axe/emergency light; door heaters working

CA rooms: locked, placarded 'Low oxygen — do not enter'; entry only after ventilation to O2 > 19.5% confirmed by calibrated meter; two persons; O2 alarm; ethylene detection and Ex equipment in ripening rooms
Cold-stress plan: work/warm-up schedule (e.g. −25 °C: 50 min work / 10 min warm-up
Below −30 °C shorter — verify against ACGIH table), heated rest room, warm drinks, medical fitness (circulatory conditions), buddy system, no lone working inside freezers
PPE: freezer suits (EN 342), insulated gloves with liners, thermal boots (EN ISO 20345 CI), balaclava, anti-fog goggles; forklift cabs heated where possible

Forklifts: cold-rated hydraulics and batteries, lights, cameras; floor ice management; racking inspected for frozen-load damage; refrigerant (NH3/CO2) detectors in rooms with evaporators linked to alarm
steps: Entry: sign in on door board/headcount system, carry radio or alarm pendant, check internal release works before door closes behind you; report any frozen handle immediately.
Work inside within scheduled durations; leave at first signs of shivering, numbness or confusion; buddy checks every 20–30 min in freezers.
Forklift work: speed ≤ 5 km/h inside rooms, horn at doors, lights on; stop in fog; de-ice floors; never stack above rack SWL; report damaged racking.
Blast freezers: isolate fans before entry; interlocked door; never enter while air blast running; product on trolleys secured.
CA/ripening rooms: no entry without permit, ventilation record and O2 reading at door and inside; never enter to rescue without SCBA — raise alarm; keep room locked during storage period.
Hygiene and defrost cleaning: isolate evaporator fans, PTW for work at height, hot water/steam scald control, chemicals per cleaning cards.
Reefer containers/trucks: chock and lock before entry, door held open with stop, internal release checked, never close with person inside; genset exhaust away from doors.
Refrigerant alarm inside room: leave immediately, close door, report; re-entry only after plant operator clears.
Emergency (person missing): check headcount, search all rooms including CA with SCBA team, call ERT; frostbite — warm slowly, no rubbing; hypothermia — insulate, warm drinks if conscious, hospital.
Weekly tests: internal releases, alarms, emergency lights, door heaters, O2 meters; monthly ice/floor audit; records.
ppe: Freezer suit (EN 342), insulated gloves with liners, thermal safety boots, balaclava/hood, anti-fog goggles, alarm pendant/radio; SCBA for CA-room rescue
stop: Internal door release or trapped-person alarm not working
Lone working inside freezer or CA room
CA room O2 < 19.5% at entry
Forklift without lights/cameras in foggy room or icy floor uncleared
Refrigerant detector alarm in room
records: Door-release and alarm test log, headcount/sign-in records, work/warm-up schedule, cold-stress fitness, O2 readings for CA entries, forklift and racking inspections, refrigerant detector tests, incident log

IS 4544 (ammonia); Shops & Establishments Acts for dark stores; FSSAI cold-chain guidelines; Sch. II (CO2)

t: Solvent Recovery, Flammable Solvent Storage & Dispensing
purpose: Prevent fire, explosion and toxic exposure in solvent recovery (distillation), bulk and drum storage, dispensing and spent-solvent handling in API, formulation, agrochemical and speciality chemical plants.
scope: Methanol, acetone, toluene, IPA, ethyl acetate, THF, DCM, hexane and mixed spent solvents; recovery columns and receivers; tank farms and day tanks; drum stores; dispensing booths; solvent transfer by pump, vacuum and nitrogen; waste solvent.
hazards: Class A petroleum (flash point < 23 °C): vapours heavier than air travel to ignition sources; static from splash filling, non-conductive hoses/liners, people; non-Ex lighting, phones, forklifts
Column upsets: loss of cooling → over-pressure; vacuum leaks admitting air into hot vapour; peroxide formation in THF/ether/dioxane and detonation on distillation to dryness
Toxicity: methanol (blindness), DCM (CO formation, carcinogen), hexane (neuropathy), toluene (CNS); oxygen deficiency from nitrogen in confined receivers
Drum handling: bulging drums, pressure on opening, spills, falls from racks; hot work on 'empty' drums; waste solvent mixing (incompatibles, peroxides)
pre: Petroleum Rules 2002 licence for Class A/B storage beyond exemption; layout and separation distances per Rules and OISD-118 benchmark
Dyke 110%; tank venting with flame arresters, nitrogen blanketing or conservation vents; day-tank quantities limited to shift needs

Hazardous-area classification (IS 5572 / IEC 60079-10-1) with drawings; Ex-rated electricals, forklifts and tools; IS/IEC 60079-17 inspections; LEL detection in recovery and storage areas (alarm 20% LEL, trip 40% — verify)
Static control per IS 7689 / NFPA 77 / IEC TS 60079-32-1: bonding and earthing of tanks, drums, pumps, hoses (conductive)
Dip-pipe or bottom filling, initial flow ≤ 1 m/s, relaxation time, conductive footwear and flooring, no plastic liners/scoops with Class A
Process: HAZOP of recovery system; interlocks on cooling water, reflux temperature, vacuum and receiver level
Relief sized for fire and runaway cases to scrubber/safe location; peroxide testing before distilling peroxide-formers (discard > 100 ppm — verify); never distil to dryness
Fire: foam (alcohol-resistant) hydrants/monitors, deluge on tank farm, CO2/DCP extinguishers at 15 m, no smoking zone 30 m, emergency isolation valves remote from tanks
Spill kits; solvent-rated ventilation in dispensing booths (face velocity ≈ 0.5 m/s)
steps: Receipt: check tanker earthing and bonding before hose connection; sample and verify material; unload with pump within flow limits; stand by throughout; record quantity against licence limit.
Dispensing: in booth with LEV running, drum earthed and bonded to receiving vessel, Ex pump, closed transfer; no open pouring of Class A; label containers; return drums capped.
Recovery start-up: verify cooling water, vacuum integrity, receiver earth, nitrogen purge; charge within batch limits; monitor column temperatures and pressure; respond to alarms per SOP.
Peroxide-formers: test before every distillation; never heat residues to dryness; discard dated containers; store THF/ether in dark, dated, inhibitor-checked.
Shutdown/maintenance: pump out, nitrogen purge, gas-free verification (< 10% LEL and O2 20.9% for entry), LOTO, PTW with hot-work controls; blind flanges on live solvent lines.
Hot work anywhere in solvent area: process stopped or isolated, drains covered, gas test at work location and dyke, fire watch 60 min after
No hot work on drums or tanks that held solvent without cleaning and gas-free certificate.
Spills: stop source, eliminate ignition, absorb with inert material, ventilate, dispose as hazardous waste; vapour > 20% LEL → evacuate area, call ERT.

Waste solvent: segregated by compatibility, labelled, earthed collection drums, stored ≤ 90 days (HOWM) and sent to authorised recycler/co-processing with manifest; no mixing of oxidisers, acids or peroxide-formers.
Health: solvent exposure monitoring (methanol 200 ppm, toluene 20 ppm, DCM 50 ppm ACGIH — verify), biological monitoring where used, annual medical; first aid for splashes and inhalation.
Audit quarterly: licence compliance (quantities, drawings), Ex register, earthing resistance tests, LEL detectors, foam stocks, drills; MoC for any solvent or equipment change.
ppe: Antistatic FR coveralls (EN 1149/ISO 11612), conductive safety shoes, chemical goggles/face shield, solvent-resistant gloves (butyl/nitrile per SDS), respirator with A2 filter for dispensing, escape set in recovery plant
stop: Earthing/bonding not verified before transfer
Non-Ex equipment or phone in Zone 1/2
LEL > 20% or detector out of service
Peroxide test not done for THF/ether/dioxane
Hot work in solvent area without gas test and isolation
records: PESO licence and approved drawings, stock registers, Ex inspection register, earthing test records, LEL detector calibration, HAZOP and MoC, PTW/gas-test records, HW manifests, exposure monitoring, drill reports

Rule 17 SDS); IS 5572, IS/IEC 60079-14/-17; IS 7689 (static); IS 11457 Pt 1 (fire safety of chemical plants); IS 15325 (foam); HOWM Rules 2016; Sch. II PELs

t: Potent Compound (OEB 4/5) Containment & Occupational Exposure Control
purpose: Protect workers from highly potent APIs (hormones, cytotoxics, immunosuppressants, high-potency peptides) with occupational exposure limits below 10 µg/m³, and prevent cross-contamination of products.
scope: Dispensing, granulation, milling, compression, coating, filling and packing of OEB 4 (1–10 µg/m³) and OEB 5 (< 1 µg/m³) materials; isolators and RABS; sampling and QC labs; cleaning, maintenance, waste; gowning and de-gowning.
hazards: Inhalation and skin absorption of dusts/aerosols at µg levels: hormonal effects, reproductive toxicity, carcinogenicity, sensitisation; effects may be irreversible and delayed

Containment breaches: torn isolator gloves, open split-butterfly valves, bag changes, spills during dispensing, dust on gowns carried to canteen; positive-pressure cleanroom pushing contaminated air into corridors
De-gowning is the highest-exposure step; respirator fit failure (beards); cross-contamination of other products (regulatory and patient risk)
Waste and effluent: cytotoxic residues in wash water, HEPA filters, cleaning cloths; maintenance on contaminated equipment without decontamination
pre: Occupational Exposure Banding by toxicologist; OEL/ADE set per compound; containment strategy selected from band (OEB 4: closed handling, local containment, RPE as backup; OEB 5: isolators, closed transfer, no open handling)

Engineering: isolators at −30 to −50 Pa (verify) with H14 HEPA on exhaust, glove-port integrity testing per campaign, split-butterfly valves or continuous liners for transfers, closed milling/granulation, wash-in-place
Dedicated or campaign facilities per Schedule M (beta-lactams, hormones, cytotoxics)
Containment verification by surrogate testing (ISPE SMEPAC: lactose/naproxen/mannitol) at installation and after modification; routine air and surface monitoring against OEL; results trended
Gowning: dedicated gowning/de-gowning airlocks with pressure cascade (negative to corridor for potent suites)
Disposable coveralls (Type 5/6), double gloves, PAPR (APF 1,000 — verify) or supplied-air hoods for OEB 5 interventions
Fit testing yearly; no beards with tight-fitting masks

Medical: pre-placement and periodic surveillance; women of child-bearing age and pregnant workers counselled/relocated for hormone and cytotoxic exposure per policy; exposure records retained 30–40 years
steps: Before entering suite: check pressure differentials, isolator alarms, glove inspection log; gown per pictorial SOP; buddy check of PAPR flow and seals.
Dispensing/charging: through isolator or split-butterfly valve only; liners and bags tied and cut inside containment; no open scoops; vacuum any visible dust immediately with HEPA vacuum.
Interventions (jams, sampling): plan with supervisor, use glove ports/half-suits; if containment must be opened — PAPR/supplied air, local extraction, minimum persons, decontaminate before closing.
Glove-port breach: stop, withdraw hand slowly, change outer glove, replace port glove per SOP, record as containment incident; monitor exposure.
Cleaning: wet methods only (no dry sweeping/compressed air); cleaning agents validated to deactivate compound where possible; cloths and PPE bagged as hazardous waste inside suite.
De-gowning: slowest step — remove outer gloves and coverall rolling inside-out in airlock, respirator last, shower where OEB 5; dispose into sealed bins; wash hands and face.
Maintenance: equipment decontaminated and swab-verified before release; BIBO (bag-in/bag-out) HEPA changes by trained team in PAPR; filters double-bagged for incineration.
Waste and effluent: segregated potent waste to incinerator (HOWM/BMW rules as applicable); wash water to dedicated treatment/detoxification before ETP; no release untreated.
Monitoring: personal air sampling per campaign; surface wipes on exit side of airlocks and canteen door handles as spread indicators; investigate any result > 10% of OEL (verify trigger).
Review: containment incidents, monitoring trends, medical findings and SMEPAC results reviewed quarterly; re-test after any change (MoC).
ppe: Disposable Type 5/6 coveralls, double nitrile gloves taped, PAPR with P3/HEPA or supplied-air hood, goggles (if not hooded), dedicated footwear/overshoes; never reuse disposable PPE
stop: Isolator pressure or HEPA alarm active
Glove-port or liner breach not managed per SOP
Open handling of OEB 5 material
PAPR not fit-tested/flow-checked for the user
Pressure cascade reversed (suite positive to corridor)
records: OEB/OEL assessments, containment verification (SMEPAC) reports, air and surface monitoring, glove integrity logs, fit-test records, medical surveillance (long retention), containment incident log, waste manifests, MoC

MSIHC Rule 17; IS 17859 (GHS); HOWM Rules 2016 & BMW Rules 2016 (cytotoxic waste); Third Schedule notifiable diseases; Sch. II PELs (where listed)

t: Clean Rooms & Pharma HVAC – AHU Work, HEPA Changes, Fumigation & Gas Suppression
purpose: Prevent injuries and exposures in clean-room suites and their HVAC/utility systems: falls from AHU platforms, entrapment by interlocked doors, fumigant/decontaminant exposure, gaseous fire-suppression discharge, UV and nitrogen hazards.
scope: Grade A–D pharma cleanrooms and ISO 5–8 electronics cleanrooms; AHUs, HEPA/ULPA filters, ducts, plenums and interstitial spaces; VHP/formaldehyde fumigation; clean-agent and CO2 suppression rooms; laminar airflow units, isolators, autoclaves, depyrogenation tunnels, lyophilisers.
hazards: AHU work: fan start-up during filter change, belt/pulley nip points, electric heaters, falls from AHU roofs and service platforms, ladders in plant rooms, noise

Interlocked airlocks trapping persons during fire/evacuation if fail-locked; disorientation in smoke in windowless rooms; gaseous suppression (CO2 lethal; inert gas/Novec oxygen reduction) discharging with people inside
Fumigation: VHP (H2O2 35% liquid corrosive; vapour TLV 1 ppm), formaldehyde (IARC Group 1; TLV 0.1 ppm) — leaks to adjacent rooms, re-entry before aeration; sporicides (PAA/hypochlorite)
Hot/cold utilities: autoclave steam, depyrogenation tunnels 300 °C, lyophiliser nitrogen/vacuum, LN2
UV-C lamps in LAF/pass-boxes (eye and skin burns); slips on polished epoxy floors; gowning heat stress; IPA 70% bulk (flammable)
pre: HVAC work under PTW: AHU isolated (LOTO) at starter plus local isolator; fans proved stopped
Duct dampers closed/locked where others feed the system; filter changes with FFP3/PAPR and bagging (BIBO for potent or biological areas)
Platforms, guardrails and fixed access for AHUs and rooftop units; fall-arrest anchors where guardrails impossible; ladders secured; lighting in plant rooms; permit for roof work

Door interlocks fail-safe: fire alarm or power loss releases interlocks for egress; manual override at every door; emergency exit signage visible in cleanroom; evacuation drill includes gowned staff (no de-gowning in a fire)
Gaseous suppression: pre-discharge alarm and time delay (≥ 30 s), abort switch, manual isolation (lock-off) before anyone enters protected enclosure for maintenance
CO2 systems in occupiable rooms replaced or strictly interlocked (NFPA 12); O2 monitoring where inert gas stored
Fumigation: written plan, room sealed and placarded, adjacent-area checks, HVAC isolation/recirculation set
Continuous monitoring with calibrated sensors, re-entry only after aeration to < 1 ppm H2O2 or < 0.1 ppm HCHO (verify), trained operators in PPE
Formaldehyde phased out where possible
steps: Daily: check pressure differentials, alarms, door-interlock override function, suppression panel status (no unexplained isolations), UV lamp interlocks.
Before AHU/filter work: PTW, LOTO at panel and local isolator, test start, close dampers, allow fan run-down; wear FFP3/PAPR for used filters; bag and label filters; test platform guardrails.
HEPA change on terminal housings: work from stable platform/scaffold, two persons, no leaning over equipment; validate (DOP/PAO) after change — test aerosol handled per SDS.
Duct/plenum entry: treat as confined space — isolate fans, test atmosphere, attendant, lighting; no entry to live interstitial spaces without permit.
Fumigation (VHP): seal room, post warnings, lock doors with key control, start cycle, monitor leaks at doors with handheld sensor
After cycle aerate and verify concentration at head height in several points before unlocking; log.

Gas-suppression rooms: before maintenance inside, isolate release (panel + mechanical lock-off), hang tag, restore after exit; never defeat abort or delay; if pre-discharge alarm sounds — leave immediately, close door.

Autoclaves/tunnels/lyophilisers: operate per pressure-vessel rules (autoclave is a pressure vessel), door interlocks, let cool before unloading, heat-resistant gloves; nitrogen areas with O2 monitors (< 19.5% alarm).
UV-C: switch off before opening LAF/pass-box; interlocks tested; eye protection if servicing lit lamps.
Cleaning and disinfectants: 70% IPA bulk stored per Petroleum Rules; sporicides per cleaning cards with PPE and ventilation; slip control (dry floors, footwear).
Emergency: evacuate gowned, follow lit exit signs, assembly headcount by room; fire service told about suppression gases, fumigation in progress and LN2/solvent storage.
ppe: Cleanroom garments plus task PPE over them: FFP3/PAPR for filter changes, chemical goggles and gloves for disinfectants/H2O2
Heat-resistant gloves for autoclaves, harness for AHU roofs, hearing protection in plant rooms, UV face shield when servicing
stop: AHU not isolated/verified before filter or belt work
Door interlock does not release on alarm/override test
Gas-suppression release not isolated before entry for maintenance
Fumigation re-entry without concentration verification
Fall protection missing at AHU/roof platforms
records: PTW and LOTO records, HEPA change and validation reports, fumigation logs (concentration, aeration), suppression isolation log
Interlock and override tests, O2/VHP sensor calibration, evacuation drill reports, confined-space permits

NFPA 2001 / NFPA 12 as gaseous-suppression benchmark; Petroleum Rules (IPA storage); Sch. II (formaldehyde, H2O2 — verify); BMW/HOWM Rules for filters and chemicals

tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 (Rule 61 pressure vessels — autoclaves; verify); TNFRS; TNPCB

t: Reactor Charging, Inerting & Reactive Chemistry Control
purpose: Prevent flash fires, explosions, runaway reactions and exposures during manual and closed charging of powders and liquids into reactors containing flammable solvents, and during reaction, sampling and discharge.
scope: Glass-lined and SS reactors 100 L–20 kL in API, intermediate and speciality chemical plants; manual drum/bag charging through manways, closed charging (hoppers, split valves, vacuum transfer), inerting, exothermic and gas-evolving reactions, sampling, filtration/centrifuge discharge.
hazards: Electrostatic ignition of solvent vapour when pouring powder through an open manway: brush discharges from non-conductive liners/drums, cone discharges from powder heaps, charged operators; MIE of many APIs < 10 mJ
Runaway reaction: wrong order/quantity of reagent, cooling failure, agitator stop, accumulation of unreacted reagent, late initiation; gas evolution over-pressuring vessel; relief undersized
Exposure: solvent vapour and API dust at open manway; hot vapour release on opening; toxic by-products (HCl, H2S, HCN in some chemistries); nitrogen asphyxiation on entry
Mechanical: falls into open manway, agitator start during charging, glass-lining failure, hose whip, centrifuge/filter discharge of solvent-wet cake (static), hot surfaces
pre: Reaction hazard assessment for every process: DSC/ARC data, adiabatic temperature rise, onset temperature vs operating temperature margin, gas-evolution rate, relief sizing (DIERS methods)
HAZOP; safe operating limits in batch record
Inerting: nitrogen purge to O2 below limiting oxygen concentration with margin (typically keep < 5–8% O2 — verify per solvent) before and during charging of powders into flammable solvent
O2 analyser with alarm; N2 supply assured
Static control (IS 7689 / IEC TS 60079-32-1): reactor, hopper, chute, drums and operator earthed (equipment < 10 Ω; footwear/floor < 10⁸ Ω — verify)
Conductive or static-dissipative liners and FIBCs (Type C earthed or Type D); metal scoops; no plastic drums for Class A solvents; restrict charging rate
Closed charging preferred: hopper with LEV and split-butterfly valve, vacuum conveying or drum-tipping enclosure
Manway charging only after risk assessment, with inerting, LEV and solvent temperature below flash point where possible
Hazardous-area Ex equipment; agitator interlocked to charging mode; cooling-water low-flow and high-temperature alarms with automatic actions (stop feed, emergency cooling, quench/dump)
Emergency power for agitator/cooling; PTW for maintenance; manway guard rail/grating
steps: Pre-batch: verify batch record, materials (identity, quantity, order of addition), reaction hazard sheet, inert gas supply, O2 analyser, cooling, agitator, relief and vent path, earthing clamps; sign off.
Set inert atmosphere: purge to O2 target, confirm on analyser; keep purge on during charging; solvent temperature below flash point where feasible.
Powder charging: operator earthed (conductive shoes, floor check), drum/bag earthed and bonded to reactor, LEV on, add through chute/hopper at controlled rate
No pouring from height; close manway between additions; no tipping of plastic liners into solvent vapour.
Liquid charging: by pump or vacuum through dip pipe; bottom or submerged entry; limit velocity; never free-fall flammable liquids into reactor.

Reaction: controlled addition with temperature tracking — stop feed if temperature deviates from profile (accumulation sign); never leave an exothermic addition unattended; verify agitation before and during reagent addition.
Sampling: closed sampler or through sample valve with inert blanket; PPE; never open manway of hot or pressurised reactor; vent and cool first.
Deviation/runaway signs (rapid temperature or pressure rise, venting): stop feeds, maximum cooling, emergency quench/dump per SOP, evacuate area, alert ERT; do not open vessel.
Discharge to centrifuge/filter: earth and bond, inert where solvent-wet, Ex equipment, keep lids closed; cake handling with LEV.
After batch: purge, clean per SOP; reactor entry only under confined-space permit with isolation of all lines, O2 20.9%, LEL 0, agitator locked.
Any new product, scale-up or change of solvent/vendor/equipment → MoC with reaction hazard review; incidents and near misses (static sparks, temperature excursions) investigated.
ppe: Antistatic FR coveralls, conductive safety shoes, chemical goggles/face shield, solvent/API-rated gloves, respirator (A2P3 or PAPR per dust/vapour), hard hat near manways; escape set for toxic chemistries
stop: O2 above inerting limit or analyser not working during powder charging
Earthing of operator/drum/reactor not verified
Unknown or undocumented reaction hazard / deviation from batch record
Cooling or agitator failure with exotherm in progress
Open manway with solvent above flash point without inerting and LEV
records: Reaction hazard assessments and HAZOP, batch records with O2/earthing checks, N2/O2 analyser calibration, earthing resistance tests, relief/interlock test records, MoC, incident and deviation reports, exposure monitoring

india: Factories Act ss.37, 41B–H via state rules / OSH Code Ch. XII; MSIHC Rules (safety report, on-site plan where thresholds exceeded)
IS 7689 (static); IS 5572 & IS/IEC 60079 series; IS 4209 (chemical plants); IS 11457 Pt 1; Petroleum Rules 2002; Sch. II PELs; IS 17893 (permits)

intl: IEC TS 60079-32-1 (electrostatic hazards); CCPS Guidelines for Chemical Reactivity Evaluation & Application to Process Design
UK HSE HSG143 (chemical reaction hazards); DIERS (AIChE) relief design; EN 1127-1 (explosion prevention)

t: Cotton Dust & Byssinosis Control (Blow Room to Weaving)
purpose: Prevent byssinosis, chronic bronchitis and asthma from cotton, flax and jute dust in spinning mills, ginning, waste processing and weaving sheds, and meet medical-surveillance duties.
scope: Bale opening, blow room, carding, combing, drawing, speed and ring frames, open-end spinning, winding, warping, sizing, weaving; waste/willow rooms; cotton ginning and pressing; housekeeping and waste handling.
hazards: Cotton dust (lint-free respirable fraction with bacterial endotoxin): byssinosis — Monday chest tightness progressing to permanent airflow obstruction; highest exposure in blow room, carding and waste rooms
Secondary: dust fires in blow room/filter plant, lint build-up on hot motors; endotoxin fever; eye irritation; noise 90–100 dB(A) in ring and weaving sheds
Cleaning with compressed air and brooms re-suspends dust; untreated (unwashed) cotton; poor filter-plant maintenance returning dust to shed
Vulnerable workers: smokers, asthmatics; new workers reacting on first exposure
pre: Exposure limits: OSHA 1910.1043 benchmark — 0.2 mg/m³ (yarn manufacturing), 0.75 mg/m³ (slashing and weaving), 0.5 mg/m³ (waste houses) lint-free dust by vertical elutriator
Indian Sch. II cotton dust limit (verify value) — set site action level at half
Engineering: enclosed blow-room machines with suction, card suction hoods and continuous waste removal (pneumafil), travelling cleaners on frames
Central filtration plant with rotary filters discharging outside the shed, air changes and humidification (see humidification procedure)
Housekeeping: vacuum or wet methods; no compressed-air blow-down while workers present; scheduled floor and overhead cleaning; waste bagged at source
Medical surveillance: pre-placement history, spirometry (FEV1, FVC) before and after the shift on the first working day of the week
Annual (6-monthly for high-exposure) by certifying surgeon; byssinosis is a notifiable disease (Third Schedule)
Respirators (FFP2/FFP3) for blow room, card stripping, filter cleaning and waste rooms until controls achieve limits; fit, training, replacement schedule
steps: Monthly dust monitoring at fixed stations (blow room, carding, ring, weaving, waste room) and personal samples on rotation; results on department notice board; action if > action level.
Daily: check suction at hoods, filter-plant differential pressure and discharge, travelling cleaners, waste removal; report blocked ducts.
Card stripping/grinding and blow-room cleaning: machine stopped and isolated; respirators worn; waste bagged; floor vacuumed after.
Filter-plant maintenance: isolate fans, treat chamber as confined space, FFP3/PAPR, clean with vacuum; fire watch for lint accumulations on motors and lights.
New workers: baseline spirometry and symptom questionnaire before posting to dusty departments; start in low-exposure jobs where possible; educate on Monday symptoms.
Weekly symptom check by supervisors: chest tightness, cough, breathlessness on Mondays → refer to OHC; relocate symptomatic workers to low-dust areas pending medical review.
Annual medical: spirometry; FEV1 fall ≥ 5% across shift or ≥ 200 mL (verify criteria) → investigate; grades of byssinosis recorded; notify DISH/DFBISH and ESI for notifiable disease.
Smoking banned in mill premises (fire and health); health education in local language.
Noise: hearing-protection zones and audiometry in ring and weaving sheds (see noise procedure).
Annual review: exposure trends, medical findings, control effectiveness; capital plan for enclosure/suction upgrades.
ppe: FFP2/FFP3 respirators for dusty tasks, safety glasses, hearing protection in ≥ 85 dB(A) sheds, head covering, no loose dupatta/scarf near machines
stop: Dust at monitoring point above PEL with controls down
Filter plant or card suction not operating while running
Compressed-air cleaning while workers present
Worker with suspected byssinosis kept in high-dust job
Spirometry programme lapsed > 12 months
records: Dust monitoring results, LEV/filter-plant maintenance, spirometry and medical records (Form per state rules), notifiable disease reports, respirator issue and training, symptom surveillance, noise/audiometry

Sch. II cotton dust PEL (verify); IS 3103 (ventilation); IS 7194 (noise); ESI occupational-disease benefits

t: Dye House & Wet Processing – Chemicals, HT Dyeing Machines, Stenters & Boilers
purpose: Prevent chemical burns, toxic gas release, scalds and pressure-vessel failures, stenter and lint fires, and boiler incidents in dyeing, bleaching, printing and finishing units.
scope: Chemical stores and dispensing; bleaching (H2O2, hypochlorite), scouring and mercerising (NaOH), dyeing (reactive, disperse, vat with sodium hydrosulphite), jigger/winch/soft-flow/HT dyeing machines, stenters and dryers, printing, boilers and thermic-fluid heaters, ETP/ZLD.
roles: Maintenance (pressure vessels, gas trains, stenter ducts)
hazards: Caustic soda (lye 48–50%, flakes — exothermic dissolution), sulphuric/acetic/formic acids, H2O2 50% (oxidiser), hypochlorite (+ acid → chlorine)
Sodium hydrosulphite (self-heating with moisture → SO2, fire), reactive dye powders (respiratory sensitisers)
HT dyeing machines at 130 °C / 3 bar: door opened under pressure, PRV failure; hot liquor and steam scalds from jiggers/winches; steam line failures
Stenters: lint and oil accumulation in ducts ignites at 180–220 °C; thermic-fluid leaks on hot surfaces; gas-fired burners without purge/flame failure; roller nip points at entry
Boilers/thermic heaters: low water, scale, uncertified attendants; ETP: H2S in anaerobic sumps, sludge handling, chlorine dosing
pre: Chemical store: segregation (oxidisers from reducers — H2O2 away from hydrosulphite

Acids from hypochlorite and caustic), dry cool store for hydrosulphite in sealed drums, bunding, labelled containers, SDS in local language, dispensing booth with LEV and weighing under extraction for dye powders
HT machines: pressure vessels registered and tested under state Factories Rules (Rule 61 TN / KA equivalent — verify) with door interlock preventing opening above 0.3 bar / 80 °C (verify)
PRV and gauge calibrated, operator trained
Stenters: scheduled duct and filter cleaning (weekly minimum), lint traps, temperature limits, gas train with pre-purge and flame safeguard (NFPA 86 benchmark)
Thermic-fluid leak checks, fire detection/suppression in exhaust ducts, nip guards and e-stops
Boilers: Boilers Act 2025 / IBR registration and annual certificate; attendant and operation engineer certified (Boiler Attendants Rules 2011 / BOE Rules 2011)
Water treatment; low-water cut-offs tested; thermic-fluid heaters under state rules where applicable
Emergency showers/eyewash within 10 s travel; spill kits (dry absorbent — no sawdust with oxidisers); chlorine awareness; ETP sumps as confined spaces with H2S monitors
steps: Dispensing: weigh dye powders in booth with LEV and FFP2/3; dissolve caustic flakes by adding to cold water slowly with stirring; never water into acid or caustic; label all buckets.
Hydrosulphite: keep drums sealed, handle dry, use only what is needed, never return to drum; wet or warm drum → isolate outdoors, do not seal, inform supervisor.
Bleaching: H2O2 stored vented, away from organics and reducers; hypochlorite never near acids; ventilate bleach ranges.
HT dyeing: check interlock, PRV, gauge; load/unload only after cool-down below 80 °C and pressure zero; stand aside when cracking door; hot liquor drained to safe drain.
Jiggers/winches/steam: guard nips, lids closed while running, steam valves opened slowly, lagging intact; scald first aid (cool 20 min).

Stenter start-up: purge, ignition sequence, no manual lighting; check duct cleaning done; respond to over-temperature or flame-failure alarms; fire in stenter — stop fabric, close dampers, use suppression/CO2, call fire team.
Boiler operation: only certified attendant; blow-down, water tests, low-water cut-off test each shift; annual inspection and hydraulic test by Boiler Inspectorate; log book.
Thermic fluid: leak checks each shift; fluid sampled yearly; no hot work near; drip trays; smoke from lagging → shut down and cool.
ETP: H2S monitoring at anaerobic units and sumps, confined-space permits, chlorine dosing PPE, sludge as HW; ZLD evaporator hot surfaces and chemicals.
Monthly audit: chemical segregation, showers, PRV/interlock tests, duct cleaning records, boiler log, PPE; incident review.
ppe: Chemical goggles and face shield, gauntlet rubber/nitrile gloves, acid/alkali apron, gumboots, FFP2/3 for dye powders, heat-resistant gloves at stenters/HT doors, hearing protection in jet dyeing areas
stop: Opening HT machine above interlock limits or interlock bypassed
Hydrosulphite drum warm, wet or smoking in store
Stenter duct cleaning overdue or flame-safeguard defeated
Boiler run by uncertified person or low-water cut-off failed
Shower/eyewash out of service in dye house
records: Chemical inventory/SDS, dispensing logs, pressure-vessel certificates and interlock tests, stenter cleaning and burner service
Boiler certificate and log book, attendant certificates, thermic-fluid tests, ETP gas-monitor logs, incident and first-aid log

MSIHC Rule 17; IS 17859 (GHS); IS 10592 (showers); IS 4209; Water Act consents (ZLD in Tiruppur per Madras HC orders); HOWM Rules (ETP sludge)

t: Textile & Garment Machinery Guarding (Carding, Ring Frames, Looms, Cutting)
purpose: Prevent entanglement, amputation, cuts and burns on spinning, weaving, knitting and garment machinery, with special attention to cleaning and piecing while running.
scope: Blow room beaters and cleaners, cards, combers, draw/speed frames, ring frames, OE rotors, autoconers, warping and sizing, shuttle and shuttleless looms, circular/flat knitting; garment cutting (band knife, straight knife), sewing, fusing, ironing/pressing; beam and cone handling.
roles: Department supervisors (authorise cleaning while running only where designed)
hazards: Blow room: hands in beaters while clearing choke; lids opened before run-down (rotors spin > 1 min); card lickerin/cylinder/flats during stripping or lap removal; comber nippers
Ring/speed frames: spindle tapes, drafting rollers, flyers, hair/dupatta/saree pallu entanglement while piecing; doffing trolleys; OE rotors opened running
Looms: shuttle fly-out (eye/head), beam lifting (200–500 kg), heald/reed changes, air-jet noise and compressed-air injection; knitting needles and cams

Garments: band-knife and straight-knife cuts, needle punctures, overlock eye injury, fusing press and iron burns, steam boiler/iron hoses; sitting ergonomics; fire exits blocked by stock in dense halls
pre: Guards per Factories Act ss.21–22 and state schedules (TN Rule 53 Schedule I textile machinery; KA Rule 56 Schedule — verify): fixed guards at gears, belts, tapes
Interlocked lids with time-delay on beaters/cleaners/rotors; lickerin and cylinder covers interlocked; nip guards on drafting and calender rollers
Rule: clearing chokes, lap-ups and cleaning only with machine stopped and isolated unless the machine is designed for safe running maintenance; written list of permitted running tasks per machine
Dress code: hair covered, no loose dupatta/scarf/jewellery, fitted sleeves; enforced for all including visitors; women and children not employed at cotton openers (Factories Act s.27)
Looms: shuttle guards and fly catchers, e-stops reachable from both sides, beam hoists/trolleys inspected, noise zone ≥ 85 dB(A) marked; knitting machines with needle-bed guards
Garment cutting: band knife with chain-mail glove and finger guard, straight knife with blade guard and sharpening interlock; needle guards and eye guards on sewing/overlock
Fusing press interlocks and heat shields; irons on insulated stands with steam-hose checks; exits and aisles ≥ 1.2 m kept clear
steps: Shift start: supervisor checks guards and interlocks on each line, e-stops, time-delay function on beater lids; defects tagged and machine stopped until fixed.
Blow room choke: stop, isolate, wait for rotor run-down (interlock timer), open lid, clear with tool; never bypass lid switch.
Card stripping/grinding, lap removal: machine stopped and locked; two persons for cylinder work; respirators (dust); restore guards before restart.
Ring/speed frames: piecing with hands only in permitted zones; stop frame for roller lapping removal and tape replacement; doffing with trolleys on marked paths.
Autoconer/warping: guard splicers and drums; stop before threading inside guards; beam handling with hoist and trained crew, clear path.
Looms: shuttle guards in place; stop before heald/reed/pick-finding inside; air-jet lines isolated for nozzle work; hearing protection in zone.
Garment cutting: chain-mail glove on free hand, blade guard set to fabric height, no cutting above shoulder; blade change under isolation; straight-knife cord management.
Sewing floor: needle guards fitted; broken-needle procedure; no bypassing eye guards; posture breaks every 2 h; adjustable chairs/footrests where possible.
Fusing/ironing: heat-resistant gloves, steam-hose inspections, iron boilers (small boilers) inspected per IBR exemption limits (verify), hot-surface signage; burns first aid.
Monthly: guard audit with safety committee, young-worker (< 18) check against dangerous-machine list, dress-code compliance, exit/aisle audit; incidents reviewed.
ppe: Head covering/hairnet, safety glasses (looms, cutting), chain-mail glove for band knife, hearing protection in weaving/ring sheds, FFP2 for cleaning, safety shoes; no loose garments
stop: Interlock or time-delay lid switch bypassed
Clearing/cleaning inside a running machine not on permitted list
Shuttle guard missing on running loom
Band knife used without chain-mail glove and guard
Exit or aisle blocked by stock/trolleys
records: Machine guard register and audits, interlock tests, permitted running-task list, training/dress-code briefings, young-worker register, beam-hoist inspections, injury/near-miss log, exit audits

ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 Rule 56 Schedule (textile machinery — verify); DFBISH
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rule 53 Schedule I (textile machinery: cotton openers, scutchers, cards, ring frames, looms, hosiery machines — verify); DISH TN; Tiruppur garment cluster fire-safety drives
intl: ILO Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Textiles, Clothing, Leather and Footwear (2022); ISO 11111 series (textile machinery safety)
EN ISO 10821 (sewing machines); UK HSE Textiles Industry Advisory Committee guidance; EN 13998 (band knives — verify)

t: Humidification, Ventilation & Heat in Spinning and Weaving Sheds
purpose: Keep humidified textile sheds within statutory temperature and humidity limits, prevent heat illness, and control legionella and water-quality hazards from humidification plants and air washers.
scope: Humidification plants (air washers, spray nozzles, ultrasonic/evaporative systems), ducting and return-air filtration, water supply and treatment, hygrometer stations, spinning/weaving sheds operating at RH 50–75%, high-heat zones (sizing, stenters, compressors).
hazards: Heat stress: dry-bulb 32–38 °C with RH 60–75% gives WBGT > 30 °C in summer sheds; heat exhaustion/stroke, especially new or fasting workers; 12-hour shifts
Humidification water: stagnant sumps and spray systems — legionella and biofilm; untreated water aerosolised into breathing zone; dust-laden return air
Air-washer plant rooms: confined sump tanks, chemical dosing (biocide, scale inhibitor), slippery floors, fan and pump guards, electrical in wet areas
Poor ventilation: CO2 and lint build-up; fogging on floors; condensation on electrical panels
pre: Statutory: Factories Act s.15 (artificial humidification) and state rules — water of drinking quality or purified, hygrometers at prescribed stations
Dry/wet-bulb readings recorded at prescribed times (e.g. thrice daily — verify TN/KA schedule), humidification stopped when wet-bulb exceeds the rule limit (TN/KA table — verify value ≈ 29.4 °C)

Heat stress plan: WBGT measurement in each department (IS 7243 / ISO 7243), action levels with work-rest and hydration, cool rest rooms, ORS/water points within 50 m, acclimatisation for new workers (7–14 days), buddy watch
Summer timetable for heavy tasks
Legionella control: written scheme for air washers and humidifiers — sump cleaning and disinfection ≥ quarterly (verify)
Biocide dosing, water quality (TVC monthly, Legionella quarterly where risk), drift eliminators, no dead legs
Filters cleaned; make-up water treated
Plant room: pumps/fans guarded, RCD-protected sockets, non-slip floors, drainage; sump entry = confined space; chemical dosing with PPE and SDS
Ventilation: air changes and return-air filtration designed to remove lint and heat; exhaust in sizing/stenter areas; temperature display boards in sheds
steps: Readings: take dry/wet-bulb at each station at the rule times, record in Humidity Register; if wet-bulb exceeds limit — switch humidification to ventilation-only and inform manager.
Daily: check air-washer water clarity, nozzle spray, drift eliminators, sump level, biocide dosing; remove lint from filters; log.

Summer protocol (WBGT ≥ action level): extra breaks, rotate heavy tasks, water/ORS rounds every hour, loosen production targets, monitor new and older workers; stop heavy outdoor/roof work in peak hours.
Heat illness response: move to cool area, cool with water/fans, oral fluids if conscious, OHC/hospital for confusion or no sweating (heat stroke — emergency); record and report.
Weekly: flush low-use spray lines, check hygrometer wicks and calibration, clean spray nozzles; monthly TVC sampling.
Quarterly: drain, clean and disinfect air-washer sumps and tanks (confined-space permit), Legionella sampling, filter replacement; disinfectant neutralised before discharge.
Positive Legionella or cluster of pneumonia: shock-dose, re-sample, inform health authority and workers; review scheme.
Plant-room work: isolate fans/pumps, LOTO, dry floors; chemical dosing in PPE; eyewash available.
Monsoon/condensation: inspect panels and lights for water ingress; ELCB/RCD tests; anti-slip measures.
Annual: review hygrometer locations, WBGT survey, legionella scheme, worker heat-illness records; training refresh in local language.
ppe: Light cotton clothing, head covering, non-slip footwear; gloves/goggles for dosing chemicals; FFP3 and harness/retrieval for sump cleaning
stop: Wet-bulb above statutory limit with humidification running
Humidification water not of required quality/untreated
Air-washer sump entry without confined-space controls
Worker showing heat-stroke signs not removed and treated
Legionella ≥ 1,000 cfu/L untreated
records: Humidity Register (dry/wet-bulb), hygrometer calibration, WBGT surveys, heat-illness log, legionella scheme with cleaning/disinfection and sampling results, water-quality tests, biocide logs, confined-space permits

india: Factories Act s.13 (ventilation & temperature), s.15 (artificial humidification), s.18 (drinking water) via state rules / OSH Code s.6, s.23–24
IS 7243 (WBGT), IS 3103 (ventilation), IS 10500 (water quality); NDMA heat-wave guidelines; Sch. II

tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rules 20–26 on humidification (hygrometers, prescribed times, wet-bulb table — verify); TN Heat Wave guidelines (TNSDMA); DISH TN
osha: OSHA Heat NEP & proposed 1910.148; OSHA Technical Manual Sec. III Ch. 4 (heat) & Ch. 7 (legionella); 1910.146 (sumps)
intl: ISO 7243 (WBGT), ISO 7933 (PHS); ACGIH Heat Stress TLV; UK HSE L8/HSG274 Pt 2 (humidifiers & air washers); ILO Code of Practice Textiles (2022); ASHRAE 188

t: Injection Moulding Machines – Guarding, Purging, Mould Changes & Fumes
purpose: Prevent crush and trap injuries in the mould and clamp area, burns from hot plastic and heaters, injuries during mould changes, and exposure to thermal-decomposition fumes on injection and blow-moulding machines.
scope: Hydraulic, electric and hybrid injection moulding machines 50–3,000 t; blow moulders; vertical insert moulders; take-out robots and sprue pickers; hopper loaders and dryers; granulators; mould changing and storage; hot-runner systems; nitrogen gas-assist.
hazards: Clamp closing (up to 3,000 t) with body part in mould area: failed/bypassed gate interlocks, reaching through rear or top openings, insert loading in semi-auto; ejector and core pulls
Hot plastic: purging at 200–300 °C — splash, gas pockets expelling molten material, barrel and nozzle contact burns; hot-runner leaks (drool); nitrogen gas-assist pressure (300 bar)
Fumes: PVC → HCl; acetal/POM → formaldehyde; polyurethane → isocyanates; PTFE > 400 °C → polymer fume fever; overheated residues; dust from regrind and masterbatch
Mould changes: 0.5–10 t moulds on EOT/forklift, hands between halves, inadequate clamping/pin alignment; granulator rotor knives; hydraulic injection injuries; noise; slips on spilled pellets
pre: Machines to ISO 20430 (ex-EN 201) benchmark: front gate with at least two independent interlocks (electrical plus hydraulic/mechanical), rear and top guards interlocked, purge guard, nozzle guard, hopper interlock
Safety circuit PL d/e; gate interlocks tested every shift
Setter authorisation and written set-up procedure; mould area entry (for insert loading, cleaning) only in set-up mode with clamp blocked or machine isolated
Semi-auto insert loading via two-hand/gate cycle with mechanical restraint where risk assessed
Purging: written procedure — purge shield down/guard closed, operator to side, face shield and heat gloves, purge into tray, no one in front of nozzle
Material-specific limits for residence time/temperature to prevent decomposition
Fume control: LEV at nozzle/purge and at hopper dryers for PVC/POM/PU; general ventilation; exposure monitoring for HCl, formaldehyde, isocyanates where processed; material SDS reviewed

Mould change: lifting plan — rated eyebolts (inspected, correct thread), slings, EOT with certificate, mould clamps torqued, locating ring engaged before releasing crane, die-height set, safety strap on mould halves
Forklift mould carts rated; granulators with interlocked hopper and time-delay, LOTO for blade work
steps: Shift start: test front gate interlocks (machine must not close with gate open), e-stops, purge guard, hopper guard, hydraulic leaks; record in machine log; defects → machine off until repaired.
Normal running: reach into mould area only through the front gate in semi-auto cycle; never through rear/top; use tongs for sprues/stuck parts; keep hands clear of ejectors.
Stuck parts or blocked nozzles: set-up mode, clamp open and blocked (or machine isolated), tools not hands; nozzle cleaning with heat PPE after pressure released.
Purging: shield/guard in place, face shield and gloves, purge in short shots, step aside; dispose of purge in metal bin after cooling; vent fumes.
Material changes: follow temperature profiles; never leave heated barrels full of PVC/POM idle — purge with stable resin; respond to smell/smoke (decomposition) by lowering heat and evacuating fumes.

Mould change: isolate hydraulics and heaters as required, confirm crane/eyebolt capacity, two persons, hands never between mould halves while crane holds load, clamp before releasing, verify alignment and safety strap
Test with low pressure.
Granulator: feed only closed items by hand; blockage → stop, isolate, wait run-down, use tools; blade change under LOTO with cut-resistant gloves.
Hopper loaders/dryers: isolate before clearing; hot-dryer burns; dust LEV; pellet spills swept immediately (slips).

Maintenance: LOTO at main isolator, hydraulic accumulators discharged, barrel heaters cooled or guarded, electrical cabinets by electricians; safety-circuit changes only by OEM/competent person and re-validated.
Monthly: interlock audit on all machines, fume/LEV check, noise, lifting-gear inspection, incident review; retrain setters yearly.
ppe: Safety glasses (face shield for purging), heat-resistant gloves/sleeves, safety shoes, hearing protection where > 85 dB(A), FFP2/respirator per material, cut-resistant gloves for granulator blades
stop: Gate interlock failed or bypassed
Hands in mould area outside set-up mode or without clamp block
Purging with person in front of nozzle or without shield
Smoke/decomposition fumes at barrel
Mould lifted with uninspected eyebolt or hands between halves
records: Machine safety log (interlock tests), setter authorisations, purge and material procedures, LEV checks and exposure monitoring, mould lifting-gear inspections, LOTO records, granulator blade-change log, injury/near-miss log

india: Factories Act ss.21–23, 26, 29 via state rules / OSH Code s.6; IS 9474 (guarding); IS 16819 / ISO 12100; IS 17893 (permits)
Sch. II (HCl 5 ppm ceiling, formaldehyde — verify); HOWM Rules (purge waste); lifting-gear-codes (eyebolts/slings tests)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 Rule 56 Schedule (rubber/plastic machinery — verify); DFBISH
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rule 53 Schedule (plastic/rubber mills — verify); DISH TN
osha: 1910.212, 1910.147 (incl. OSHA letters on IMM guarding), 1910.179 (EOT), 1910.1000, 1910.134; ANSI/PLASTICS B151.1 (horizontal IMM safety), B151.11 (granulators)
intl: ISO 20430:2020 (injection moulding machines), EN 422 (blow moulding), EN 12012-1 (granulators), ISO 13849-1; UK HSE PPS1/PPS series (plastics processing: IMM guarding, purging, fumes); BPF guidance

t: Extruders, Film Lines & Hot-Melt Systems
purpose: Prevent burns, entanglement, high-pressure release and fume exposure on single/twin-screw extruders, blown and cast film lines, pipe/profile lines, compounding and hot-melt adhesive systems.
scope: Extruder barrels, dies and screw changes; blown-film towers and winders; cast film chill rolls; pipe/profile lines with haul-offs, cutters and saws; pelletisers and strand baths; compounding with side feeders and vacuum vents; hot-melt tanks, hoses and applicators (150–200 °C).
hazards: Hot surfaces 180–300 °C on barrels, dies and adaptors; molten polymer splash during start-up, die bolt tightening and blockage clearing; frozen-die over-pressure and rupture; rupture-disc discharge
Entanglement: haul-off and nip rolls, winders (web wrap pulls hand in), corona treaters (HV), chill rolls, pelletiser rotors, strand cutters, pipe saws; manual threading of web
Screw removal: hot screw pulled with hoist/pusher; residual pressure; weight; burns; use of torch on blocked die (fire/decomposition)

Fumes/dust: decomposition on over-temperature or long residence (PVC, PE additives, flame retardants), ozone from corona treaters, resin dust and masterbatch; hot-melt vapours; height on film towers; noise
pre: Guarding per ISO 12100 / EN 1114 series (extruders and dies), EN 12012 (size reduction), EN 1612 (reaction moulding)
Nip guards on all in-running nips, interlocked guards with run-down on winders/pelletisers, pull-wire e-stops along lines, enclosed corona treaters interlocked (HV)
Barrel pressure protection: rupture disc or relief rated for barrel/die, discharge directed away from operator stations and shielded
Melt-pressure transducer with high-pressure shutdown; heater-zone over-temperature alarms and interlocks
Written start-up and die-change procedures: heat soak times, torque sequence with heat-resistant PPE, no one in line of die face during start-up
Blockage clearing without naked flame (use heaters, not torch); screw removal with purpose tool, hoist and cooled barrel
Film towers: guardrails, fixed stairs/platforms, roll-change hoists; web threading with threading tools or tapes at creep speed only

LEV at die/exhaust hoods and at pelletiser/vent ports; ozone extraction at corona treaters; material SDS; hot-melt systems with insulated tank lids, pressure relief, hose inspections, applicator guards
steps: Heat-up: verify zone temperatures, soak time, pressure transducer and rupture disc in place; never start screw with cold or partially melted polymer; stand clear of die.
Start-up/threading: creep speed, threading tools, nip guards closed before speed-up; gloves and face shield for die area; remove purge with tools to metal bin.

Running: monitor melt pressure and temperatures; respond to over-temperature or decomposition smell by reducing heat and ventilating; keep guards closed; clear scrap at winders only with winder stopped.
Roll changes/winders: stop winder or use turret in safe mode; cut web with guarded knife; no hands near nip during wrap; secure heavy reels (500–1,000 kg) with cores/stands; mechanical aids.
Die change/bolt tightening: pressure released, heaters as required, two persons, heat PPE, torque sequence; shield against melt squeeze-out; hot tooling in marked cooling area.
Blocked die/frozen melt: isolate screw, follow heater-based procedure; never use oxy torch or apply pressure to a frozen die; replace rupture disc if it has fired and investigate.
Screw removal: barrel at procedure temperature, pressure zero, use screw puller/hoist, heat PPE, exclusion zone; store hot screw in cradle.
Pelletisers/cutters/saws: interlocked guards, stop and isolate for blade changes (cut-resistant gloves), strand bath electrical RCD-protected.
Hot-melt: fill tanks slowly with lid guard, pressure release before hose/applicator change, hose condition checks, heat gloves/face shield, burn first aid kit at station.
Monthly: guard/interlock audit, rupture-disc and transducer checks, LEV flow, hoist/lifting gear, noise; incident review and retraining.
ppe: Heat-resistant gloves/sleeves and face shield at die/barrel, safety glasses, safety shoes, hearing protection
Respirator per material (A/P combined where fumes), cut-resistant gloves for blades, harness on tower work without rails
stop: Rupture disc missing/fired or pressure transducer bypassed
Nip or winder guard open while running at speed
Torch or naked flame used on blocked die
Hands threading web at speed
Decomposition fumes without LEV
records: Start-up/die-change procedures and logs, rupture-disc/transducer records, interlock audits, LEV checks, exposure monitoring (ozone, HCl, fumes), hoist/lifting inspections, burn and injury log, training records

india: Factories Act ss.21–23, 29, 31 via state rules / OSH Code; IS 9474; IS 16819 / ISO 12100; Sch. II (ozone 0.1 ppm; HCl; dusts); HOWM Rules; lifting-gear-codes
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (fencing; Rule 56 Schedule — verify)
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 (Rule 53 Schedule — verify); DISH TN
intl: EN 1114-1/-3 (extruders and die heads), EN 12012-1/-3 (size reduction/granulators, pelletisers), EN 1034 (winders/paper & film), ISO 13849-1; UK HSE PPS series (extrusion, winders, hot melt); BPF Health & Safety guidance

t: Two-Roll Mills, Calenders, Internal Mixers & Curing Presses (Rubber)
purpose: Prevent in-running nip entrapment and amputation on mills and calenders, crush injuries at mixers and presses, burns and exposure to rubber fume, carbon black and solvents in rubber and PVC compounding and product plants.
scope: Open two-roll mills, calenders (3–4 roll), internal (Banbury-type) mixers, extruders/strainers, curing presses and autoclaves, tyre building and retreading, hose and belting, cement/solvent mixing, carbon black handling.
hazards: Mill nip: hand drawn in while feeding/cutting/blending stock; trip bar (Lunn bar) not stopping rolls within required distance; working alone; roll heat 60–150 °C
Calender nips and hot rolls; stock guides; thread-up; Banbury ram and charging door crush, hopper access, dust; press platens 150–180 °C closing on hands, mould handling; autoclave door/pressure

Rubber fume and dust (IARC Group 1 for rubber industry exposures), carbon black, talc, zinc oxide, accelerators and nitrosamines at curing; solvents (toluene, naphtha, hexane) in cements — fire and neuropathy
Noise; manual handling of 25–30 kg bales and batches; slips from release agents; fire in mixers/mills from overheated stock
pre: Mills per Factories Act s.22 and state schedules (TN Rule 53 Schedule — rubber mills
KA Rule 56 Schedule — verify) and EN 1417 benchmark: trip bar/cable at knee and chest height across front and back
Automatic braking stopping rolls within the specified distance for roll speed (verify EN 1417 table), automatic roll separation or reversal on trip, brake tested every shift

Operator rules: two trained persons present when mill runs; feeding tools for cutting and blending; stock cut with mill knife on marked side; sleeves fitted; no gloves near nips (or breakaway gloves only where assessed)
Calenders: nip guards, trip wires, e-stops at both ends, run at creep for thread-up
Mixers: interlocked charging door and hopper, ram control two-hand or guarded, LOTO for chamber cleaning (confined/hot), dust LEV at charging and carbon-black station
Presses: light curtains/two-hand controls, guards for falling moulds, platen heat shields
Health: LEV on mills/curing presses for fume, exposure monitoring (rubber fume/dust, carbon black, nitrosamines where relevant), medical surveillance
Solvents stored and dispensed per flammable-liquids rules, Ex equipment in cement rooms
Fire: hot stock and mill fires — CO2/DCP extinguishers at each mill, no water on hot oil; autoclaves as pressure vessels registered and tested
steps: Shift start: test trip bar on each mill (rolls must stop within marked distance and separate/reverse), e-stops on calenders/presses, mixer door interlocks; log; defective mill out of service.
Mill feeding: stand to the side, feed with both hands only from above the nip-guard line, use tools for pushing stock; never reach to clear sticking stock — trip and stop first.
Cutting/blending: mill knife cuts on roll away from nip; peel with tool; no reaching behind the roll.
Calender thread-up: creep speed, two persons, guards closed before run speed; stock guides adjusted only with rolls stopped.
Banbury: charge via hopper with LEV; ram down only with door closed and hands clear; never enter chamber without LOTO, cooling and permit; carbon black bags handled with LEV and FFP2.
Curing presses: load/unload with hands clear of platen zone; two-hand/light curtain functional; heat gloves; mould handling with lifting aids; autoclave door opened only at zero pressure and cooled.
Cement/solvent rooms: earth containers, Ex ventilation, respirators, no ignition sources, quantities limited; waste solvent closed drums.
Fume/dust: LEV running during mixing/milling/curing; hoods positioned; filters maintained; housekeeping by vacuum.
Health surveillance: periodic exams for dust/fume-exposed and solvent-exposed workers; audiometry; skin checks (accelerator dermatitis).
Monthly: trip-bar stopping-distance test with marks recorded, brake maintenance, guard audit, LEV flow, lifting aids; investigate every nip near miss.
ppe: Fitted FR cotton overalls (no loose sleeves), safety shoes, safety glasses, hearing protection, FFP2/P3 for carbon black and curing fume, heat gloves for presses/autoclaves, solvent gloves/respirator in cement rooms
stop: Trip bar fails stop/separation test or brake worn
Single operator on a running mill
Gloves or loose sleeves worn at mill nip
Mixer door interlock or press light curtain bypassed
Autoclave door opened under pressure / solvent room ventilation off
records: Trip-bar/brake test log (stopping distance), mill operator authorisations, interlock audits, LEV and exposure monitoring
Pressure-vessel certificates (autoclaves), medical surveillance, solvent inventory, incident/near-miss log

ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 Rule 56 Schedule (rubber mills — verify) & Rule 129 schedules; DFBISH
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rule 53 Schedule (rubber mills/calenders — verify); DISH TN
osha: 1910.216 (mills and calenders in rubber and plastics — trip/stopping distances), 1910.212, 1910.147, 1910.1000, 1910.106
intl: EN 1417 (two-roll mills), EN 12301 (calenders), EN 12013 (internal mixers), EN 289 (compression/transfer presses), EN 1612 (reaction moulding)
UK HSE rubber industry guidance (RUBIAC: mills, mixers, fume); IARC Monograph 100F

t: Solvent-Based Printing & Lamination (Flexo/Gravure) – Flammable Inks, Dryers & Static
purpose: Prevent fire and explosion from solvent inks and adhesives in printing and converting plants, and control solvent exposure, static, dryer hazards and web/roll injuries.
scope: Rotogravure and flexographic presses, solvent inks (ethyl acetate, toluene, IPA, MEK), solvent and solventless lamination (PU adhesives/isocyanates), ink kitchens, solvent storage and recovery, dryers and ovens, slitters/rewinders, cylinder handling and plating, waste solvent.
hazards: Flammable vapours (flash points −10 to 12 °C) in ink trays, kitchens and dryers; ignition from static on fast-moving films (speeds 200–400 m/min), non-Ex lighting/motors, hot bearings, dryer flame or electrical fault
Dryer explosion when LEL exceeded (NFPA 86: ≤ 25% LEL, or 50% with continuous monitoring); fire spread along web and ducts; solvent recovery/RTO flashback
Health: solvent CNS effects, toluene (TLV 20 ppm), ethyl acetate (400 ppm), MEK (200 ppm); isocyanates in PU adhesives (asthma); Cr(VI) in cylinder plating; ozone from corona treaters; noise
Mechanical: nips, doctor blades, rewinders, cylinder lifting (100–500 kg), slitter blades; chemical burns from plating/cleaning; roll handling
pre: Hazardous-area classification (IS 5572 / IEC 60079-10-1): Zone 1 at ink trays/kitchen, Zone 2 extended around presses (verify extents)
Ex-rated motors, lights, instruments, forklifts; IS/IEC 60079-17 inspections; LEL detection in press areas with alarms
Static control: earthing/bonding of presses, rollers, doctor blades, ink pumps and containers; passive/active ionisers at unwind/rewind
Conductive flooring and footwear; humidity control; periodic static-charge measurement (keep below ignition levels)
Dryers to NFPA 86 benchmark: LEL monitors with alarm at 25% and shutdown at 50% (continuous monitoring) or exhaust sized for ≤ 25%, purge before ignition, flame safeguard, airflow interlocks
Duct cleaning schedule; solvent recovery or RTO with flashback protection

Solvent storage per Petroleum Rules 2002 (Class A licence beyond exemption), bunded, earthed, closed dispensing systems; ink kitchen with LEV; daily quantities limited at press; waste solvent in closed earthed drums
Fire protection: sprinklers/deluge or CO2 for presses and dryers, foam for storage, extinguishers at each press, exits, fire watch for hot work
Exposure monitoring and health surveillance; isocyanate controls for PU lamination
steps: Shift start: check LEL monitors, Ex lighting, ioniser function, earthing straps, dryer safeguards, extinguishers; record.
Ink kitchen: mix under LEV with earthed containers and Ex pumps; keep lids closed; no plastic open containers for Class A; label inks; clean spills with inert absorbent.
Press operation: keep ink trays covered where possible, no electronic devices unless Ex, respond to LEL alarm by slowing/stopping and increasing exhaust; monitor web static; stop on sparking.
Dryer start-up: purge, verify airflow and LEL monitor, ignite via safeguard; never bypass; shut down on flame failure or LEL high.
Web threading, splicing and roll changes: creep speed, nip guards, cutting with guarded knives, roll lifts with shaft/hoist; doctor blade changes with cut-resistant gloves and blade covers.
Cylinder handling: rated lifting devices, two persons, racks secured; plating shop with LEV, Cr(VI) controls and PPE.
Cleaning: solvents in closed washers or with minimum quantities; rags in self-closing metal bins emptied each shift; no cleaning of running press.
Hot work or maintenance: PTW, solvent lines isolated, LEL 0%, ventilation running, fire watch 60 min; Ex equipment reinstated and inspected.
Waste: solvent, inks and rags as hazardous waste (HOWM) with manifests; VOC emissions within SPCB consent; recovery solvent quality controlled.
Health: solvent/isocyanate exposure monitoring, biological monitoring (hippuric acid for toluene — verify), annual medical, audiometry; training and drills (press fire, solvent spill).
ppe: Antistatic FR clothing, conductive footwear, chemical goggles, solvent gloves (nitrile/laminate per SDS), respirator (A2/P3) in kitchen and cleaning, cut-resistant gloves for blades, hearing protection
stop: LEL alarm or monitor out of service with press running
Non-Ex equipment/phone in Zone 1/2
Static control (earthing/ionisers) not functioning on film line
Dryer safeguard or purge bypassed
Solvent stored beyond licence or unbunded
records: Area classification drawings, Ex inspection register, LEL calibration, static measurements and earthing tests
Dryer safeguard tests, PESO licence/stock, HW manifests, exposure/biological monitoring, PTW records, drill reports

IS 11457 Pt 1; Sch. II (toluene, ethyl acetate, MEK, Cr(VI)); HOWM Rules 2016; Air Act consent (VOC); Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 (EPR)

t: Soldering, Reflow & Wave Solder – Flux Fume and Lead Control
purpose: Prevent occupational asthma from rosin (colophony) flux fume, lead poisoning from tin-lead solder and dross, burns from molten solder and exposure to cleaning solvents in electronics assembly.
scope: Hand soldering and rework stations, wave and selective soldering machines (solder pots 250–300 °C), reflow ovens (air/nitrogen), stencil and PCB cleaning (IPA, saponifiers), conformal coating and potting, solder paste handling, dross and waste.
roles: Industrial hygienist; occupational physician (blood lead, asthma)
hazards: Colophony fume: respiratory sensitiser causing asthma (UK WEL 0.05 mg/m³ 8-h, 0.15 mg/m³ STEL — verify); once sensitised, trace exposure triggers attacks
Lead: ingestion via hands/food from solder, dross and dust; lead oxide fume at pots; blood lead rises silently (ACGIH BEI 20 µg/dL; action 30 µg/dL benchmark — verify); reproductive toxicity
Burns from solder pots, splash during dross skimming or wet PCBs (steam explosion), hot irons; reflow oven nitrogen (asphyxiation in enclosed oven or N2 room); hot-air rework
Solvents: IPA (flammable), flux thinners; conformal coating fume and UV curing (eye/skin); fine particulate from fume-filter changes; ESD wrist straps without 1 MΩ resistor (shock path)
pre: Fume control: tip extraction (on-iron) or arm/hood LEV at every hand-soldering station capturing at source
Enclosed wave/selective/reflow machines exhausted to outside or HEPA/carbon filters; smoke test and airflow checks weekly; LEV thorough examination 14-monthly (benchmark)
Lead hygiene: dedicated area for Pb solder, no food/drink/cosmetics, hand-wash before breaks, wet-wipe benches, HEPA vacuum (no brushing), separate lead work clothes
Prefer lead-free (SAC) where product allows; dross and lead waste as hazardous waste
Medical surveillance: blood lead at placement and 6-monthly for pot/dross workers (yearly for hand soldering), remove from exposure above action level
Respiratory questionnaire and spirometry yearly for colophony-exposed; asthma is a notifiable disease
Solder pots: temperature controllers with over-temperature cut-out, splash shields, dross tools, face shields; dry PCBs/components (moisture)
N2 systems with O2 monitors (< 19.5% alarm) in enclosed areas; reflow oven exhaust and flux condensate management
Solvents stored per flammable rules, dispensed in small closed containers, used under LEV; conformal-coating booths with LEV and UV-shielded curing
ESD programme with 1 MΩ series resistors in wrist straps/mats; electrical safety of irons/stations (earthing, RCD)
steps: Shift start: switch on LEV, check airflow indicator/smoke test, filter status, pot temperature, splash shields; report defects.
Hand soldering: keep tip extraction nozzle within 50 mm of joint (verify by smoke test); never lean into fume; use lead-free where specified; sponge/wire tip cleaning.
Wave/selective soldering: pre-heat and dry boards; skim dross with tools and face shield, pour into labelled metal container, let cool, seal as hazardous waste; add solder bars slowly (dry).
Reflow ovens: verify exhaust before start; N2 flow monitored; no entry into oven tunnel until cool and purged; clean flux condensate traps with gloves/respirator.
Breaks and end of shift: wash hands and face before eating/smoking; remove lead-area coat; no food at benches.
Cleaning: wet-wipe benches daily; HEPA vacuum floors; change LEV/fume filters with FFP3 and bag as hazardous waste.
Solvent use: small quantities in dispensers, lids closed, under LEV, away from heat/irons; empty containers capped; spill kit.
Conformal coating/potting: LEV booth, gloves (nitrile), eye protection for UV; skin contact with uncured resin avoided (sensitiser).
Health: blood lead and spirometry programme on schedule; symptoms (wheeze, chest tightness at work) reported and investigated; sensitised workers moved away from flux fume.
Monthly: LEV check records, lead hygiene audit (swabs on benches/canteen doors), waste manifests, training refresh; annual review of exposure data.
ppe: Safety glasses (face shield at pots), heat-resistant gloves for pots/rework, nitrile gloves for solvents/paste, FFP3 for filter/dross cleaning, lab coat/dedicated clothing in lead areas, ESD footwear/wrist strap with resistor
stop: LEV off or failed smoke test at a soldering station
Eating/drinking in lead area
Blood lead above action level without removal from exposure
Pot splash shield missing / wet boards into wave
O2 alarm in nitrogen reflow area
records: LEV checks and examinations, blood-lead and spirometry records, lead hygiene audits, pot temperature/maintenance logs
O2 monitor calibration, solvent inventory, HW manifests (dross, filters), training, notifiable disease reports
