t: Clean-Room Chemicals & Specialty Gases – HF, Wet Benches, Silane/Arsine, ESD
purpose: Prevent chemical burns, toxic and pyrophoric gas incidents, asphyxiation and fire in semiconductor, display, PCB and solar-cell fabs using hydrofluoric acid, strong acids/bases, solvents and specialty gases.
scope: Wet benches and chemical delivery (HF, BOE, H2SO4/H2O2 piranha, HNO3, HCl, TMAH, KOH, NMP, PGMEA), gas cabinets and bunkers (SiH4, AsH3, PH3, NH3, Cl2, HCl, NF3, WF6, H2), bulk gases (N2, O2, Ar, LN2), exhaust and scrubbers, PCB plating/etching, waste.
roles: Emergency response team (SCBA, HF first aid)
hazards: HF: penetrates skin, binds calcium — delayed, deep burns; > 1% body area at 49% or any exposure to concentrated HF can be fatal (verify); TLV 0.5 ppm TWA / 2 ppm ceiling (ACGIH — verify); eye exposure blinding

TMAH (developer ≥ 2.38%; concentrate 25%): skin absorption lethal with respiratory arrest; piranha (H2SO4+H2O2) exothermic and explosive with organics; hot phosphoric 160 °C; nitric/HCl fumes; KOH/NaOH burns
Gases: silane pyrophoric (ignites in air), arsine (TLV 0.005 ppm) and phosphine (0.05 ppm) acutely toxic, Cl2/HCl/NH3 corrosive, NF3/WF6, H2 explosive
Cylinder change-out leaks; exhaust failure; nitrogen/argon asphyxia in sub-fab
Fire in wet benches (plastic + solvents), exhaust duct fires; electroplating Cr(VI)/cyanide (HCN with acid); ESD discharges; slips; ergonomics; confined ducts and plenums
pre: Design per NFPA 318 / SEMI S2 / IFC Ch. 27 benchmark: exhausted wet benches with lids and interlocks, chemical delivery systems with double containment and leak detection
Gas cabinets with exhaust, excess-flow valves, restrictive flow orifices, coaxial tubing, automatic shut-off and purge panels
Toxic gas monitoring system (TGMS) at ½ TLV alarm with auto isolation (verify setpoints)

Gas Cylinders Rules 2016 / PESO: toxic and flammable cylinder storage, licences, segregation; silane in dedicated bunker outdoors with deluge; bulk cryogens per SMPV(U) Rules; O2 depletion monitors in sub-fab and gas rooms
HF response: 2.5% calcium gluconate gel at every HF-use point, HF-specific first-aid training, hospital tie-up with calcium protocols (gluconate IV/arterial), eyewash/showers within 10 s
Medical surveillance; TMAH handled only in closed systems or with full PPE and immediate flush
Chemical hygiene plan: SDS (IS 17859), compatibility segregation, labelled delivery lines, waste segregation (HF to calcium treatment
Cyanide separate from acids), scrubbers for acid/base/VOC exhaust; Cr(VI)/cyanide controls in plating; PPE matrix per chemical

Emergency: ERT with SCBA and Level A/B suits for gas releases, gas-release drills with fire service, shelter-in-place procedure for fab, TGMS alarm response tree; MSIHC compliance where thresholds exceeded
steps: Daily: TGMS and O2 monitors status, exhaust flows at benches/cabinets, scrubber pH/flow, leak-detection panels, eyewash/showers; log and escalate faults.
Wet-bench work: lids closed between steps, chemicals added via delivery system or with small labelled containers
Never pipette by mouth; piranha made fresh (acid first, slow peroxide), never stored closed; hot baths with splash guards.
HF/BOE: double gloves (nitrile under neoprene/laminate), face shield + goggles, apron
Any skin contact — flush 5 min, apply calcium gluconate gel while massaging, go to OHC/hospital immediately with SDS; eyes — flush 15 min, hospital.
TMAH: closed dispensing; any skin contact → remove clothing, flush ≥ 15 min, hospital even if feeling well.
Gas cylinder change-out: two certified technicians, PPE per gas (SCBA for AsH3/PH3/Cl2 cabinets per site rule), cabinet exhaust verified, purge cycles completed, leak check, valve protection
Silane change-out outdoors with deluge armed.
TGMS alarm: follow response tree — low alarm: investigate with PPE; high alarm: evacuate zone, isolate at auto shut-off, ERT with SCBA; account for all; notify.
Exhaust or scrubber failure: stop chemical/gas processes in affected area; no wet-bench work without exhaust; duct work as confined space with gas test.

Plating/etching (PCB): LEV at tanks, cyanide and acid separated with physical barriers, Cr(VI) exposure controls (PEL 5 µg/m³), eyewash, waste treatment (cyanide oxidation, chrome reduction) before ETP.
Waste: segregated, labelled, double-contained; HF waste neutralised with lime/calcium; solvent waste earthed; manifests under HOWM; empty cylinders returned with caps.

Training: chemical-specific (HF, TMAH, piranha) before authorisation; gas technician certification; annual drills (gas release, HF burn, cryogen spill); medical surveillance (As, F, Cr biomonitoring where relevant — verify).
ppe: Chemical goggles + face shield, chemical-resistant gloves (double; laminate for HF), acid apron/suit, chemical boots; SCBA and gas suits for ERT/cylinder change-out per gas; cryogenic gloves/face shield for LN2; ESD garments
stop: TGMS, exhaust or O2 monitor out of service in area with process running
Calcium gluconate or eyewash missing at HF point
Cylinder change-out by single/uncertified person
Piranha stored closed or mixed with organics
Cyanide and acid handled in same area without barrier
records: TGMS/O2 calibration and alarm logs, exhaust and scrubber checks, gas cylinder register and PESO licences, chemical inventory/SDS
Change-out logs, HF/TMAH exposure and first-aid records, biomonitoring, HW manifests, drill reports, MSIHC documents

t: Lithium Cell & Pack Storage, Handling and Thermal-Runaway Response
purpose: Prevent and respond to thermal-runaway fires and toxic off-gassing of lithium-ion cells, modules and packs in cell manufacturing, pack assembly, warehouses, repair/returns and recycling.
scope: Incoming cell inspection and storage, formation and ageing, pack assembly lines, finished-goods and spares warehouses, damaged/defective/returned (DDR) handling, transport packaging, battery waste; lithium-metal and sodium-ion cells where present.
roles: ERT (Li-ion fire trained) and fire service liaison
hazards: Thermal runaway from internal short, over-charge/discharge, mechanical damage, heat: cell venting (hissing, sweet solvent smell), smoke, jet flames > 600 °C, propagation through racks
Gases HF, CO, H2, hydrocarbons (toxic and explosive)
Storage: high state of charge, dense stacking, damaged cells mixed with good stock, ignition of packaging; sprinkler water insufficient for deep-seated pack fires; re-ignition for days
Manufacturing: electrolyte (LiPF6 → HF with moisture), NMP solvent in electrode coating (reprotoxic
Verify limit), dry rooms (dew point −40 °C), formation racks (over-charge faults), laser welding fume, lithium-metal (water-reactive — Class D)
Handling: shorting by tools/jewellery, drops, punctures; transport of untested/damaged cells (UN 38.3); recycling/disassembly of charged packs
pre: Storage per NFPA 855 / FM Global DS 8-1 benchmark: SoC 30–50% for storage, temperature 10–25 °C, segregated fire compartment or detached building
Sprinklers (density per FM 8-1 — verify), racks with limited stack height, aisles ≥ 2.4 m (verify), quantity limits per fire area, no mixed combustible storage
Detection: early off-gas (VOC/CO/H2) and smoke detection linked to alarm and HVAC isolation, thermal imaging rounds, CCTV
Fire-service information sheet (chemistry, kWh, layout); water supply for prolonged cooling (hydrants/monitors)

DDR cells: separate outdoor quarantine ≥ 15 m from buildings (verify) in metal containers with sand/vermiculite or in rated cabinets; inspected for swelling/leak/heat; discharged before disposal where safe
Manufacturing controls: formation racks with per-channel temperature/voltage trips and local suppression, electrolyte filling under LEV with HF response (calcium gluconate)
NMP recovery and exposure monitoring, dry-room entry limits (hydration, time), ESD/short-circuit prevention (insulated tools, covered terminals)
Transport: UN 38.3 tested cells, UN 3480/3481 packaging and labels, SoC ≤ 30% for air (verify), damaged cells under special provisions; Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 for end-of-life
steps: Receipt: inspect packaging and cells (dents, swelling, leakage, odour, temperature); reject suspect lots to quarantine; record SoC/voltage sample; store in designated compartment.
Storage rounds: twice-daily visual and thermal-camera check of racks; check detection panel; no charging in storage; keep aisles and sprinkler clearance; FIFO to limit ageing.
Handling: two persons for packs > 25 kg or lifting aids; terminals covered; no metal tools/jewellery near terminals; never puncture or crush; drop → quarantine 24 h with monitoring.
Formation/ageing: monitor trips; on over-temperature alarm isolate channel, remove cell with heat gloves to quench container (water or sand) if safe; evacuate if venting.
Suspected thermal runaway (hissing, smell, smoke, heat): raise alarm, isolate power, move people away, evacuate area
If a single cell/pack is safely movable at early stage — move to outdoor quench tank; otherwise leave for ERT.
Fire response: call fire service stating 'lithium-ion'; ERT in SCBA applies large volumes of water to cool and prevent propagation (do not try to 'extinguish' with small extinguishers)
Keep upwind; monitor for re-ignition 24–72 h with thermal camera; isolate affected stock outdoors.
Lithium-metal cells: no water — Class D agent/dry sand; segregated storage.
After event: treat debris as hazardous waste, HF/contaminated water contained, investigate root cause, review storage layout and detection.
Waste: discharged and insulated cells to registered recycler under BWMR 2022 with manifests; no landfill or mixing with general scrap.
Drills twice yearly with fire service; training for all handlers (signs of runaway, quarantine, PPE); review of NFPA 855/FM updates and OEM advisories.
ppe: Safety glasses/face shield, insulated or nitrile gloves (heat gloves for hot cells), FR clothing, FFP3 for cleanup; SCBA and chemical suit for ERT; cryo/HF kit where electrolyte handled
stop: Swollen, hot, hissing or leaking cell inside main storage/production
DDR cells stored indoors with good stock
Detection or sprinkler system impaired without compensating measures
SoC or quantity limits exceeded in storage compartment
Charging of cells/packs in warehouse
records: Receipt inspection and quarantine register, storage SoC/temperature logs, thermal rounds, detection/sprinkler tests, formation alarm logs, incident and quench records, HW/BWMR manifests, drill reports, UN 38.3 certificates

india: IS 16046 Pt 1/2 (IEC 62133) & IEC 62619 / IS 17855 (cell/battery safety); BIS CRS registration (cells); Battery Waste Management Rules 2022
Factories Act ss.37, 38 via state rules / OSH Code; Fire NOC conditions (NBC Part 4 storage); HOWM Rules (electrolyte, NMP); Sch. II (HF, NMP — verify); IS 2190 (Class D agents)

tn: TNFRS; TN Factories Rules 1950; TNPCB; TN EV/ACC cell plant EHS conditions (verify)

t: Wind Turbine Tower Climbing, Ladders, Lifts & Fall Arrest
purpose: Prevent falls and medical emergencies while ascending and descending wind turbine towers (80–140 m hubs) by ladder, climb assist or service lift, and while transitioning between platforms.
scope: Onshore WTG towers (tubular steel, concrete, hybrid) during construction, commissioning and O&M; internal ladders with fall-arrest rail/rope systems, climb-assist, service lifts, platforms and hatches; hub-height work preparation.
hazards: Fall from ladder during transitions, hatch openings or when fall-arrester not engaged; rail/rope system defects; harness misuse; dropped tools onto persons below
Physical exhaustion and heat (tower interior 40–50 °C in Indian summer), dehydration, cardiac events during climb; weight of tools and PPE
Service lift faults: overload, trapped persons, door interlocks; pinch points; falls through hatches left open; poor lighting; slippery rungs (oil, water)
Electrical: 690 V/33 kV switchgear at tower base; lightning; wind-induced tower sway; monsoon lightning season; snakes/animals at tower base
pre: Training: GWO Basic Safety Training (Working at Heights, First Aid, Manual Handling, Fire Awareness) or equivalent, site induction, turbine-specific familiarisation
Refresher every 24 months; medical fitness assessment (BP, cardiovascular, BMI/weight within PPE limits ~ 136 kg incl. tools — verify) yearly
PPE: full-body harness EN 361 with front/dorsal attachment, twin-leg energy-absorbing lanyard EN 355
Guided-type fall arrester EN 353-1 matched to rail/rope, work-positioning lanyard EN 358, helmet with chin strap EN 12492/397, gloves, boots
6-monthly PPE inspection by competent person plus pre-use
Fall-arrest systems: rail/rope and anchors inspected annually (and after lightning, fault or heavy use) by competent person; ladder rungs, hatches and platforms inspected
Service lift examined per manufacturer and 12-monthly (verify state Lifts Act applicability), with trapped-person release procedure
Rules: minimum two persons per turbine, communication with control room/site office at tower base and hub
Climb only within weather window (see weather procedure), hydration and rest at platforms, tool bags with tethers, hatches closed after passing
Emergency: rescue kit (descender EN 341 Class A, rope ≥ hub height + margin) at nacelle/top platform, first-aid kit and AED at site, evacuation plan to hospital (see remote-site procedure)
steps: Pre-climb: tower base check — switchgear status, no lightning alert, wind within OEM limit for climb, communication test, buddy check of harness/lanyards/arrester, tools tethered, water carried; log climb start with control.

Ascending: attach fall arrester to rail/rope before stepping on ladder; three points of contact; one person per ladder section between platforms (verify OEM); rest at each platform; close hatch behind you.
Transitions at platforms/hatches: use twin lanyards to stay connected 100% — one hook on before the other off; anchor only to rated points (marked); never to cable trays or pipes.
Climb assist: pre-use check of motor, rope, brake; weight setting; still connect fall arrester; stop if rope slips or noise.
Service lift: check inspection sticker, load limit (persons + tools), door interlocks, emergency stop, communication
Do not use in lightning alert or when fault lamp lit; follow trapped-person release only by trained persons.
At top: connect to nacelle anchor before unclipping from ladder; report arrival to control; check rescue kit present before starting work.
Descending: same discipline; fatigue is highest — rest at platforms; lower tools by bag/hoist, not carried in hands.
Dropped-object control: exclusion zone at tower base when work in progress above; tool tethers; hatch covers closed; tool inventory before leaving.
Heat: climb early morning in summer; 500 mL water per 30 min of climbing (verify); stop and rest if dizzy; heat-illness first aid.
Monthly: PPE and rescue-kit inspection, ladder/rail checks, lift logbook, climb-log review (durations, incidents); yearly: competent-person inspection of fall-arrest systems and lift.
ppe: Full-body harness (EN 361), twin energy-absorbing lanyard (EN 355), guided fall arrester (EN 353-1), work-positioning lanyard (EN 358), climbing helmet with chin strap, gloves, safety boots, headlamp, tool tethers
stop: Lightning alert or wind above OEM climb limit
Fall-arrest rail/rope or lanyard defective / inspection overdue
Single person on turbine or no communication with control
Technician unwell, dizzy or not medically cleared
Rescue kit missing at top platform/nacelle
records: GWO/competence certificates, medical fitness, PPE inspection register (6-monthly), fall-arrest system and lift inspections, climb logs, dropped-object and near-miss reports, rescue-kit inspections

IEC 61400-1; EN 81-43 / EN 1808 (service lifts — verify applicable standard); UK RenewableUK Onshore Wind H&S Guidelines

t: Rescue from Height in Wind Turbines (Tower, Nacelle, Hub)
purpose: Ensure an injured or suspended technician can be reached, stabilised and lowered to the ground within the suspension-trauma window using the team on the turbine, and evacuated to hospital from a remote site.
scope: Self-evacuation and assisted rescue from nacelle roof, nacelle interior, hub/spinner, tower ladder and platforms, service lift; casualty types: suspended in harness, unconscious on ladder, injured in nacelle, trapped in hub; nacelle fire evacuation.
hazards: Suspension trauma: a motionless suspended person may lose consciousness within 5–20 min; death if not lowered and managed; rescue must start within minutes — fire service cannot arrive in time at remote sites
Rescuer falls while attaching to casualty; rope burns/descender failure; rope too short; casualty struck against tower; nacelle fire with only descent as escape
Casualty on ladder inside tower: extraction up/down narrow sections; weight; platforms and hatches; heat and fatigue of rescuers
Communication failure; ambulance 45–90 min away; night rescue; wind/lightning preventing external descent
pre: Every technician trained in GWO Advanced Rescue Training (hub, spinner, nacelle, tower) or equivalent; refresher every 24 months; site rescue plan per turbine model with pre-rigged anchor points identified
Rescue kit at nacelle/top platform: descender EN 341 Class A with rope ≥ hub height + 10% (e.g. 120 m hub → ≥ 135 m)
Rescue stretcher/evacuation sling, pulleys for lifting, casualty harness attachment, rescue knife, head torch
Inspected monthly and after use; second kit for tower ladder rescue at base or mid-platform
Suspension relief: trauma straps on every harness; policy — if suspended and conscious, pump legs/use straps; rescuers lower casualty to ground or platform within 15 min (verify target)

Ground: first-aid responders, AED, trauma kit, stretcher, vehicle ready, GPS coordinates of each WTG, hospital and ambulance numbers posted, mobile/radio coverage map; dedicated access road kept clear
Nacelle fire: automatic suppression/alarms where fitted; escape route via nacelle hatch with personal descender (auto-descent device) carried by each technician in nacelle; drills
steps: Alarm: witness calls control and site manager (turbine ID, casualty condition, location); control stops turbine (if safe) and alerts ambulance/fire service with meeting point.
Rescue leader assesses: can casualty self-rescue? conscious? breathing? location; choose pre-planned method (lower from nacelle externally, lower inside tower, lift to platform).
Suspended casualty (external/nacelle roof): rescuer anchors independently, attaches descender rope to casualty, transfers load, cuts/releases lanyard, lowers to ground with controlled speed
Ground crew receives, lays casualty flat/semi-recumbent per current guidance, monitors.
Casualty on tower ladder: attach rescue system above, lift slightly to release fall arrester, lower to nearest platform or ground through ladder bay; manage hatches; second rescuer guides.
Hub/spinner casualty: rotor lock confirmed, hub stable; extract through hub hatch using pulley system to nacelle, then lower externally or via lift if operable.
First aid during rescue: airway, bleeding, spinal care if fall; AED on ground; oxygen if available; keep casualty warm.
Handover to ambulance at meeting point; send technician with casualty details; inform family and statutory authorities as required.

Nacelle fire: raise alarm, attempt extinguisher only on small fire, otherwise evacuate by lift if safe or descend externally with personal descender from pre-identified anchor; account for team at base.
Post-rescue: isolate scene, preserve evidence, replace used kit, debrief, incident investigation and reporting (OSH Code/BOCW/CEA as applicable).
Drills: full rescue drill per team every 6 months (verify) covering at least two scenarios; annual drill with local fire service and ambulance; records.
ppe: Standard climbing PPE plus personal descender, rescue gloves, head torch; ground crew: first-aid kit, AED, trauma kit, stretcher, blankets
stop: Team not current in rescue training or fewer than two trained persons on turbine
Rescue kit missing, rope length insufficient or inspection overdue
No communication with ground/control
Weather prevents safe external descent and no alternative plan
Ambulance/hospital route not known or inaccessible
records: Rescue training certificates, site rescue plans per model, rescue-kit inspection register, drill reports and lessons, incident reports, emergency contact and hospital tie-up records

t: Nacelle & Hub Entry, Rotor Lock and Stored-Energy Isolation
purpose: Prevent crushing by rotating or pitching components, electrical shock/arc flash, hydraulic injection and falls during work inside nacelles, hubs and spinners, and on nacelle roofs.
scope: Nacelle interior (gearbox, generator, converter, yaw, brake, hydraulics), hub and spinner (pitch systems, blade bearings, batteries/capacitors), nacelle roof (anemometry, lightning receptors), tower-base switchgear and transformer; O&M, retrofit and commissioning tasks.
hazards: Rotor turning or pitching while persons in hub: rotor lock not engaged, brake release, wind gust, pitch system energised; crush between hub and nacelle, blade bearing rotation
Electrical: 690 V generator/converter, 33 kV switchgear, back-feed from grid, capacitor banks and pitch batteries/UPS; arc flash; induced voltages

Stored energy: hydraulic accumulators 150–250 bar (brake/pitch), spring-applied brakes, gearbox/bearing heat (70–90 °C), hot oil, high-torque bolting tools (hydraulic 700 bar — injection injury); nacelle crane loads
Falls: open hatches, nacelle roof without rails (wind), hub hatch; confined character of hub (limited egress, heat, fumes from grease/solvents); fire in nacelle
pre: Turbine stopped and set to service mode from control
Turbine-specific isolation procedure (LOTO) covering HT (where required — HT PTW via DISCOM/pooling substation)
LV main breaker, converter, pitch/yaw supplies, UPS/batteries, hydraulics (depressurise accumulators), and mechanical locks
Rotor lock: engage all lock pins (both where fitted) with blades feathered and rotor at designated position; verify engagement indicator and visually
Wind below OEM limit for lock engagement (typically ≤ 12–15 m/s — verify); yaw lock where needed; pitch lock/mechanical blocks for blade-bearing work
Hub entry treated as permit-controlled (confined-space-like): two persons, communication, atmosphere check if solvents/grease fumes, lighting, hatch secured open, exit route clear
Nacelle roof access only with anchor points, wind below roof-work limit (≤ 12 m/s — verify) and no lightning

Arc-flash assessment for LV/HT panels; arc-rated PPE and insulated tools for live testing; capacitor discharge times observed (converter/pitch — per OEM, typically 5–10 min — verify); test-before-touch

Lifting: nacelle crane/hoist tested 12-monthly with SWL marked; rigging inspected; exclusion at tower base during lifts; hydraulic bolting tools inspected, hoses and couplings rated; hot-surface and oil handling controls
steps: Request service mode from control; verify turbine stopped, brake applied; log start of work and expected duration.
Apply electrical isolation per turbine LOTO list: open and lock main LV breaker, isolate converter and pitch/yaw supplies, isolate UPS/batteries
HT isolation via authorised person with permit where work requires; verify dead with tested instrument on each circuit; apply earths where required.
Depressurise hydraulics (brake/pitch accumulators) per OEM and verify gauges at 0 bar; release spring energy only with tooling specified.
Engage rotor lock: feather blades, rotate to lock position with turning gear/motor, insert pins, verify indicator and visual; place lock tag; engage yaw lock if work on yaw or roof.

Hub entry: open hatch and secure; two persons (one may remain at hatch); check pitch system isolated and mechanical blocks fitted before touching blade bearings; carry radio; no entry without rotor lock verified.
Nacelle roof: connect to anchor before exiting hatch; check wind and lightning status; tools tethered; limit time; no roof work in rain.
Bolting/torqueing: hydraulic tool inspection, hoses clear, hands away from reaction arm, pressure released before adjusting; injection injury → hospital immediately regardless of appearance.
Hot work in nacelle (rare): permit, fire watch, extinguishers, fume control; grease/oil spill control; cleaning solvents in small quantities.

Return to service: remove tools and persons from hub/roof, remove blocks and pins (confirm indicator), remove earths and locks in reverse order, close hatches, reset converter, inform control; final headcount at tower base.
Records: isolation and rotor-lock logs, permits, crane/tool inspections, incident reports; review near misses (unexpected movement, residual voltage) with OEM.
ppe: Climbing PPE, arc-rated clothing and face shield for electrical testing, Class 0 insulating gloves, insulated tools, heat-resistant gloves, hydraulic-tool face shield, hearing protection near generator, headlamp
stop: Rotor lock pins not verified engaged before hub entry
Residual voltage found after isolation / dead test not possible
Accumulator pressure not at zero before hydraulic work
Wind above lock/roof limits or lightning alert
Single person in hub or on roof
records: Turbine LOTO procedures and logs, rotor-lock register, HT permits, test-before-touch records, accumulator checks, nacelle crane and bolting tool inspections, hub-entry permits, incident log

t: Blade Inspection & Repair – Rope Access, Suspended Platforms, Composites
purpose: Prevent falls, dropped objects, composite-dust and resin exposures, and lightning/weather incidents during external and internal blade work using rope access, blade access platforms, cranes or drones.
scope: Leading-edge erosion repair and LEP application, lightning receptor and down-conductor checks, crack and damage repair, internal blade-root inspection, blade cleaning, drone inspection; rope access (IRATA/SPRAT), suspended blade platforms, crane baskets; ground-level blade repair after down-tower.
roles: Blade repair supervisor (IRATA L3 or platform competent)
hazards: Falls: anchor failure, rope damage on blade edge, single-rope reliance, platform suspension failure, winds swinging technician against blade/tower; dropped tools/materials onto ground crew
Composites: glass/carbon-fibre dust from grinding (respiratory, skin), styrene/epoxy/PU resins and hardeners (sensitisers
Dermatitis), solvents (acetone), heating blankets (burns, fire) — in confined blade interior exposure is intense
Weather: wind > limits, rain (slip, cure failure), lightning (blade is the strike point), heat on composite surface 60 °C+; rotor rotating/pitching if lock fails
Blade interior: confined space — limited egress, dust, solvent vapour, heat; falls inside blade; working alone
pre: Rotor locked with blade in 6 o'clock (down) position for external work, pitch locked; turbine isolated per nacelle procedure; adjacent turbines in rotor-shadow assessed
Rope access per IRATA ICOP: two independently anchored systems (working and safety lines), anchors rated (≥ 15 kN each — verify) at designated hub/nacelle points
Rope protectors on edges, Level 3 supervisor on site, rescue plan with pre-rigged system
Platforms (BAP) per EN 1808 with wire ropes, secondary brakes, daily checks and 12-monthly thorough examination

Weather window: wind ≤ 10–12 m/s (verify OEM/IRATA), no rain, no lightning within alert radius, temperature within resin cure limits; forecast checked and monitored continuously (see weather procedure)
Composite controls: LEV/vacuum-shrouded grinders, FFP3 or PAPR, disposable coveralls, nitrile gloves, eye protection
Resin SDS, skin-care programme; heating blankets with thermostats and fire extinguisher; waste in sealed bags
Blade interior entry: permit, two persons (one at root/hub), gas test if solvents used, forced ventilation, lighting, lifeline inside, maximum entry distance per OEM, communication
Drone inspection preferred for external survey (Drone Rules 2021 registration, pilot certificate, airspace)
steps: Day plan: weather check, rotor lock and isolation completed and recorded, anchor inspection, rope/platform pre-use checks, ground exclusion zone (radius ≥ blade length — verify) with signage and spotter, radio check.
Rigging: rig working and safety lines to separate anchors, protect ropes at hub/nacelle edges and blade root, verify knots/devices by second technician; lower repair kit by haul line, not carried.
Descent to work zone: continuous monitoring of wind; use positioning aids to stay off blade edge; tools and pots tethered; no loose items.
Repair: grind with LEV and PAPR; mix resin in measured kits, apply within pot life, heating blanket set and monitored; solvent use minimal with vapour control; collect dust and waste in bags.
Platform work: load within SWL, persons harnessed to independent lifeline, no leaning out, stop in gusts; emergency lowering procedure known.
Communication: ground spotter watches weather and traffic, calls 'stop' on gusts/lightning/vehicles; technicians report every 30 min.
Internal blade: ventilate, test atmosphere, enter with lifeline and attendant; grind/sand with extraction; limit continuous time (heat); exit before resin curing fumes build.
Lightning alert: suspend work, ascend/descend to safe position, leave turbine per weather procedure; after a strike on turbine, inspect lightning protection system before further work.
End of day: inventory of tools, remove ropes/platform, release rotor lock per nacelle procedure, clear exclusion zone, dispose waste per HOWM, log hours and observations.
Health: medical fitness for rope access (yearly), skin checks for sensitisation, respiratory surveillance; drone ops logged per DGCA.
ppe: Rope-access harness (EN 813/361) and devices, helmet, gloves, FFP3/PAPR, disposable coveralls (Type 5/6), nitrile gloves, goggles/face shield, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves for blankets, headlamp
stop: Rotor/pitch lock not verified for blade in work position
Wind, rain or lightning outside limits
Anchor or rope inspection not current / single-rope working
Working inside blade alone or without ventilation and attendant
Exclusion zone not maintained below work
records: IRATA/SPRAT certificates and logbooks, anchor and rope inspection records, platform examinations, weather logs
Permits (blade interior), resin/solvent SDS and exposure records, dropped-object log, drone flight logs, waste manifests

t: Lightning, Wind & Weather Windows for Turbine Work
purpose: Define go/no-go weather criteria and monitoring so that climbing, nacelle, hub, roof, blade, crane and electrical work on wind and solar sites stops before lightning, high wind, heavy rain, heat or cyclone conditions make it unsafe.
scope: All work at wind farms (towers, blades, cranes, substations) and solar parks (rooftop and ground-mount) in India's monsoon, pre-monsoon thunderstorm, cyclone and heat seasons; weather monitoring tools, alerts and stop-work authority.
roles: Control room / SCADA operator (met mast, lightning service)
hazards: Lightning: turbines and towers are strike points; strike while climbing, in nacelle, on roof or blade can be fatal
Induced voltages on structures and cables; storms build fast in pre-monsoon (Apr–Jun) and north-east monsoon (Oct–Dec) in TN
Wind: gusts throw technicians on roofs/blades, make lock engagement unsafe, overturn cranes and lifted modules; wind shear; dust storms reducing visibility
Rain/monsoon: slippery ladders and roofs, flooding of tower bases/cable trenches, electrical faults, lightning; cyclones on TN/AP/Gujarat coasts
Heat: tower interiors 45–50 °C, solar fields 45 °C+ with radiant load; cold at hub height in winter in north
pre: Weather limits table per OEM/site (verify each): climbing ≤ 20 m/s (10-min mean); rotor-lock engagement ≤ 12–15 m/s; nacelle roof/spinner external ≤ 12 m/s
Blade rope/platform work ≤ 10 m/s; crane lifts per load chart (often ≤ 9–10 m/s, lower for modules/blades); PV module handling ≤ 10 m/s
Lightning policy: alert when lightning within 30 km (prepare, finish task, pack)
Stop and evacuate turbine/roof when within 15 km (verify radii) or thunder heard (30/30 rule: flash-to-bang ≤ 30 s), resume 30 min after last strike within radius
Sources: IMD nowcasts, lightning-detection subscription, SCADA met mast, Damini app
Monitoring: control room watches met mast wind/gusts and lightning feed and radios all teams; each lead carries anemometer and lightning app; site weather board updated each morning and after changes
Shelter: vehicles (not under turbines or lines), substation control building; no shelter under trees or at tower base in the open; cyclone season plan with evacuation triggers from IMD warnings
Heat plan: WBGT-based schedule, shaded rest, water/ORS, early starts; monsoon plan: drainage of tower bases/inverter stations, cable trench inspections, slip controls, RCD tests
steps: Morning brief: review IMD forecast, lightning outlook, wind forecast at hub height, heat index; set work plan and no-go times; record on weather board; brief all teams.
Before each task: lead checks live wind and lightning status against the task limit; log go decision; control room acknowledges team location.
Continuous monitoring: control room alerts any team when wind trend approaches limit (e.g. 80% of limit) or lightning enters 30 km; teams respond and prepare to secure work.
Lightning 15 km / thunder heard: stop, secure tools, descend/evacuate turbine or roof immediately (do not finish tasks), move to vehicles/control building
Do not touch tower, fences or cables during storm; headcount by radio.

Wind over limit: stop task-specific work (roof, blade, lift) first; if climb limit exceeded, no ascents — teams aloft decide to descend while within limit or shelter in nacelle (OEM guidance) and inform control.
Rain: suspend roof/blade/external work, PV module work and open-panel electrical work; check tower-base water ingress; resume only when surfaces dry.
Heat: enforce rest schedule; suspend climbing at WBGT above action level in afternoon; watch for heat illness; hydrate.
Cyclone/red alert: secure site (crane booms down, loose material, modules), evacuate non-essential staff per IMD timeline, turbines in storm mode, communication plan with HQ.
After event: inspect lightning protection (LPS continuity, receptor damage), flooded areas, electrical insulation before re-energising/re-climbing; record strike events.
Review monthly: weather stop events, near misses, forecast accuracy; update limits with OEM; refresher briefing before pre-monsoon and NE-monsoon seasons.
ppe: Standard site PPE; rain gear with grip soles for monsoon; sun protection (hat under helmet brim, long sleeves), cooling towels; no metal umbrellas in storms
stop: Lightning within stop radius or thunder heard
Wind above task limit or gusting erratically
Heavy rain or standing water on work surfaces
WBGT above stop level for strenuous tasks
Communication with control room lost
records: Daily weather board/log, lightning alerts and stop events, wind readings at task start, LPS inspection after strikes, heat-stress logs, cyclone preparedness checklists, near-miss reports

india: OSH Code s.6 & Central Rules 2026; IMD warnings and nowcasts; NDMA Guidelines on Lightning Safety & Heat Wave; IS/IEC 62305 (lightning protection), IEC 61400-24; CEA 2023; BOCW rules (weather stoppage during erection)
ka: KSNDMC weather/lightning alerts; Karnataka Heat Action Plan; Karnataka OSH draft rules
tn: TNSDMA; IMD Chennai RMC; TN Heat Wave guidelines; NE monsoon and cyclone protocols (Thoothukudi/Tirunelveli wind zones)
osha: OSHA Lightning Safety Fact Sheet (30/30, 30 min); 1926.1431/1926.1417 (crane wind limits), 1926 Subpart M; OSHA Heat NEP
intl: IEC 61400-1 (design wind classes), IEC 61400-24 (lightning); GWO/RenewableUK weather guidance; NOAA/NWS lightning safety; ISO 7243 (WBGT); BS 7121 (crane wind limits)

t: Remote-Site Emergency Response (Wind & Solar Parks)
purpose: Ensure that serious injuries, electrical and HV incidents, snakebite, heat stroke, road accidents and fires at remote renewable-energy sites get first aid, extraction and definitive care despite distances of 30–100 km to hospitals.
scope: Wind farms and solar parks spread over 10–100 km², pooling substations, access roads, O&M bases, camps; day and night operations; contractor crews; emergencies: trauma, electrical burns/arrest, falls, heat illness, snakebite, vehicle accidents, fire, flood, lost or missing persons.
roles: Local hospital, 108 ambulance, fire station, police (pre-briefed)
hazards: Golden hour lost: ambulance 45–90 min away, rural roads, no signage to turbine locations; mobile dead zones inside towers and valleys
Electrical: HT (33/110 kV) switchyard incidents, arc burns, DC arc on solar; cardiac arrest needing AED within minutes
Environment: snakebite (Russell's viper, cobra, krait, saw-scaled viper), scorpion sting, heat stroke, dust storms, flash floods crossing causeways, wildlife
Road accidents on site/public roads (the leading fatality cause in renewable O&M), lone working, night call-outs; fire in inverter stations/transformers; theft/security incidents
pre: Emergency plan with maps: GPS/plus-code of every WTG, inverter station and gate
Road map with distances/times to primary and secondary hospitals (verify 24×7 trauma, ASV availability); ambulance meeting points; posted in vehicles and control room
Communication: VHF/UHF radio network covering site (incl. tower interiors via repeaters), satellite phone at control room for dead zones, mobile coverage map, check-in protocol (every 60 min
Lone working prohibited for HT, height and confined tasks)
Medical: first-aid responders (16-h course or GWO First Aid) on every crew, AED in each O&M vehicle or at least one per cluster (verify)
Trauma kits (tourniquet, dressings, splints, burn gel), stretcher/basket, oxygen where trained
Snakebite kit (pressure-immobilisation bandage; no cutting/sucking/tourniquet) and tie-up with hospital stocking anti-snake venom

Vehicles: fit-for-purpose 4×4 with seat belts, first-aid kit, fire extinguisher, tow rope, torch; drivers trained and rested; journey management for night call-outs; speed limits on site roads; causeway depth gauges
Fire: extinguishers in inverter stations, transformers and vehicles; fire breaks/vegetation control; grass-fire plan; local fire station contact; MSIHC/CEA incident reporting matrix
steps: Alert: anyone sees an emergency → radio/phone control room with location (asset ID), nature, casualties; control room starts incident log and alerts site manager and ERT.
Control room: call 108/ambulance and police/fire as needed, give GPS and meeting point, dispatch site vehicle to guide ambulance from the highway; send nearest first-aid responders with AED.

Scene: make safe (isolate electrical supply via control/HT authorised person, stop traffic, lightning/wind check), then first aid; CPR/AED for cardiac arrest; burns cooled; spinal precautions for falls.
Snakebite: calm and immobilise limb, pressure-immobilisation bandage, remove jewellery, note time and snake if seen (photo), transport fast to ASV hospital; no incision, suction or tourniquet.
Heat stroke: move to shade/AC vehicle, cool aggressively (water, fans, ice packs to neck/armpits/groin), hospital.
Transport decision: site vehicle to hospital may be faster than waiting — decide by condition and ETA; responder accompanies; control room informs hospital in advance.
Fire: evacuate, isolate electrical source if safe, fight only small fires; grass fire — fire breaks, wet lines, call fire service; transformer/inverter fire — keep distance, HT isolated.
Missing person/lost contact: last known location, radio call, vehicle search by grid, check tower logs; escalate after 30 min.
Reporting: statutory notices (OSH Code/BOCW/CEA accident report within 48 h; police for fatal), client/HQ notification, family liaison, investigation.

Readiness: monthly AED/kit checks, quarterly drills (one scenario each: trauma at hub height, electrical arrest, snakebite, vehicle crash), annual joint drill with ambulance and fire service; review routes after road changes.
ppe: First-aid gloves, CPR face shield, hi-vis for scene control, torch; standard site PPE; snake gaiters for vegetation work
stop: Control room unmanned or radio network down
Crew without certified first-aider or AED access
Lone working on HT, height or confined tasks
Night work without journey management and vehicle checks
Route to hospital blocked (flood) without alternative
records: Emergency plan and maps, hospital/ambulance agreements, responder certificates, AED and kit inspection logs, radio checks, journey logs, drill reports, incident logs and statutory notices

india: OSH Code s.6, s.23 (welfare/first aid) & Central Rules 2026 (ambulance/first aid thresholds); BOCW rules (first aid, ambulance ≥ 500 workers — verify)
CEA Safety Regulations 2023 (accident reporting 48 h); MoHFW National Snakebite Management Protocol & NAPSE 2024; NDMA heat/lightning guidelines; MV Act (site vehicles)
ka: Arogya Kavacha 108; KSFES district stations; Karnataka OSH draft rules; district hospitals near Chitradurga/Gadag/Pavagada wind-solar zones
tn: 108 GVK EMRI; TNFRS; TN BOCW Rules; GH Tirunelveli/Thoothukudi/Udumalpet near wind zones (verify ASV stock)
osha: 1910.151 (medical/first aid — near proximity), 1910.269(b), 1910.38 (emergency action plans), 1926.50; ANSI/ISEA Z308.1 (first-aid kits)
intl: GWO First Aid standard; ISO 45001 cl. 8.2 (emergency preparedness); WHO snakebite guidelines (SE Asia); ERC/AHA resuscitation guidelines; UK HSE L74 (first aid); IRATA rescue provisions

t: Solar PV DC Systems – Shock, Arc Flash & Safe Isolation (Rooftop & Utility)
purpose: Prevent electric shock, DC arc-flash burns and fires from PV strings, combiner boxes, inverters and DC cabling that remain live whenever there is light, during installation, commissioning, O&M and fault-finding.
scope: Rooftop (10 kW–5 MW) and utility-scale (1–500 MW) PV: modules, strings (600–1,500 V DC), DC cables and connectors, SCBs/combiner boxes, string and central inverters, DC isolators, earthing and SPDs, trackers; cleaning and vegetation work near live DC; inverter rooms/stations.
hazards: Strings cannot be switched off at the module: 1,000–1,500 V DC present in daylight; shock on touching damaged cables/connectors or during connector mating under load

DC arc: no current zero — arcs sustain at low current; arc flash when opening isolators or connectors under load, loose terminations, water ingress in SCBs; fires in combiner boxes and at MC4 mismatches
Ground faults energising frames/trackers; back-feed from inverter/battery; AC side 415 V–33 kV; capacitor energy in inverters after shutdown
Heat on roofs/fields (module surface 60–70 °C), glare, dehydration; tracker motion (pinch) during maintenance; cable trench collapses; snakes under modules
pre: Design per IS/IEC 60364-7-712, IEC 62446-1 and CEA 2023: DC isolators (load-break rated) at string/array and inverter, labelled; 'live in daylight' warning labels on all DC enclosures; SPDs

Earthing of frames; cable routing with UV/rodent protection; firefighter isolation/rapid-shutdown signage; CEIG approval before energising installations above thresholds (verify ≥ 650 V or capacity-based)
Only authorised electrical persons work on DC; PV-specific training (DC isolation, arc-flash, connector practice)

Insulated tools (IEC 60900 1,000 V), Class 0 gloves (verify for 1,500 V — Class 00/0 ratings), arc-rated face shield and clothing (DC arc assessment per NFPA 70E/IEEE 1584 methods); CAT III 1,500 V meters
Written isolation procedure: open AC breaker, open DC isolators, wait inverter capacitor discharge (per OEM ≥ 5 min — verify)
Test string polarity/voltage, use opaque module covers for work on connectors where strings cannot be isolated, never disconnect connectors under load

Thermography programme (IR) for SCBs, inverters and connectors; insulation-resistance and earth-continuity tests per IEC 62446 at commissioning and periodically; SCB covers sealed (IP65), no water ingress
Permit (Electrical) for DC work; LOTO for inverters/trackers; roof/field work per fragile-roof and heat procedures; vegetation and cleaning crews briefed not to touch cables/enclosures
steps: Plan: identify strings/equipment, obtain Electrical PTW, confirm isolation points on single-line diagram, check weather (no rain/lightning), tools and PPE inspected.

Isolate: open AC breaker and lock; open DC isolators at inverter and SCB; wait discharge time; verify absence of voltage at work point with proven meter (test on live source before and after); apply lock and tag.

If a string cannot be isolated (connector work): cover modules with opaque covers to drop voltage, measure, work with insulated gloves/tools, never open a connector carrying current (check with clamp meter first).
Connector practice: use matching make/model connectors only, torque per OEM, crimp with correct tooling; replace burnt/discoloured connectors; document.
SCB/inverter inspection: thermography under load from safe distance; open covers only after isolation; check terminations, moisture, rodent damage, SPD indicators; close and seal.
Fault-finding (ground fault/arc-fault alarms): isolate array section, measure IR string by string; do not reset arc-fault trips without finding cause.
Re-energise: remove tools, verify polarity, close DC isolators string by string, then AC; check inverter start and alarms; remove locks; record.

Cleaning crews: water cleaning only when arrays isolated or per OEM for live washing with demineralised water and insulated lances; no pressure jets on connectors/enclosures; dawn/dusk schedule for heat.
Fire: isolate AC and DC where safe, inform fire service that DC remains live in daylight — no cutting cables; CO2/DCP on electrical fires; keep distance from arcing SCBs.
Records: commissioning tests (IEC 62446), PTW/LOTO, thermography reports, connector replacements, ground-fault investigations, incidents (electrical accidents to CEIG within 48 h).
ppe: Insulated gloves (Class 0; verify 1,500 V) with leather protectors, arc-rated face shield and clothing per assessment, insulated tools, safety glasses, non-conductive helmet, EH-rated boots, module covers
Sun protection and water
stop: Voltage not verified absent at work point / meter not proven
Connector disconnected under load
Working on DC without Electrical PTW or alone
Rain or lightning during open-enclosure work
SCB or inverter enclosure with water ingress or burnt smell energised
records: Electrical PTW/LOTO records, test-before-touch logs, IEC 62446 test reports, thermography, connector/SPD replacement log, authorisations and training, CEIG approvals, electrical accident reports

india: CEA Safety Regulations 2023 (incl. renewable/DC installations, approvals, accident reporting); IS/IEC 60364-7-712; IEC 62446-1
IS 14286 & IS 61730 (modules, QCO); IS 16221 / IEC 62109 (inverters); IS 3043 (earthing); IS/IEC 62305 (lightning); IS 5216; MNRE/BIS ALMM; OSH Code s.6
ka: CEIG Karnataka approval & periodic inspection; KREDL/BESCOM net-metering safety; Pavagada solar park EHS rules (verify)
tn: CEIG Tamil Nadu; TANGEDCO/TEDA interconnection safety; Kamuthi/Ramanathapuram solar park procedures (verify)
osha: 1910.333–335, 1910.269 (generation), 1926 Subpart K; NFPA 70 Art. 690/691 (PV, rapid shutdown), NFPA 70E (DC arc flash), NEC 2023; IEEE 1584 (DC methods — verify)
intl: IEC 62446-1/-2 (testing, maintenance), IEC 61730 (module safety), IEC 60364-7-712; UK IET Code of Practice for Grid-Connected Solar PV; UK HSE PV guidance; EN 50110-1; SEIA/SolarPower Europe O&M best practice

t: Rooftop PV on Industrial Sheds – Fragile Roofs, Edge Falls & Module Handling
purpose: Prevent falls through fragile roof sheets and skylights, falls from roof edges and ladders, and injuries from module handling and lifting during rooftop solar installation, cleaning and maintenance.
scope: Industrial and warehouse sheds with asbestos-cement, fibre-cement, metal (GI/aluminium) and polycarbonate sheets and skylights; RCC roofs with parapets < 1 m; access ladders and hatches; module lifting by crane, hoist or manual; cleaning and O&M visits.
hazards: Fragile roofs: AC/fibre-cement sheets, rusted metal, rooflights — give way without warning under a person's weight; falls 6–12 m onto concrete/machines; asbestos fibres when cutting/drilling AC sheets
Edge falls: no parapet or parapet < 1 m, open eaves, gable ends; ladder falls at access; falls through hatches; wind pushing persons/modules
Module handling: 20–35 kg modules in wind, cut hands, dropped modules onto people below; crane/hoist lifts over occupied buildings; overhead power lines near sheds
Heat (roof surface 60–70 °C), glare, dehydration; slippery wet/mossy sheets in monsoon; lightning; snakes/birds' nests
pre: Roof survey before any work: sheet type and condition, fragile areas and rooflights marked on drawing, structural capacity for crawl boards/walkways and PV load, parapet heights, anchor options, overhead lines
Owner's information; AC sheets treated as asbestos-containing — no cutting/drilling without wet methods and asbestos controls (preferably avoid penetration; use clamps on purlins)
Fall protection plan (hierarchy): avoid roof access where possible (drone surveys, ground-level pre-assembly)
Collective protection — edge guardrails (EN 13374), safety nets below fragile roofs (IS 11057/EN 1263), covered/caged rooflights, walkways/crawl boards spreading load across purlins
Where not possible — horizontal lifelines (EN 795 type C) or anchors tested to design load and harness with twin lanyards; ladders secured and extending 1 m above landing
Work-at-height permit; weather limits (wind ≤ 10 m/s for module handling — verify; no work in rain/lightning)
Exclusion zones below work and lifts; power-line clearance; rescue plan (casualty suspended or on roof) with equipment on site

Module lifting: crane/hoist with lift plan and certified gear, module pallets secured, tag lines, lift away from occupied areas or with building evacuated below; manual carrying by two persons with gloves on walkways only
Heat and welfare: early/late schedules, shaded rest at ground, water; first aid; asbestos awareness training where AC sheets present; HOWM disposal for AC debris
steps: Pre-start: review roof survey, permit, weather, anchors/guardrails in place, rooflights covered, walkways laid, exclusion zones set, rescue kit present; toolbox talk on fragile areas.
Access: secured ladder/stair tower or scaffold access; attach to lifeline/anchor before leaving ladder; hatch covers closed after passing.
Movement: only on walkways/crawl boards over purlins or on marked safe zones; never step on sheets between boards or on rooflights; no running; stay clipped on when outside guardrails.
Fixing structure: clamps on purlins/standing seams preferred; if drilling AC sheets unavoidable — wet drilling, FFP3, bag debris, no abrasive cutting; metal sheets — cut edges deburred, gloves.
Module handling: two persons, gloves, carry edge-on into wind; stack on rated frames; secure against wind at end of shift; lifting over roof edge with hoist and tag lines, no one under load.
Cabling and connectors: see solar DC procedure; route away from walkways; protect from sheet edges.
Cleaning/O&M visits: same access and fall-protection rules apply even for 10-minute jobs; check anchors/lifelines before use; water from ground-fed lances where possible.
Weather: stop module handling at wind limit, all roof work in rain/lightning; dry wet sheets before access; monsoon moss removal.
End of shift: remove loose items, secure modules, close hatches, check guardrails for next day; report damaged sheets to owner immediately and barricade below.
Records: roof survey, permits, anchor tests, equipment inspections, asbestos records (where applicable), near misses; review after any sheet breakage.
ppe: Full-body harness with twin lanyards, helmet with chin strap, soft-soled grip boots, cut-resistant gloves, safety glasses/tinted, FFP3 for AC sheet work, sun protection, hi-vis
stop: Fragile sheet/rooflight not protected and no walkway/net/lifeline
Worker on roof unattached beyond guardrails
Wind, rain or lightning beyond limits
Lift over occupied area without evacuation/exclusion
AC sheets cut or drilled dry
records: Roof condition survey, WAH permits, anchor/lifeline test certificates, PPE and net/guardrail inspections, lift plans and crane certificates, weather log, asbestos work records, incident and near-miss reports

india: OSH Code s.6 & Central Rules 2026; BOCW Central/state rules (work at height, fragile roofs, ladders, nets); IS 3521 (harness), IS 11057 & IS 5175 (nets), IS 3696 (scaffolds/ladders), IS 15298
HOWM Rules & asbestos provisions (state rules dangerous-operations schedule — asbestos); CEA 2023; MNRE rooftop guidelines
ka: Karnataka BOCW Rules 2006 (height work, fragile roofs — verify rule numbers); BBMP/GBA building permissions for rooftop PV loads; KSFES
tn: TN BOCW Rules 2006 (amended 2025); CMDA/DTCP structural-stability certificate for rooftop PV (verify); TNFRS
osha: 1926.501(b)(4) (holes/skylights), 1926.502, 1926 Subpart M & X (ladders), 1926.1101 (asbestos), 1926.1400 (cranes); ANSI/ASSP Z359
intl: UK HSE HSG33 (health and safety in roof work — fragile roofs), INDG284, Work at Height Regs 2005
EN 13374 (edge protection), EN 1263 (nets), EN 795; ACR[M]001 (fragile roofs test); Control of Asbestos Regs 2012 (UK) as benchmark

t: Battery Energy Storage Systems (Utility & C&I) – Commissioning, O&M & Fire Response
purpose: Prevent thermal runaway, explosion from accumulated off-gas, electric shock and arc flash in containerised and building-mounted lithium-ion BESS (LFP/NMC) from 100 kWh to GWh scale co-located with solar/wind or at substations.
scope: Containerised and enclosure BESS, battery buildings, PCS/inverters, DC bus (1,000–1,500 V), BMS/EMS, HVAC/thermal management, gas detection and suppression, deflagration venting; delivery, installation, commissioning, energisation, O&M, module replacement, decommissioning.
roles: Fire officer / local fire service liaison
hazards: Thermal runaway in one cell propagating through module/rack; off-gases (H2, CO, hydrocarbons, HF) accumulate in sealed enclosure — deflagration/explosion when door opened or ignition occurs (Surprise, Arizona 2019 benchmark)
DC 1,500 V and AC MV: shock, arc flash on racks/combiners, pre-charge faults, reverse polarity during commissioning; stored energy cannot be switched off — only isolated
Suppression limitations: clean agents stop flame but not runaway; water needed in large volume; re-ignition for days; HF in runoff; container entry after event
Installation: 30–40 t container lifts, trench and cable work, heat; HVAC failure causing over-temperature; coolant leaks (liquid-cooled); rodents
pre: Design per NFPA 855 / IEC 62933-5-2 / UL 9540 benchmark with UL 9540A test data: separation distances (≥ 3 m between units, ≥ 15 m to exposures/occupied buildings or fire-rated barriers — verify)

Explosion control (deflagration vents NFPA 68 or exhaust ventilation NFPA 69), gas detection (H2/CO/VOC) with ventilation and alarm, smoke/heat detection, suppression as per OEM, BMS trips, thermal management redundancy

Approvals: CEIG approval before energisation (CEA 2023), Fire NOC with BESS-specific conditions, Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 EPR, BIS/IS 16046/IEC 62619 cell certification; grid code and protection studies
Emergency Response Plan (ERP) agreed with local fire service: site map, chemistry and kWh per unit, isolation points
'do not open doors during gas alarm' rule, water supply (hydrants/monitors ≥ 2 h — verify), runoff containment, standoff distances, re-ignition monitoring
Fire service familiarisation visit before energisation

Electrical: arc-flash study for DC racks and PCS, labels, Class 0 gloves/1,500 V tools, remote racking where possible, LOTO procedures per OEM (DC disconnects, rack breakers, pre-charge), test-before-touch; HV PTW for MV side
Commissioning plan: polarity and insulation tests before closing DC, staged energisation, BMS alarm verification, gas-detector and suppression function tests, HVAC proving
O&M schedule: thermography, torque, coolant, filters, detector calibration, firmware under MoC
steps: Receipt/installation: inspect containers for damage and BMS logs during transport; SoC as shipped (≤ 30–50%)
Lift with certified crane and rated lifting points; ground and bond; keep doors closed; no hot work within 15 m without permit.
Commissioning: verify DC polarity and IR string by string, pre-charge sequence per OEM, close rack breakers one at a time monitoring BMS
Test gas detection, ventilation, suppression (simulated), e-stops and remote trips before first charge cycle.
Energisation: HV PTW, CEIG approval in hand, fire service informed, exclusion zone, two authorised persons; staged charge/discharge with thermal monitoring.
Routine O&M: review BMS/EMS alarms daily (cell voltage/temperature deviation), HVAC performance, detector status
Monthly thermography of busbars and PCS; quarterly detector calibration and suppression inspection; annual torque/IR tests.

Module/rack work: isolate rack (DC disconnect + breaker), wait discharge, verify 0 V at work point, insulated tools and gloves, cover adjacent live parts; two persons; module handling with lifting aids (30–60 kg).
Gas alarm / thermal event: DO NOT open doors
Evacuate to standoff (≥ 50 m — verify), trip PCS and isolate AC remotely, let ventilation/deflagration systems work, call fire service with ERP, monitor remotely (BMS/thermal camera).
Fire response (with fire service): defensive posture, protect exposures, apply water from distance via monitors if required for cooling adjacent units
Contain runoff, no entry until gas readings safe and temperatures stable for 24 h
Expect re-ignition.

Post-event: isolate and quarantine damaged units outdoors, handle debris as hazardous waste, HF-contaminated water to authorised disposal, root-cause investigation with OEM, notify CEIG/fire/SPCB as required.
Changes (firmware, chemistry, layout, HVAC) under MoC with hazard review; annual ERP drill with fire service; training records for all technicians.
Decommissioning: discharge to safe SoC, isolate, remove under OEM procedure, transport as UN 3480, recycle under BWMR 2022 with manifests.
ppe: Arc-rated clothing and face shield per study, Class 0 insulating gloves with protectors, insulated tools, safety glasses, EH boots, hard hat, FFP3; SCBA and chemical suit for ERT post-event; heat gloves
stop: Gas (H2/CO) alarm active — doors must stay closed
DC rack not verified de-energised before work

t: Quay Cranes, Yard Equipment & Container Lashing
purpose: Prevent struck-by, crush, fall and dropped-container incidents in container and bulk terminals involving ship-to-shore cranes, RTGs/RMGs, reach stackers, straddle carriers, internal transfer vehicles and lashing gangs.
scope: STS/quay cranes, mobile harbour cranes, RTG/RMG yard cranes, reach stackers, empty handlers, straddle carriers, terminal tractors, lashing/unlashing on deck and on quay, twistlock handling, reefer monitoring, hatch-cover handling; wind and night operations.
hazards: Persons struck by containers, spreaders, hatch covers or ITVs on quay; working under suspended loads; crane boom/gantry collision with ship or other crane; wind-driven gantry run-away
Lashing: falls from container tops and lashing bridges (> 2.5 m), struck by swinging containers while on deck, lashing rods/turnbuckles (20 kg) dropped, twistlock bins; hand injuries

Yard: reach stacker tip-over with high load, straddle blind spots, RTG wheel crush, pedestrians/truck drivers out of cabs, stack collapse in wind, damaged or over-weight (VGM) containers, hazardous DG containers
Fatigue (12-h shifts, night), heat on steel decks, slips on wet quay/hatch covers, falls into open hatches/between ship and quay
pre: Lifting appliances tested and examined per Dock Workers (Safety, Health & Welfare) Regulations 1990 (under OSH Code): initial and periodic tests, 12-monthly thorough examination, register
Spreader twistlock indicators, load/overload and anti-collision devices, boom limits, gantry anti-collision and storm anchoring
Operators: certification per port/DG Shipping or terminal competency scheme, medical (vision, fitness), simulator/practical assessment; fatigue limits per Dock regs/OSH Code hours
Pedestrian exclusion: no walking on quay operational lanes; marked walkways, lashing platforms/cages for twistlock work, ITV drivers stay in cab under crane
Radio/visual signals; night lighting ≥ 50 lux at work areas (verify)
Wind: operations stop limits (e.g. STS ≥ 20 m/s / 72 km/h — verify terminal limit), stack height reduced and empties secured ahead of cyclone warnings, storm pins; anemometers on cranes with alarms
Container integrity: CSC plates, VGM verification, damaged boxes isolated; DG per IMDG and port DG rules; reefer plugs/unplug with gloves and insulated tools
steps: Shift start: crane pre-use checks (brakes, limits, spreader, anti-collision, wind alarm, lights), yard equipment daily checks, radio check, lashing gear inspection; defects tagged out.
Vessel planning: stow plan reviewed for DG, over-height/out-of-gauge, hatch sequence; lashing gang briefed on bays, cell guides, falls from height and exclusion zones.
Hatch covers: lifted only with crane in correct mode, no persons on deck in swing path, placed on marked quay areas with barricades.
Container lifts: operator confirms twistlocks locked (indicators), lifts clear of cell guides, no person within 10 m on quay; ITV driver in cab; load not passed over people.
Lashing: use lashing platforms/cages; never climb container stacks or work on top without edge protection/fall arrest; handle rods in pairs; twistlocks to bins; stop when crane works adjacent bay.
Yard: speed limits (≤ 25 km/h ITV

≤ 10 km/h near pedestrians — verify), reach stackers lift at height only with stable load and no slope, straddle paths segregated, truck drivers stay in cab at interchange or in marked zone; RTG wheel-turn alarms.
Wind rising: TOS control monitors; at pre-alarm stop high stacking and lashing on top tiers; at limit stop crane operations, stow booms, pin gantries, secure stacks.
Damaged/leaking container: isolate, identify contents (UN number/DGD), DG procedure; over-weight → re-weigh, do not lift until verified.
Incidents: stop operations in zone, treat casualty, preserve scene, notify port authority/Dock Safety Inspector and police as applicable (fatal/ dangerous occurrence) within statutory time.
Weekly: lashing-gear inspection, walkway/lighting audit, near-miss review; annual: thorough examination of cranes and spreaders, operator refresher and medical.
ppe: Helmet with chin strap, hi-vis, safety boots, gloves (impact-rated for lashing), safety glasses, harness where fall-arrest used on container tops/bridges, lifejacket near open water edges, hearing protection in engine areas
stop: Person on quay/deck within crane working radius or under load
Wind above terminal limit or anemometer failed
Twistlock indicator fault or spreader not locked
Lashing on container tops without platform/fall arrest
Crane examination overdue or safety device bypassed
records: Lifting appliance register and test/examination certificates, operator certificates and medicals, daily equipment checks
Lashing-gear inspections, wind logs and stop events, DG container register, incident/dangerous-occurrence notices, near-miss log

india: Dock Workers (Safety, Health and Welfare) Act 1986 & Regulations 1990 (now under OSH Code Ch. on dock work; DGFASLI Dock Safety Inspectorate); OSH Code 2020 & Central Rules 2026
Major Port Authorities Act 2021 & port regulations; IS 3177/IS 807 (crane design), IS 13367; MV Act (terminal tractors on public roads); IMDG via Merchant Shipping Act/DG Shipping circulars
ka: New Mangalore Port Authority / Karwar port regulations; Karnataka Maritime Board; DGFASLI Mangalore inspectorate (verify)
tn: Chennai, Kamarajar (Ennore), V.O. Chidambaranar (Thoothukudi) Port regulations; TN Maritime Board; DGFASLI Chennai inspectorate
osha: 29 CFR 1917 (marine terminals — 1917.45 cranes, 1917.71 terminal lifting, 1917.112 guarding), 1918 (longshoring — 1918.85 containerised cargo), 1910.179; ANSI B30.2/B30.4
intl: ILO Code of Practice 'Safety and Health in Ports' (2016), ILO C152; PEMA/ICHCA safety briefings (lashing, twistlocks, wind); BS 7121 Pt 1/14; IMO CSC 1972; SOLAS VI/2 (VGM); FEM/ISO 4306 crane standards

t: Ship Hold & Enclosed-Space Entry – Oxygen Depletion, Fumigants & Bulk Cargoes
purpose: Prevent deaths of stevedores, surveyors and crew entering cargo holds, tanks and adjacent spaces with oxygen-deficient, toxic or flammable atmospheres, and injuries from hold ladders, grabs and mobile plant in holds.
scope: Bulk carriers and general cargo ships at berth or anchorage (coal, ore, DRI, grain, fertiliser, sulphur, logs, wood pellets, steel turnings), fumigated cargoes, container holds, tanker and barge spaces; hold ladders, hatch coamings, dozers and grabs in holds.
roles: Ship's master and officers (enclosed-space procedures, SOLAS)
hazards: O2 depletion by cargo oxidation/respiration (coal, DRI, steel turnings, grain, logs, wood pellets, copra); CO from wood pellets/coal self-heating
CH4 from coal; H2 from DRI contact with water; dust; adjacent spaces (stools, ducts, store rooms) sharing atmosphere

Fumigants: phosphine (AlP tablets/sachets in grain — TLV 0.05 ppm ACGIH; OSHA PEL 0.3 ppm) persists in cargo and adjacent spaces; methyl bromide, sulfuryl fluoride; 'fumigated in transit' cargoes under IMO recommendations
Falls from vertical hold ladders (20–25 m), hatch coamings, open hatches, into hoppers; struck by grab/bulldozer
Cargo shifting/slides (iron ore fines, bauxite liquefaction), sulphur dust explosion, ammonium nitrate decomposition; heat 45 °C+ in holds
Rescue fatalities: would-be rescuers entering without SCBA are a large share of enclosed-space deaths (IMO data)
pre: Every hold/tank/adjacent space is an enclosed space until proven otherwise: master's enclosed-space entry permit (SOLAS XI-1/7 — ship carries calibrated multi-gas detector) plus stevedore permit
Atmosphere tested at several levels (O2 20.9%, LEL < 1% / 10% for work, CO < 25 ppm, H2S < 5 ppm, PH3 < 0.3 ppm — verify) before and during entry; ventilation ≥ 2 air changes before test (verify)
Fumigated cargo: fumigator's gas-free certificate for holds and adjacent spaces, placards removed only after clearance
Residual-fumigant check before stevedore entry and daily; no entry during 'in-transit' fumigation; disposal of spent AlP residues by licensed fumigator

Access: ladders inspected by officer, rest platforms, safety harness and fall arrester on Australian ladders where fitted, lighting, hatch coaming guardrails or exclusion, lifelines/retrieval for vertical access
One person on ladder at a time
Mobile plant in holds: CO monitoring with diesel equipment, exhaust scrubbers/ventilation, no persons in hold while grab working or dozer moving (except in protected cage), trimming hatch sequence
Cargo-specific IMSBC Code precautions (self-heating, liquefaction, dust)
Rescue: SCBA sets at hatch (≥ 2), rescue harness/tripod/stretcher, attendant at hatch with communication to crane/ship; ship-shore emergency plan; medical oxygen; never enter to rescue without SCBA
steps: Before gangs board: ship-shore meeting — cargo type and IMSBC hazards, fumigation status, hold ventilation status, enclosed-space permits, emergency contacts; agree exclusion and signalling.

Ventilate hold (open hatches, fans) and test atmosphere from the top at three depths with calibrated detector; record; if any reading fails — continue ventilation and re-test; no entry on smell/visual judgement.
Issue permit (ship and stevedore), post attendant, log entrants; entrants carry personal 4-gas monitors; continuous monitoring in deep holds and whenever cargo disturbed.
Descend hold ladder one at a time, three points of contact, harness/arrester where fitted, tools on hoist line; rest at platforms; no descent during grab/dozer operation.

Work in hold: stay out of grab swing and dozer path; exit before grab resumes; dust control (water sprays for coal/ore where allowed); hydrate and rotate for heat; report dizziness/headache immediately (CO/O2).
Adjacent spaces (stool, duct keel, store rooms): separate test and permit — toxic gases migrate from fumigated or self-heating cargo.
Fumigated holds: wait for fumigator clearance; check PH3 at cargo surface and in pockets; treat tablet residues/sachets as hazardous; stop and exit if detector alarms.
Emergency in hold: attendant raises alarm (ship's whistle/ radio), never enters; rescue team in SCBA with lifelines
Casualty hoisted in rescue harness/stretcher by crane; oxygen and medical evacuation; notify Dock Safety Inspector.
Hot work or repair in holds/tanks: ship's hot-work permit, gas-free certificate, fire watch; tank entry per tank-cleaning procedure.
Records: permits, gas logs, fumigation certificates, ladder inspections, incident reports; weekly review of readings and near misses with ship agents and stevedore foremen.
ppe: Helmet, boots, gloves, personal multi-gas monitor, dust respirator (FFP3) for bulk cargo, goggles, harness/fall arrester on vertical ladders, hi-vis; SCBA for rescue team; chemical PPE for fumigant residues
stop: Atmosphere not tested or outside limits
Fumigated cargo without gas-free certificate
Attendant or rescue SCBA not at hatch
Grab or dozer operating with persons in hold
Hold ladder damaged or coaming unguarded
records: Enclosed-space entry permits (ship and shore), gas-test logs, calibration records, fumigation/gas-free certificates
Ladder and hatch inspections, entrant logs, rescue equipment checks, drill records, incident/dangerous-occurrence notices

india: Dock Workers (Safety, Health & Welfare) Regulations 1990 (entry into holds/enclosed spaces, ladders, mobile plant in holds — verify regs); OSH Code 2020
Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (verify — replaces 1958) & DG Shipping circulars on enclosed-space entry; Insecticides Act 1968 & PPQS fumigation accreditation (AlP); IMSBC Code adoption; Port DG rules
ka: New Mangalore Port (coal/iron ore handling) regulations; DGFASLI Dock Safety Mangalore
tn: Kamarajar (coal), V.O. Chidambaranar (coal, fertiliser), Chennai Port regulations; DGFASLI Dock Safety Chennai; TNPCB dust norms at ports
