ILO Code of Practice Ports (2016); ICHCA/InterManager enclosed-space guidance; UK MCA MGN 659

t: Mooring Operations, Snap-Back & Ship–Shore Interface
purpose: Prevent deaths and amputations from parting mooring lines, falls between ship and quay, drowning and gangway incidents during berthing, unberthing, shifting and cargo watch at ports, jetties and SPMs.
scope: Shore mooring gangs and linesmen, mooring boats, bollards and quick-release hooks, ship's mooring decks and winches, gangways/accommodation ladders, ship–shore access control, tugs and pilot transfers, tanker jetties with ESD and breakaway couplings.
roles: Ship's officers and crew (OCIMF MEG4 practices)
hazards: Snap-back: a parting line (synthetic or wire) recoils at high speed across the whole mooring area — the entire deck/quay zone is a potential snap-back zone (MEG4); HMPE lines recoil less but still kill
Bights and tension: standing in or stepping over a bight; hands on drum/bollard while heaving; heaving lines with weighted monkey's fists
Line surge on rising/falling tide, passing ships, swell; bollard failure (overloaded or corroded)
Falls into water between ship and quay (crushed by hull), from quay edge in dark/wet; mooring boat capsizing; gangway without net, unsecured, steep at tidal extremes; no lifejacket
Tankers: hose/arm failure, static, vapour; night, fatigue, poor communication (language), lighting; vehicle traffic on quay during mooring
pre: Mooring plan agreed ship–shore before arrival: number/position of lines, bollard SWL vs line MBL, tidal range, weather (wind/swell limits for berthing/remaining alongside), tug use, communication channel (VHF) and language
Emergency release (quick-release hooks tested)
Linesmen trained (line handling, snap-back awareness, boat safety), fit; minimum team size per line; PPE incl. lifejackets (EN ISO 12402-3 150 N) within 2 m of quay edge or on boats
Quay edge lighting ≥ 20 lux (verify), lifebuoys with lines every 50 m, ladders at intervals for self-rescue
Bollards/hooks inspected and load-tested (periodic — verify), corroded or cracked bollards taken out of service
Snap-back and no-standing zones marked on quay/deck as 'whole area' with warning signs; heaving lines without added weights
Gangway/accommodation ladder: ship's responsibility but shore verifies — safety net rigged, angle ≤ 55° (verify), handrails, secured against surge, lit, lifebuoy at foot, access controlled (ISPS)
Only authorised persons board
Tanker jetties: ESD, breakaway couplings, drift/excursion alarms, ISGOTT ship–shore checklist, mooring tension monitoring where fitted; weather and swell limits for disconnect
steps: Pre-berthing: foreman briefs gang on berth plan, tide, line sequence, snap-back zone rules and stop signals; verify boat, PPE, lighting, bollard condition and quay traffic stopped.
Receiving lines: stand clear of quay edge until line is in reach; never grab a line until it is slack and on the quay; keep clear of bights; one hand for the line, eyes on the ship's winch.

Making fast: eye over bollard in correct sequence (dip the eye when two lines on one bollard), step back out of the line path, signal 'fast' to ship; never stand between line and quay edge or in line of pull.
Heaving/tension: watch for line creaking, strand breaks, kinks; if a line appears over-tensioned or chafing — warn ship and stand well back; do not approach a tensioned line.
Letting go: only on ship's order, with winch slack confirmed; slip eye off bollard and step away; quick-release hooks operated from safe position; keep hands clear of hook jaws.
Mooring boat: coxswain in charge, lifejackets for all, no overloading, keep clear of propeller wash and lines in water, communicate with quay and ship.
Cargo watch alongside: check lines each watch and at tide changes; report slack/tight lines; weather change → extra lines or cease cargo and prepare to depart per plan.
Gangway: verify net and securing each shift; no one on gangway while ship shifts; persons who fall into water → lifebuoy, alarm, boat rescue — never jump in.
Tankers: ISGOTT checklist, ESD test, hose/arm connection with PPE, spill containment, no hot work or phones in zone, continuous watch at manifold.
Incident/near miss (line parted, person in water) reported to port authority; investigate with ship; review mooring plan; annual training refresher and drills (man-overboard, line parting).
ppe: Lifejacket (150 N) near quay edge and in boats, helmet, hi-vis, gloves (not loose), safety boots with grip, eye protection; hearing protection near winches; torch at night
stop: Person in snap-back/line-of-pull zone during tensioning
Bollard SWL below line MBL or bollard damaged
Linesman without lifejacket at quay edge/boat
No communication with ship's mooring officer
Gangway without net or unsecured; weather beyond berth limits
records: Mooring plans and ship–shore agreements, bollard/hook inspection and test records, linesman training, PPE/lifejacket inspections, lighting and lifebuoy checks, gangway checks, incident and near-miss reports, drill records

india: Dock Workers (Safety, Health & Welfare) Regulations 1990 (access to ships, gangways, lifesaving appliances, lighting — verify regs); OSH Code 2020
Indian Ports Act 1908 & Major Port Authorities Act 2021 (port rules on mooring/berthing); Merchant Shipping Act (ship-side duties); IS 13416 Pt 5 / IS 14946 (lifejackets — verify)
ka: New Mangalore Port Authority marine regulations; Karnataka Maritime Board minor ports (Karwar, Belekeri)
tn: Chennai/Kamarajar/VOC Port marine departments; TN Maritime Board (Cuddalore, Nagapattinam); TNFRS marine wing
osha: 29 CFR 1917 (marine terminals — 1917.124 gangways/ladders, 1917.26 first aid/lifesaving, 1917.123 illumination), 1918.22 (gangways); 1926.106 (working over water)
intl: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4, 2018) — snap-back and line management; ISGOTT 6 (tanker ship–shore); ILO Code of Practice Ports (2016)
IMO MSC.1/Circ.1620 (mooring safety); UK MCA Code of Safe Working Practices Ch. 26 (mooring); EN ISO 12402 (lifejackets); PIANC guidelines

t: Dangerous Goods in Containers – IMDG Handling, Fumigated Units & Leak Response
purpose: Prevent fires, explosions, toxic exposures and environmental releases from dangerous goods and fumigated cargo transport units in ports, CFSs, ICDs and warehouses, including mis-declared and leaking containers.
scope: IMDG classes 1–9 in containers and tank containers; DG yards and segregation; stuffing/de-stuffing and customs examination at CFS; fumigated and off-gassing containers; ammonium nitrate, calcium hypochlorite, lithium batteries, charcoal, fish meal; leaking or damaged units.
hazards: Mis-declared or undeclared DG (Tianjin 2015, Beirut 2020 benchmarks): ammonium nitrate stored long-term, calcium hypochlorite self-heating, charcoal/fish meal self-ignition, lithium battery fires, compressed gases
Fumigated containers: phosphine/methyl bromide residue at lethal levels when doors opened; unmarked units
Off-gassing from goods (toluene, formaldehyde, benzene, 1,2-dichloroethane) in CFS de-stuffing — workers overcome on entry
Leaks: corrosives, toxics, flammables from drums/IBCs; incompatible goods in one unit; tank-container valve leaks; reaction with water from firefighting; environmental release to harbour
Fire in stack spreading to adjacent DG; explosives in transit; container-top/door injuries during inspection; heat accelerating decomposition
pre: DG acceptance: Dangerous Goods Declaration, UN number, class, packing group, SDS, placards/marks on all four sides, CSC plate
Port DG rules and MSIHC/Explosives/Ammonium Nitrate Rules compliance; refusal of undeclared/mis-declared units; direct delivery for Class 1 and AN (no storage beyond permitted hours — verify)
Segregation per IMDG Code segregation table in a dedicated DG yard with separation distances, shade for Class 5.1 (calcium hypochlorite ≤ 35 °C — verify)
Away from occupied buildings, drainage containment, fire hydrants/monitors, CCTV, access control, inventory updated in real time with max quantities per class
Fumigated CTUs: IMDG 5.5.2 warning mark (UN 3359 'Fumigated unit'), register of fumigated/ventilated units
De-stuffing only after ventilation (door opening by trained person from side with respirator) and gas test (PH3, MeBr, SF; VOCs) by competent person; licensed fumigator for treatment and clearance
Emergency: port hazmat plan (EmS codes, ERG/CHEMTREC-style data), PPE (Level A/B suits, SCBA), absorbents, neutralisers, overpack drums, spill booms for harbour
Fire service familiar with DG yard; evacuation distances per ERG (e.g. 800 m for AN fire — verify)
Training: IMDG Code Ch. 1.3 training for all DG-handling staff (function-specific), refresher 2 years; customs examiners trained in container-atmosphere hazards
steps: Receipt: verify documents vs placards; check for damage, leaks, odour, heat (IR thermometer), bulging; non-compliant unit → hold area, notify shipper/agent and DG officer.
Placement: TOS/yard plan enforces segregation and quantity limits; Class 1 and AN handled by direct delivery under PESO licence conditions; reefers with DG checked for power.
Daily DG yard round: thermal check of 4.2/5.1 units and lithium battery units, leak/odour check, drainage closed, hydrants clear, inventory reconciled.
Opening any container for examination/de-stuffing: check fumigation register and marks
Crack doors from the side, step back, ventilate ≥ 30–60 min (verify), gas test at breathing height inside before entry; use respirator per reading; never enter a unit with strong odour.
Fumigation on site: licensed fumigator, exclusion zone, placards, gas-tight sealing, exposure period, aeration and clearance certificate before release; residues disposed by fumigator.
Leaking unit: isolate zone (upwind), identify product (UN number/SDS), ERT in appropriate PPE, stop leak/overpack, contain runoff (block drains), decontaminate, dispose as hazardous waste
Notify port authority, SPCB and shipper.
Fire in DG yard: alarm, evacuate per ERG distances, inform fire service of contents (class, UN numbers, quantities)
Isolate adjacent units by removal if safe, no water on water-reactive goods (Class 4.3), avoid runoff to harbour where possible.
Heat/weather: shade and ventilation for 5.1/organic peroxides (5.2 temperature-controlled), cyclone plan to clear DG yard or secure.
Customs/examination staff: no entry to units until atmosphere cleared; forklifts with DG-rated operators; no smoking/phones in DG yard.
Audit monthly: segregation, marks, inventory vs limits, fumigation register, PPE and spill kits, training currency; incidents and refusals reported to port DG committee.
ppe: Standard terminal PPE plus chemical gloves and goggles for DG handling, respirator (ABEK/P3) for container opening, Level A/B suits and SCBA for ERT, face shield; IR thermometer and gas detector as 'PPE' for inspectors
stop: Undeclared/mis-declared DG or missing placards
Fumigated or odorous container opened without ventilation and gas test
Segregation table or quantity limit breached in yard
Ammonium nitrate or explosives stored beyond permitted period/conditions
Leaking or heating unit left in stack
records: DG register and acceptance records (DGD, SDS), yard plan and segregation checks, fumigation register and clearance certificates
Gas-test logs for container opening, daily DG rounds, incident/leak/fire reports, training records (IMDG 1.3), PESO licences

Explosives Rules 2008 & Ammonium Nitrate Rules 2012 (port storage limits, licences)
MSIHC Rules 1989 (storage thresholds); HOWM Rules 2016 (Basel/imports); Insecticides Act 1968 & PPQS (fumigation); Dock Workers Regulations 1990; CTU Code (stuffing)

tn: Chennai/Kamarajar/VOC Port DG rules; TNPCB; PESO Chennai; Customs Chennai CFS examination SOPs

EU/UK fumigated-container guidance (HSE, Dutch Labour Inspectorate studies on off-gassing); IAEA for Class 7

t: Sugar Mills – Cane Yard, Mills, Centrifugals, Bagasse Fire & Sulphur/Lime
purpose: Prevent vehicle and conveyor fatalities in cane yards, entanglement in mills and centrifugals, bagasse and sugar-dust fires/explosions, SO2 and lime burns, and pressure-vessel incidents through the crushing season.
scope: Cane yard and weighbridge traffic, unloaders and cane carriers, knives/shredders, mill tandem, bagasse handling and storage, boilers and co-generation, juice heaters/evaporators/pans, sulphitation and lime, centrifugals, sugar dryers/silos, molasses tanks, ETP; off-season maintenance.
roles: Cane yard controller and traffic marshals
Mill house, boiler (certified attendants) and process operators
Safety officer; fire crew; occupational health
hazards: Cane yard: trolleys overturning/rolling, workers crushed between vehicles, unloader grabs, night fatigue, bullock carts; falls from loaded trolleys; carrier/conveyor nip points and hand-feeding of cane
Mills: roller nips, Donnelly chute/knife/shredder access while running, bagasse carrier entanglement; centrifugals: basket burst (1,000–1,500 rpm), lid opened while spinning, hand in basket
Bagasse: spontaneous heating in stacks and dust explosion in conveyors/boiler bunkers; sparks from boiler chimneys igniting bagasse yard; sugar dust explosions in dryers/graders/silos (St 1)

Sulphur burner SO2 (TLV 0.25 ppm STEL), lime slaking (CaO exothermic, burns), hot juice/syrup/massecuite scalds, evaporator/pan vessel failure, molasses tank CO2/ethanol (confined), boiler incidents, HT switchyard
Seasonal migrant labour untrained
pre: Cane yard traffic plan: one-way flow, marked waiting lanes, speed ≤ 10 km/h, marshals with radios, lighting, separate pedestrian routes, unloading only when driver clear, no riding on loaded trolleys
Weighbridge queue management; cart/bullock separation

Mill house guarding per Factories Act ss.21–22: cane carrier and bagasse conveyor nip guards, pull-wire stops along carriers, interlocked covers on knives/shredders, no hand feeding (Donnelly chute), LOTO for choke clearing
Centrifugals per state schedule — interlocked lid (cannot open until basket stopped), basket inspection/NDT yearly, over-speed trip, vibration monitoring
Bagasse: stack height/size limits with fire breaks (≥ 15 m — verify), temperature probing of stacks, water monitors and hydrant ring
Spark arrestors on boiler stacks, bagasse conveyor dust control (enclosure, Ex equipment in bunkers), housekeeping
Sugar dust: DHA, Ex zoning, venting on dryers/silos, housekeeping
Boilers under Boilers Act 2025/IBR with certified attendants/BOE; pressure vessels (evaporators, pans, juice heaters) registered and tested
Sulphur burner enclosure and SO2 detection, scrubber; lime slaker guarding and PPE; molasses tanks as confined spaces
Seasonal workforce induction (see seasonal procedure); heat plan; first aid and OHC for 24×7 season; fire crew trained; MSIHC/PESO checks for ethanol/distillery where attached
steps: Season start: pre-season audit of guards, interlocks, pressure-vessel certificates, boiler certificate, fire system, traffic plan, bagasse yard layout
Refresher training for permanent staff; induction for seasonal workers before posting.
Cane yard: marshals control each unloading bay; drivers out of cab and in marked zone during grab unloading; trolleys chocked; no manual pushing of trolleys; night lighting checked.
Cane carrier/mills: never clear chokes while running — stop, isolate, use tools; pull-wire tests each shift; knives/shredder covers interlocked; two persons for roller setting under LOTO.
Centrifugals: check lid interlock and brake each shift; never hand-wash basket while turning; load within rated charge; vibration/over-speed trips tested weekly; annual basket NDT.
Bagasse yard: probe stack temperatures daily (alarm > 60–70 °C — verify), rotate stock, keep fire breaks clear, no hot work, water monitors ready; conveyor dust housekeeping each shift.
Boiler house: certified attendant only; blow-down, low-water cut-off tests; bagasse bunker fires — isolate feed, inert/flood per plan; ash handling PPE.
Process house: sulphur burner started by trained operator with SO2 detector; lime added slowly with face shield
Hot-liquor valves operated from side; pan/evaporator entry under confined-space permit after cooling and isolation.
Sugar house: dryers/graders/silos — dust housekeeping, Ex equipment, venting intact; bagging ergonomics (50 kg bags — mechanical aids).
Molasses/ETP: tank entry permit with gas test (CO2, ethanol, H2S); spent-wash lagoons fenced; biogas plant Ex controls.

Weekly season review: injuries/near misses, traffic violations, stack temperatures, interlock faults; off-season: maintenance under PTW/LOTO, confined-space and hot-work controls, contractor management.
ppe: Helmet, hi-vis (cane yard), safety boots, gloves, face shield and apron (lime/sulphur/hot liquor), hearing protection (mill house), FFP2 (bagasse/sugar dust), heat gloves (pans/boilers), harness for stack/tank work
stop: Hand-feeding or choke clearing on running carrier/mill
Centrifugal lid interlock or over-speed trip inoperative
Driver/worker in unloading bay during grab operation
Bagasse stack temperature rising or fire break blocked
Boiler run by uncertified attendant / pressure vessel test overdue
records: Pre-season audit, traffic plan and marshal logs, guard/interlock checks, centrifugal inspection/NDT, bagasse stack temperature log
Boiler and pressure-vessel certificates, SO2 monitoring, confined-space permits, seasonal induction records, injury/near-miss log

india: Factories Act ss.21–23, 29, 31, 36, 37, 38 via state rules / OSH Code (seasonal factory provisions); Boilers Act 2025 & IBR; Boiler Attendants/BOE Rules 2011
Sch. II (SO2, dusts); Petroleum Rules (ethanol distilleries); MSIHC; HOWM (press mud/ETP sludge); MV Act (cane transport); Electricity Act/CEA (co-gen)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 Rule 56 Schedule (centrifugal machines — verify) & Rule 129 schedules; Karnataka Boiler Rules 1982; KSPCB (sugar/distillery norms); Belagavi/Bagalkot sugar belt
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 Rule 53 Schedule (centrifugal/hydro-extractors — verify) & Rule 61; TN Boiler Rules; TNPCB; TN Sugar Factories Control Act 1949 (cane supply)
osha: 1910.212, 1910.219, 1910.147, 1910.272 (grain-like dust), 1910.1000 (SO2), 1910.146; NFPA 652/61/68 (sugar dust — Imperial Sugar 2008 CSB report), ASME BPVC
intl: ILO Code of Practice (agriculture) & ISO 45001; UK HSE food dust/sugar guidance; EN 12547 (centrifuges), ISO 12100; Sugar Industry Technologists / ISSCT safety papers

t: Rice, Flour & Oil Mills – Grain Dust, Elevators, Husk Boilers, Fumigation & Bag Handling
purpose: Prevent dust explosions and fires, grain engulfment, machinery entanglement, fumigant poisoning, solvent fires and manual-handling injuries in rice mills, flour/atta mills, dal mills, oil mills and warehouses.
scope: Grain receipt and cleaning, driers, parboiling, hullers/polishers, roller and hammer mills, bucket elevators and conveyors, silos and flat godowns, bag stacking and loading, husk-fired boilers, hexane solvent extraction and expellers, fumigation of stacks and silos.
hazards: Dust: flour/grain dust explosions originating in bucket elevators (belt slip, bearing heat), hammer mills, dust collectors
Grain dust respiratory disease (TLV 4 mg/m³); husk dust and rice husk ash (crystalline silica — verify)

Engulfment in silos/hopper bins and flat storage; bag-stack collapse (stacks > 15–20 bags high, wet bags); manual handling of 50–75 kg bags (ILO limit 55 kg benchmark; state rules max loads — verify) — back injuries
Machinery: hullers, polishers, roller mills, hammer mills, screw conveyors, elevator boots; unguarded belts; husk furnace fires, boiler incidents, hot parboiling water/steam scalds

Fumigation: aluminium phosphide (phosphine) — fatal exposures to workers and nearby residents; unlicensed use; residues; hexane solvent extraction — Class A petroleum fires/explosions (NFPA 36); rodenticides
pre: Dust explosion controls (NFPA 61/652 benchmark): elevators with belt-slip and alignment switches, bearing temperature monitoring, explosion vents to outside, magnets before mills
Dust collectors outside or vented, Ex-rated electricals in dusty areas (IS/IEC 60079-10-2 zones), housekeeping (no layers > 0.8 mm), no compressed-air blow-down near ignition sources, hot-work permit
Silo/bin entry per silo procedure (zero-entry policy, LOTO, lifeline, atmosphere test)
Bag stacking rules: stack height limit (e.g. ≤ 20 bags or per godown design — verify), dunnage, stepped/interlocked stacks, no climbing on stacks without ladders, 1 m clearance from walls
Manual handling: mechanical aids (conveyors, stackers, trolleys), two-person lifts for > 50 kg, bag weights reduced where possible, training in technique; heat plan for loading in summer

Machine guarding (Factories Act ss.21–22; young persons barred), LOTO for clearing chokes; boiler/furnace under Boilers Act/IBR with certified attendant; husk storage away from furnace, spark arrestors, water supply

Fumigation only by licensed fumigator (Insecticides Act 1968; PPQS accreditation for export): gas-tight covers/sealed silos, exclusion zone and placards, exposure period, aeration and clearance (PH3 < 0.3 ppm OSHA PEL
ACGIH TLV 0.05 ppm — verify), no fumigation near housing; solvent extraction per NFPA 36 and Petroleum Rules with hexane LEL monitoring
steps: Daily: housekeeping of dust (vacuum/sweep with dampening), check elevator belt tracking and bearing temperatures, dust collector operation, husk furnace area, guards in place.
Receipt/cleaning: magnets and destoners working (tramp metal ignition), aspiration on intake pits, dust suppression at unloading.
Driers/parboiling: hot water/steam valves operated with PPE, LPG/husk burners with flame failure, CO check in enclosed drier rooms, scald first aid.
Milling: clear chokes only after stopping and isolating; guards on hullers/polishers/rolls; hammer-mill doors interlocked; respirators in dusty sections.
Elevators/conveyors: respond to slip/alignment/bearing alarms immediately — stop and inspect; keep boots clean; explosion vents unobstructed.
Silos and bins: no entry without permit per silo procedure; break bridges from outside; LOTO on augers.
Bag stacking: follow height/pattern limits, inspect stacks for lean/wet bags, use ladders, keep aisles; loaders use mechanical aids and share loads; rotate crews in heat.

Fumigation: notify workers/neighbours, clear and seal area, licensed fumigator applies tablets with PPE, placards, locked for exposure period, aerate, test, remove residues; records; never allow workers to apply AlP.
Solvent extraction: Ex equipment, LEL monitoring, earthing, hot-work ban, hexane storage per licence, spent-meal desolventising; emergency plan.

Monthly: dust layer audit, Ex equipment check, boiler log review, stack audit, injury/MSD review; annual: elevator/explosion-vent inspection, electrical thermography, worker lung-function screening for dusty jobs.
ppe: FFP2/FFP3 dust respirators, safety glasses, gloves, safety boots, hearing protection (hullers/polishers), heat gloves/face shield (parboiling), back-support training (not belts), harness/lifeline for silo work
Respirator with PH3 cartridge/SCBA for fumigator only
stop: Dust layers > housekeeping limit with equipment running
Elevator bearing/slip alarm ignored or vent blocked
Silo entry without permit/lifeline
Fumigation by unlicensed person or without exclusion/aeration
Bag stack leaning, over height or climbed without ladder
records: Housekeeping/dust audits, elevator sensor logs, Ex equipment register, silo entry permits, bag-stack inspections, manual-handling training
Boiler certificate and log, fumigation records (licence, placards, clearance), solvent licence/LEL logs, injury and respiratory screening records

india: Factories Act ss.14, 21–23, 34 (excessive weights), 36, 37 via state rules / OSH Code; state rules maximum permissible loads (TN/KA — verify); Boilers Act 2025/IBR
Insecticides Act 1968 & Rules 1971; PPQS fumigation accreditation; Petroleum Rules 2002 (hexane); IS/IEC 60079-10-2; FCI/CWC storage & stacking norms; FSSAI; Sch. II (grain dust, hexane 50 ppm)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (weights, fencing, dust); Karnataka Boiler Rules 1982; Raichur/Davanagere rice-mill clusters; KSPCB (husk boilers)
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 (maximum permissible loads rule — verify number; dust); TN Boiler Rules; TNPCB; Red Hills/Tiruvarur rice mills
osha: 1910.272 (grain handling facilities), 1910.212, 1910.147, 1910.146, 1910.1000 (grain dust, phosphine), 1910.1200; NFPA 61 (agricultural & food processing dust), NFPA 36 (solvent extraction), NFPA 68/69
intl: ILO Code of Practice (agriculture), ILO R128 (max weight); UK HSE grain dust & INDG guidance; EN 1127-1; ATEX; FAO fumigation manuals; EU phosphine guidance; ISO 11228 (manual handling)

t: Seasonal & Migrant Workforce Induction and Welfare
purpose: Ensure seasonal, contract and inter-state migrant workers in sugar mills, gins, rice mills, cold stores, construction and plantations are legally engaged, inducted in their language, competent before working near hazards, and provided statutory welfare.
scope: Recruitment through contractors/sardars, age and identity verification, registration (OSH Code inter-state migrant provisions, contractor licence), induction and job-specific training, buddy system, housing/camps, welfare facilities, wages and social security, health, grievance and exit.
roles: Medical officer / first aiders; workers' committee
hazards: Untrained workers placed on dangerous machines/vehicles in the first days (sugar season peaks); language barriers (Odia, Bengali, Hindi, Chhattisgarhi crews in TN/KA mills); supervisors assuming prior experience
Child/adolescent labour via contractors; no age proof; adolescents (14–18) in hazardous processes; women on night shifts without statutory conditions

Camps: poor sanitation, unsafe drinking water, LPG/stove fires, heat, vector-borne disease, snakebite, overcrowding; no first aid or transport at night; wage theft and debt bondage reducing willingness to report hazards
Lack of ESI (seasonal factories exempt) or EC coverage; no PPE issued by contractor; fatigue from 12-h shifts; no grievance channel
pre: Legal: contractor licence (OSH Code — 50+ contract workers threshold — verify), inter-state migrant registration and journey allowance (OSH Code Ch. XI), Form/portal registrations, age verification (Aadhaar/school certificate
None < 14; 14–18 not in hazardous processes per Child & Adolescent Labour Act Schedule), women's night-work conditions (consent, transport, security per state rules)
Induction package in workers' languages: pictorial site hazards, life-saving rules, PPE, emergency, reporting, welfare entitlements, grievance
Minimum 1 day general + job-specific training with competence sign-off before unsupervised work; colour-coded helmet/band for workers in first 30 days
Buddy/mentor system: each new worker paired with an experienced worker for 2 weeks; supervisors' span of control limited
No new worker on cane yard traffic, centrifugals, boilers, HT or confined spaces until trained and authorised
Welfare: drinking water (IS 10500), toilets/bathing (ratios per state rules), rest shelters, canteen (250+ workers — verify), crèche (50+ women)
First aid boxes and OHC/ambulance arrangements, camp standards (ventilation, space, fire safety, lighting, waste), vector control
Wages via bank with slips, PF/ESI or EC insurance; grievance box and committee including migrant representatives
Health: pre-placement fitness for hazardous jobs, vaccination advice (tetanus), TB/malaria awareness, heat plan, snakebite plan; records retained
steps: Before season/mobilisation: verify contractor licence and worker lists (name, age proof, origin state, skills); register inter-state migrants; agree PPE supply and induction responsibilities in contract.

Day 1: identity and age check at gate, medical screening for hazardous jobs, issue ID card and PPE, allot housing; induction in language with interpreter; test understanding (pictorial quiz/demonstration).
Day 1–3: job-specific training with supervisor; competence demonstrated and signed; buddy assigned; coloured identifier worn.
First 30 days: daily toolbox talk in language, supervisor checks, no lone high-risk work; feedback on unsafe conditions encouraged (no retaliation).
Camps: weekly inspection (water test, toilets, cooking area/LPG, electrical, lighting, waste, mosquito control); night transport/first aid arrangements posted; fire extinguishers and exits.
Wages and records: pay through bank on time, muster rolls, overtime limits, weekly off; EC/ESI coverage confirmed; welfare officer accessible.
Health: first-aid boxes stocked, OHC hours, ambulance tie-up, heat and snakebite protocols; sick workers not pressured to work; occupational disease/injury notified.
Grievance: multilingual helpline/committee; issues logged and closed; labour department helpline displayed (Shram Suvidha/state).
Season end: exit health check for hazardous exposures, settlement of dues, return journey allowance, feedback on safety; records retained for inspection.

Audit: monthly HR–safety audit of induction coverage (100% before work), training records vs job placement, camp conditions, wage compliance; corrective action with contractor; report to safety committee.
ppe: Issued free by employer/contractor: helmet (colour-coded for new), safety shoes, hi-vis, gloves, dust mask, eye protection, task PPE; sized for women; replacement register
stop: Worker without induction/competence sign-off on hazardous task
Age proof missing or under-18 in hazardous process
Camp without safe water, sanitation or fire safety
Contractor without licence/registration for migrant workers
Wages or PPE withheld
records: Contractor licences, worker registers with age proof, migrant registrations, induction and competence records (language)
Buddy assignments, camp inspections, welfare facility checks, wage/PF/EC records, health records, grievance log, audits

india: OSH Code 2020 Ch. XI (inter-state migrant workers), Ch. on contract labour, ss.23–24 (welfare), s.6; OSH Central Rules 2026; Code on Social Security 2020 (EC, ESI — seasonal factory exemption s.1(4) ESI Act legacy — verify)
Child & Adolescent Labour (P&R) Act 1986 (amended 2016) & Schedule; Code on Wages 2019; BOCW rules (construction); Plantations provisions in OSH Code; Shram Suvidha Portal
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (welfare, canteen, crèche); Karnataka Labour Dept migrant worker registration; Karnataka Shops & Establishments (night work for women, 2026 amendment)
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 (welfare ratios); TN Labour Dept inter-state migrant worker registration (post-2023 drives); TN BOCW Welfare Board; Tiruppur/Coimbatore migrant worker guidelines
osha: 1910.142 (temporary labour camps), 1928 (agriculture), 1910.1200 (HazCom — training in understandable language), OSHA Temporary Worker Initiative
intl: ILO C97/C143 (migrant workers), C184 (agriculture), C155/C187; ILO Code of Practice (agriculture); ISO 45001 cl. 7.3 (awareness), 7.4; Ethical Trading Initiative base code; GRI 403

t: DG Sets, Fuel Day Tanks & Generator Rooms
purpose: Prevent electrocution, auto-start injuries, CO poisoning, fuel fires, noise and emission violations at diesel generator installations in offices, hospitals, malls, data centres, sites and plants.
scope: DG sets 15 kVA–3 MVA in rooms, basements, rooftops and acoustic enclosures; AMF/synchronising panels and changeover; starting batteries; diesel day tanks and bulk tanks; exhaust stacks; fuel transfer; maintenance and testing; waste oil.
hazards: Automatic start on mains failure during maintenance — rotating fan/belts, hot exhaust (400–500 °C), 415 V live terminals; back-feed to grid if changeover fails (electrocutes utility workers)
CO and exhaust gases in basements/enclosures; hot exhaust pipes igniting combustibles; diesel spills on hot manifold; fuel day tank overfill/leaks; battery hydrogen and acid
Noise > 100 dB(A) inside enclosures; vibration; crush during engine lifting; falls from rooftop DG platforms; arc flash at synchronising panels; radiator fan guards missing
Statutory: diesel storage above PESO exemption, CPCB emission (CPCB IV+) and noise norms, stack height, used-oil handling
pre: Design/approval: CEIG/Electrical Inspectorate approval for DG above thresholds (CEA 2023 — verify capacity), licensed electrical contractor
Earthing (neutral and body) tested, changeover/ATS with mechanical and electrical interlock to prevent back-feed, emergency stop outside room, panel arc-flash labels
Room/enclosure: ventilation sized for engine heat and combustion air, exhaust piped to roof/stack at CPCB height (H = h + 0.2 × √kVA), insulated and clear of combustibles (≥ 0.5 m — verify)
CO detector in basements, fire detection and CO2/DCP/clean-agent extinguishers or fixed system per Fire NOC, no storage in DG room, lighting, signage 'May start automatically'

Fuel: day tank ≤ exempt quantity per Petroleum Rules (Class B — verify current exemption and container-size condition) or PESO licence, bund 110%, drip trays, overfill alarm/level gauge, shut-off valve, spill kit, no smoking
Bulk tank per tank procedure

Maintenance control: LOTO procedure — AMF to manual/off, battery disconnected, control fuse removed, test before touching; AMC vendor inducted; PTW for work on live panels (electrical); lifting plan for alternator/engine
Compliance: CPCB IV+ compliant engines for new installs (from 1 Jul 2023 — verify), acoustic enclosure 25 dB(A) insertion loss and 75 dB(A) at 1 m
Stack emission tests, used-oil to registered recycler (HOWM/used-oil EPR), running-hour and fuel logs for SPCB/CCTS Scope 1
steps: Weekly test run: inform occupants, check coolant/oil/fuel, battery, belts, guards, exhaust leaks, vibration; run on load 15–30 min; log readings; defects to AMC.

Before any maintenance: switch AMF to OFF/manual, disconnect battery negative, remove control fuse, lock and tag, verify engine cannot crank, isolate alternator breaker and test dead; allow exhaust to cool.
Work on changeover/synchronising panels: Electrical PTW, isolate both sources where possible, arc-rated PPE for live testing, insulated tools, second person.
Fuel transfer/filling: engine off (or per OEM), bonding of drums/tanker, drip trays, watch level gauge, stop at 90%; clean spills immediately; no filling in lightning.
Battery: ventilation, no sparks near terminals, PPE for electrolyte, insulated tools; replace swollen batteries.
Basement DG rooms: CO detector tested monthly, exhaust duct integrity, door seals; stop and ventilate on CO alarm; no occupancy during runs.
Noise: enclosure doors closed during runs, hearing protection inside enclosure, neighbour complaints logged; noise test yearly.
Emission: stack monitoring per SPCB consent, maintain injectors/filters, log running hours and diesel consumption (Scope 1 reporting).
Fire: hot exhaust clearance, no rags/combustibles, extinguishers inspected, fire detection linked to BMS; fuel leak → shut down, isolate, contain.
Annual: CEIG inspection where applicable, earth testing, insulation resistance, protection relay testing, acoustic enclosure check, PESO/SPCB compliance review, AMC and operator competence records.
ppe: Hearing protection (SNR ≥ 25) inside enclosures, insulated gloves and arc-rated face shield for panel work, safety glasses, heat-resistant gloves, oil-resistant safety shoes, acid PPE for batteries
stop: AMF not disabled and battery not disconnected before work
Back-feed interlock defective or bypassed
CO alarm in basement/enclosure
Fuel leak or storage beyond licence/unbunded
Exhaust within clearance of combustibles / fire system impaired
records: CEIG approvals and test reports, DG log book (runs, readings), LOTO/PTW records, fuel receipts and stock vs licence, CO detector tests, noise and emission tests, AMC reports, used-oil manifests, fire system checks

india: Electricity Act 2003 & CEA Safety Regulations 2023 (installations, approvals, back-feed prevention, accident reporting); IS 3043 (earthing), IS 732, IS 1646, IS 5216; Petroleum Act & Rules 2002 (Class B diesel storage)

EP Act — CPCB DG set emission (CPCB IV+ from 2023 — verify) & noise norms (Schedule VI/Noise Rules; 75 dB(A) at 1 m), MoEF stack-height formula; HOWM Rules & Used Oil EPR 2023; NBC 2016 Part 4 (DG rooms); OSH Code
ka: CEIG Karnataka (DG approvals); KSPCB (consent, DG noise/emission); KSFES NOC conditions for DG in basements; BESCOM back-feed requirements
tn: CEIG Tamil Nadu; TNPCB; TNFRS; TANGEDCO conditions for captive DG/changeover
osha: 1910.147, 1910.303–305, 1910.335, 1910.95, 1910.1000 (CO 50 ppm), 1910.106; NFPA 110 (emergency power systems), NFPA 37 (stationary engines), NFPA 70 Art. 700/701/702, NFPA 70E
intl: ISO 8528 (generating sets), IEC 60034; UK BS 7671 & HSE guidance on generators/back-feed; EN 50110-1; EU Stage V emission benchmark

t: HVAC Plant Rooms, Chillers & Refrigerant Handling
purpose: Prevent refrigerant asphyxiation and toxic decomposition exposure, pressure incidents, burns, falls and legionella risks in HVAC plant rooms, chillers, AHUs, rooftop units and refrigerant servicing in buildings and plants.
scope: Centrifugal/screw chillers (R-134a, R-1234ze, R-514A, R-123 legacy), VRF/split systems (R-410A, R-32 A2L), ammonia/CO2 systems, propane (A3) chillers, AHUs and fan rooms, cooling towers, ducts and plenums, refrigerant recovery/charging, brazing, pressure testing, rooftop units.
hazards: Refrigerant leak in machinery room displaces oxygen (A1 refrigerants) — asphyxiation; A2L (R-32, R-1234yf) mildly flammable
A3 (R-290) flammable; B2L ammonia toxic; R-123 (toxic, ODS); decomposition to phosgene/HF when heated by brazing or fire

Pressure: compressor discharge, pressure testing with wrong gas (never oxygen/air — oil explosion), over-pressurised cylinders in heat, liquid-trapped lines; cylinder handling; frostbite from liquid refrigerant

Mechanical: AHU fan start during filter change, belt nips, chiller rotating parts; falls from rooftop units, AHU platforms, ladders; confined ducts/plenums/chilled-water tanks; hot surfaces and steam/hot water (calorifiers)
Electrical: VFD panels, capacitor banks; legionella in cooling towers and condensate; noise in plant rooms; chemical dosing (water treatment); ODS Rules compliance for HCFC phase-out and venting ban
pre: Machinery rooms per ASHRAE 15 / EN 378 benchmark: refrigerant detectors with alarm and automatic ventilation (setpoint per refrigerant RCL/TLV — e.g. 1,000 ppm R-134a alarm (verify))
Mechanical ventilation, self-closing doors opening outward, emergency shut-off switch outside, O2 monitor for large charges, no open flames, signage with refrigerant type and charge
Technicians trained and certified in refrigerant handling (recovery, charging, leak detection) — ODS Rules 2000 compliance: no venting
Recovery machines and cylinders; registration of servicing enterprises where required (verify); refrigerant log per system; retrofit plans for HCFC (R-22) phase-out
Pressure work: nitrogen (OFN) with regulator and PRV for pressure/leak tests at design pressure, never oxygen or compressed air
Refrigerant cylinders stored upright, shaded, ≤ 50 °C, valve caps; hot-work permit for brazing with refrigerant evacuated and OFN purge, fire watch, extinguisher
LOTO for AHUs/fans/chillers; guards on belts; fixed platforms/guardrails or anchors for rooftop units
Confined-space permits for ducts, plenums and tanks; chemical dosing with PPE, eyewash; cooling towers per legionella procedure

Emergency: escape respirators/SCBA for ammonia or large A1 charges, evacuation plan, ventilation override, refrigerant leak response (isolate, ventilate, no entry without O2 reading), first aid for frostbite/inhalation
steps: Daily round: detector/O2 status, ventilation, chiller alarms, leaks (oil traces), pressures/temperatures, plant-room housekeeping, no storage against panels.

Before service on a system: identify refrigerant and charge, isolate electrically (LOTO), recover refrigerant into rated cylinder (weigh, do not overfill > 80%), log quantity; never vent to atmosphere.
Leak testing: OFN at test pressure with gauge and relief; electronic leak detector; soap test; no refrigerant-oxygen mixtures.
Brazing: hot-work permit, system evacuated and purged with OFN flowing, ventilation on, fire watch, PPE; phosgene/HF awareness — stop if refrigerant smell/irritation.
Charging: by weight/sight glass per OEM, liquid/vapour per manufacturer, gloves and goggles; A2L/A3 — Ex-rated tools, ventilation, no ignition sources, charge limits per room size (EN 378).
AHU/fan work: LOTO, confirm fan stopped, guard belts after service, filter changes with respirator for dusty/microbial filters; condensate pans cleaned (microbial growth).
Rooftop units: edge protection/anchors, weather check, no work in lightning; ladders secured.
Ducts/plenums/tanks: confined-space permit, isolate fans and dampers, atmosphere test, attendant.

Refrigerant alarm/leak: leave room, activate ventilation, close door, isolate system if safe from outside, no re-entry until O2 and refrigerant readings safe; large/ammonia leaks → evacuate and ERT with SCBA.

Records and compliance: refrigerant inventory and loss rate (Kigali/ODS reporting), technician certificates, detector calibration, hot-work permits, pressure-test records, legionella scheme; review leaks > 5%/yr for repair.
ppe: Safety glasses/goggles, cryogenic/insulated gloves for refrigerant, hearing protection in plant rooms, heat gloves
Harness on roofs, FFP2/3 for filters, escape respirator (plant rooms with large charges), SCBA for ammonia ERT
stop: Refrigerant/O2 alarm or ventilation failure in machinery room
Pressure test with oxygen or compressed air
Brazing without recovery/OFN purge and hot-work permit
AHU/fan not isolated before internal work
A2L/A3 charging with ignition sources or without ventilation
records: Refrigerant log per system (charges, recoveries, leaks), technician certificates, detector and O2 calibration, hot-work permits
Pressure-test records, LOTO, confined-space permits, roof work permits, legionella scheme and results, ODS compliance reports

india: Ozone Depleting Substances (Regulation & Control) Rules 2000 (as amended; HCFC phase-out, venting ban, servicing enterprise registration — verify) & India Cooling Action Plan/Kigali; IS 660 (mechanical refrigeration safety)
IS 4544 (ammonia); Gas Cylinders Rules 2016 (refrigerant cylinders); Factories Act s.31/36 via state rules / OSH Code; IS 3103 (ventilation); CEA 2023; NBC Part 8 (building services)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969; KSPCB (ODS/HFC reporting); KSFES
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950; TNPCB; TNFRS
osha: 1910.147, 1910.146, 1910.1000 (refrigerant PELs), 1910.253 (brazing gases), 1910.101; ASHRAE 15 & 34 (safety classification), ASHRAE 188; EPA Section 608 (technician certification) as benchmark
intl: EN 378-1 to -4 (refrigerating systems safety), ISO 5149, ISO 817 (refrigerant designation/safety class); IIAR 2 (ammonia)
UK F-Gas Regs & IOR safety guides; EN 13313 (competence of personnel); EIGA (nitrogen pressure testing)

t: Lifts & Escalators – Machine Rooms, Pits, Car-Top Work & Passenger Release
purpose: Prevent falls into hoistways, crushing by cars and counterweights, electrocution and entrapment injuries during lift and escalator maintenance, inspection and passenger rescue in buildings, malls, hospitals and factories.
scope: Passenger, goods, hospital/bed and fire lifts (traction, MRL, hydraulic), service lifts, escalators and travelators; machine rooms, hoistways, pits, car tops, landing doors and interlocks; maintenance contractors; trapped-passenger release; statutory licensing and inspection.
roles: Lift maintenance contractor (licensed firm, trained mechanics)
Facility manager / security (first response to entrapment)
hazards: Landing door opened with no car present — persons fall into shaft (the leading cause of lift deaths); door interlocks bypassed with jumpers by mechanics; passengers climbing out of stalled car between floors
Mechanic on car top struck by overhead/crushed in headroom when car moves at normal speed; pit work with car descending or counterweight
Falls into pit from landing; stored energy (hydraulic pressure, buffer springs, suspended loads)

Electrical: live controllers, 415 V in machine room, lighting circuits separate from mainline; brake release manual operations; ropes/sheaves pinch points; escalator step/chain drives and comb plates during maintenance
Untrained security/facility staff attempting passenger release — forcing doors, moving car; fire/smoke in shaft; hospital bed lifts with patients
pre: Statutory: lift installation permission and operating licence under state Lifts Act (TN 1997 / KA 2012 — amendments 2025–26
Verify periods), periodic inspection by Electrical Inspectorate, maintenance by licensed firm under written AMC
Licence and load-capacity notices displayed in car, lift log book, ARD (automatic rescue device) and intercom/alarm working
Safe working rules for mechanics: no 'jumpers' on door interlocks except per OEM procedure with controlled removal
Car-top work only in INSPECTION mode at reduced speed with stop switch, car-top guardrail (where clearance > 0.3 m — verify EN 81-20), two persons for hoistway work
Pit stop switch and ladder; LOTO at mainline and car-light switches before work in machine room/controller
Trapped-passenger release: only by trained lift mechanics (or trained facility staff for ARD-equipped lifts per written procedure): confirm car position
Switch off mainline, release only when car within landing zone (≤ 0.3–0.5 m — verify), never pull passengers out when car is between floors beyond zone
Reassure via intercom; target response ≤ 30 min
Hoistway/machine-room access control: locked doors (keys controlled), signage, lighting, no storage
Landing-door emergency keys controlled by trained staff only; fire lift provisions per NBC; escalators: emergency stops, comb-plate/skirt guards, pit LOTO
Contractor management: induction, PTW for hoistway/machine-room work, barricading of landings during work, communication, lifting plan for motor/machine replacement
steps: Monthly maintenance visit: contractor signs in, posts 'lift under maintenance' barriers at landings, isolates as required (LOTO), checks door interlocks, brakes, ropes (discard criteria), safety gear, ARD, alarm/intercom
Records in log book.
Car-top access: call car to floor below, open landing door with key, operate car-top stop switch, set INSPECTION mode, step on car top only after confirming stop
Move only at inspection speed with stop in hand; stand clear of counterweight and overhead.

Pit access: stop switch on, light on, car parked above with doors mechanically blocked or car in inspection with second person at controls; use pit ladder; never enter pit under a car that can move normally.
Machine room/controller: LOTO mainline, verify dead, discharge capacitors (VVVF drives — wait per OEM), guard sheaves; manual brake release only with two persons and car movement controlled.
Door interlock faults: repair, never bypass permanently; test every landing door lock before returning lift to service; remove any jumper before leaving.
Return to service: all persons out of hoistway, tools removed, inspection switches reset, test run with doors; remove barriers; log.
Trapped passengers: security confirms lift and floor from indicator/intercom, calls mechanic/ARD operates
Keeps talking to passengers, tells them not to force doors; medical emergency → fire service; release by trained person per rule; record time and cause.
Escalator maintenance: LOTO, barricade both ends, work in pits with second person, replace step chains per OEM; daily visual (comb plates, skirts, handrail) by facility staff.
Fire/emergency: lifts recalled to ground (fireman's switch), fire lift for fire service only, evacuation by stairs; hospital bed lifts with ARD and emergency power.
Annual: statutory inspection and licence renewal, rope/brake/safety-gear tests, ARD and emergency-power tests, AMC review, trapped-passenger drill with security
Incidents (falls, entrapments > 1 h, injuries) reported to Inspectorate as required.
ppe: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, helmet in hoistway/pit, insulated tools and gloves for controller work, harness where car-top clearance/guardrail inadequate, torch, hi-vis for landing barricading
stop: Door interlock bypassed with lift in normal service
Car-top or pit work without INSPECTION mode/stop switch and second person
Passenger release attempted by untrained person or with car outside landing zone
Licence/inspection expired or AMC lapsed
Landing door opened without confirming car present
records: Lifts Act licence and inspection reports, AMC and maintenance log book, LOTO/PTW records, door-interlock test records
ARD/alarm tests, entrapment log with response times, trained-releaser list, escalator inspections, incident reports to Inspectorate

tn: TN Electrical Inspectorate (CEIG) licensing (e-Forms 1–34 — verify); TNFRS

t: Housekeeping & Soft-Services Contractors – Chemicals, Façade Access, Waste & Dignity
purpose: Protect housekeeping, pantry, waste and façade-cleaning contract staff from chemical, sharps, slip, height and biological hazards and ensure statutory welfare, dignity and prohibition of manual scavenging.
scope: Office, hospital, mall, campus and plant housekeeping; toilet and floor chemicals; high-level and façade cleaning (MEWPs, gondolas/BMUs, rope access); waste segregation (biomedical, e-waste, hazardous); pantry/LPG; septic tanks and drains (no manual entry); women and night shifts.
hazards: Chemicals: HCl-based toilet cleaners (10–30%) with bleach → chlorine gas; caustic drain openers; phenyl/solvents; decanting into unlabelled bottles; splashes to eyes; no gloves
Sharps and biomedical waste (needles in bins, blood spills) — HBV/HCV/HIV; infectious laundry
Falls on wet floors (own and others), ladders for high dusting, façade work from gondolas/BMUs without harness or inspection; electrical (wet mopping near sockets, floor machines)

Manual scavenging: cleaning septic tanks/sewers/drains by hand — fatal H2S/asphyxia; illegal under PEMSR Act 2013; ergonomics (bent mopping, bin lifting), heat on terraces, pest-control chemicals, LPG in pantries
Exploitation: underpayment, no PPE, long hours, harassment of women on night shifts, no toilets/changing rooms for staff
pre: Contract terms: minimum wages, PF/ESI, PPE and training supplied, supervisors trained, prohibition of manual scavenging and septic/sewer entry (mechanised cleaning only), POSH compliance, grievance channel
Principal employer verifies monthly
Chemical control: approved list with SDS in local language, colour-coded and labelled dispensers/bottles (no decanting into drink bottles)
Dilution charts, never-mix rule (acid + bleach), dosing stations, eyewash/first aid, gloves/goggles for toilet cleaning
Storage room ventilated, locked, bunded
Height and façade: no ladders above 3 m for cleaning — use MEWPs/scaffold/BMU/rope access by trained persons
Gondola/BMU tested 12-monthly (LOLER/BOCW benchmark), daily pre-use, harness to independent anchor, wind limits, exclusion below; WAH permit

Biomedical/sharps: puncture-proof containers, colour-coded BMW segregation (BMW Rules 2016), spill kits, hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis protocol for hospital staff, no hand compaction of waste
e-waste/hazardous waste segregated with manifests
Welfare and dignity: toilets, changing rooms, rest area, drinking water for contract staff; women's night-shift conditions (consent, transport, security, two or more)
ID cards; training in language with pictograms; floor-cleaning schedules to limit wet-floor exposure (signage, barriers)
steps: Daily start: supervisor allocates tasks, checks PPE, chemicals in labelled bottles, wet-floor signs, equipment (RCD-protected machines, cables), ladders condition; briefs on special risks (events, spills).
Toilet/floor cleaning: gloves and goggles, ventilate, one chemical at a time, rinse between acid and bleach products, wet-floor signs both ends, mop with technique to reduce bending
Report splashes immediately and use eyewash.
High dusting/light fittings: isolate electrical where touching fittings, use platform steps with handrail or MEWP; no standing on furniture.
Façade/atrium cleaning: WAH permit, trained operators, gondola/BMU checks, harness and lifeline, communication, weather check, exclusion zone and signage below.

Waste: segregate at source, sharps only in puncture-proof bins, no hands inside bins, lift with legs/trolleys, BMW bags ≤ 3/4 full and sealed, store in designated area; manifests for BMW/hazardous/e-waste.
Spills (blood/body fluids): gloves, absorbent, disinfectant (1% hypochlorite), dispose as BMW, wash hands; needlestick → wash, report, PEP within 2 h.
Drains/septic tanks/sumps: no manual entry — mechanised cleaning by licensed agency; facility to prove alternatives
Any sump/pit entry is a confined space under permit by trained persons with gas test and retrieval, never housekeeping staff.
Pantry/LPG: cylinder storage, regulator/hose checks, leak response; electrical appliances RCD-protected; kitchen fire extinguisher (Class F).
Night shifts: minimum two staff, security escort to transport, well-lit routes, panic/call system; POSH awareness and complaint route displayed.

Monthly: principal employer audit (wages, PPE, training, chemical labels, BMW compliance, welfare), incident review, staff feedback; annual health check for hospital housekeeping; vaccination records.
ppe: Nitrile/rubber gloves, goggles/face shield for toilet and chemical work, non-slip shoes, aprons, FFP2 for dusty/biological tasks, puncture-resistant gloves for waste, harness and helmet for façade/height, hi-vis for outdoor
stop: Manual entry into septic tank, sewer or drain
Mixing acid cleaner with bleach / chemicals in unlabelled bottles
Façade or height cleaning without permit, trained operator and fall protection
Sharps handled by hand or compacted
Woman on night shift alone or without transport/security
records: Contractor compliance file (licence, wages, PF/ESI), training (language), chemical list and SDS, PPE issue, WAH permits and gondola inspections
BMW/hazardous/e-waste manifests, needlestick/injury log, vaccination records, POSH committee records, monthly audits

india: OSH Code 2020 (contract labour, welfare, women night work) & Central Rules 2026; Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers & their Rehabilitation Act 2013 & Rules
BMW Management Rules 2016; E-Waste Rules 2022; HOWM Rules; POSH Act 2013; Minimum Wages/Code on Wages; BOCW rules (gondolas/BMUs); IS 17859 (GHS); state Shops & Establishments Acts
ka: Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act (2026 amendment on women's night work); Karnataka Contract Labour Rules; KSPCB (BMW authorisation)
tn: TN Shops & Establishments Act 1947; TN Contract Labour Rules; TNPCB BMW authorisation; TN Manual Scavenging monitoring (Madras HC orders)
osha: 1910.1030 (bloodborne pathogens — sharps, PEP), 1910.1200, 1910.22 (walking surfaces), 1910.146, 1910.67 (MEWPs), 1910.27(b) (rope descent); ANSI/IWCA I-14.1 (window cleaning)
intl: UK HSE cleaning industry guidance (chemicals, slips, window cleaning), LOLER (BMUs), Working at Height Regs; EN 1808 (BMUs/gondolas); ISO 45001 cl. 8.1.4 (contractors); ILO C189 (domestic/cleaning workers — benchmark)

t: Events, Temporary Structures & Crowd Management
purpose: Prevent crowd crush, structural collapse, fire, electrical and heat incidents at corporate events, exhibitions, product launches, campus festivals, religious/ sports gatherings and mall promotions using temporary structures and large audiences.
scope: Stages, trusses, LED walls, marquees/pandals, grandstands, barricades, temporary power and lighting, pyrotechnics/fireworks and SFX, food stalls with LPG, crowd flows (entry, egress, pits), VIP movements, medical and fire cover, weather; event build-up, show and tear-down.
roles: Police, fire service, medical provider; stewards/marshals (trained)
hazards: Crowd crush and stampede at entries/exits/stage front (Bengaluru RCB stampede June 2025, 11 dead — benchmark): over-capacity, free entry rumours, closed gates, bottlenecks, surges, no real-time counting
Temporary structure collapse (wind on LED walls/trusses/pandals, overloaded stages, inadequate ballast), falls during rigging, dropped objects; grandstand failure
Fire: pandal fabrics, decorations, pyrotechnics/cold pyro, LPG stalls, generator fuel, blocked exits (Kumbakonam/Uphaar benchmarks); electrical shocks from temporary wiring in wet conditions
Heat stroke in outdoor afternoon events, dehydration, no shade/water; medical emergencies (cardiac) without AED; traffic and parking chaos; weather (rain, lightning, wind)
pre: Permissions: police (crowd/traffic), fire service NOC for temporary structures/pandals (state Fire Act), municipal/venue permission
PESO licence for fireworks/pyro, electrical inspector/licensed contractor certificate, food-stall FSSAI/LPG compliance
Event safety plan submitted (capacity, crowd plan, structures, fire, medical, weather, emergency)
Capacity and crowd plan: occupant load per NBC Part 4 (assembly, e.g. 0.6 m²/person standing — verify) and exit width (≥ 2 exits, widths per NBC), ticketed/counted entry with real-time counting

Segregation of flows, no free-entry announcements without plan, front-of-stage barriers with pit and extraction, stewards ratio (benchmark 1:250 — verify, more at pinch points), PA and signage, VIP routes separate
Temporary structures: design and certification by structural engineer for wind (IS 875 Pt 3) and crowd loads, ballast/anchoring, daily inspections
Wind action plan (lower LED walls/sails at defined speeds), erection by trained riggers with fall protection and exclusion zones
Grandstands certified and inspected
Fire and electrical: flame-retardant pandal fabrics (certificates), extinguishers per area, fire lane access, no pyro without licensed operator and fire-service presence
LPG stalls separated with extinguishers, generators fenced with fuel bunding, temporary wiring with RCDs, earthing, cable protection, weather-proof distribution
Lighting of exits
Medical/weather: medical post with doctor/paramedics, ambulances (ratio per attendance — verify), AEDs, first-aid points
Water points and shade for outdoor; heat plan; weather monitoring with lightning/wind triggers; emergency communication (radios, control room, CCTV)
steps: Planning (weeks before): risk assessment, capacity calculation, crowd-flow drawings, structural designs, permissions, contractor appointments, stewards' briefing material; tabletop exercise for evacuation and crush scenarios.

Build-up: site induction for all crews, PTW for rigging/height and hot work, exclusion zones under rigging, structural inspection and sign-off before loading, electrical certification, fire extinguishers placed, exits marked.
Pre-doors: final walk-through with police/fire/venue: exits unlocked and clear, barriers secure, stewards in position with radios, counting system live, PA tested, medical post staffed, weather check
Go/no-go decision recorded.

Entry: controlled queuing with barriers in snake lanes, counters at each gate, stop entry at capacity, communicate wait times, separate exits; monitor density (stop and relieve if > 4 persons/m² — verify) at pinch points.
During event: control room monitors CCTV/density/weather; stewards report surges; stage manager can pause show on crowd-manager call; announce safety messages; keep fire lanes clear.
Wind/lightning/rain: follow structure wind action plan; suspend outdoor event and shelter at trigger; never continue with LED walls/trusses above limits.
Egress: staged dispersal announcements, all exits open and staffed, traffic plan active, lighting on; avoid counter-flows; monitor until crowd disperses.
Emergency: evacuation announcement script, stewards guide to exits, medical triage, fire service access, incident commander (police) liaison
Crush indicators (people falling, screams, pressure) → stop entry, open all exits, pause show, relieve pressure.
Tear-down: PTW, exclusion zones, fall protection, controlled dismantling, electrical isolation, waste clearance; debrief.
Post-event report: attendance vs capacity, incidents, near misses, structural/electrical issues, lessons; share with authorities as required.
ppe: Stewards: hi-vis, radios, torches; riggers: harness, helmet, gloves, boots; electricians: insulated tools/gloves; pyro: FR clothing, eye protection; medical: standard kits
stop: Attendance approaching capacity without controlled entry/counting
Exit locked, blocked or stewards not in position
Temporary structure uncertified or wind above action limit
Pyro/LPG/generator without licence, separation or extinguishers
Lightning or storm trigger at outdoor event
records: Event safety plan and risk assessment, permissions/NOCs/licences, structural certificates and inspections, electrical certificate
Steward training and deployment, counting/attendance logs, medical and incident logs, weather log, post-event report

Karnataka Crowd Control (Managing Crowd at Events and Venues of Mass Gathering) Bill/Act 2025 (verify status); NBC 2016 Part 4 (assembly occupancy, exits, temporary structures) & SP 7:2026
State Fire Acts (pandal/temporary structure NOC); Explosives Rules 2008 (fireworks/pyro — PESO); IS 875 Pt 3 (wind loads)
CEA 2023 (temporary installations); Police Acts (licences for public assemblies); Disaster Management Act 2005
ka: Karnataka Fire Force Act 1964 (temporary structures NOC); Bengaluru City Police event permissions; GBA/BBMP; KSNDMC weather alerts; Karnataka Crowd Control law 2025 (verify)
tn: TN Fire & Rescue Services Act 2025 (verify) — temporary structure licences; Chennai Police event permission; TN Public Buildings (Licensing) Act 1965 (pandals); TNSDMA
osha: General Duty Clause; 1910.36–38 (exits, emergency action plans); NFPA 101 (assembly occupancies), NFPA 102 (grandstands/tents), NFPA 1126 (proximate pyrotechnics), NFPA 70 Art. 525/590; ANSI E1.21 (temporary stage structures)

BS 7909 (temporary electrical systems for events); IStructE Temporary Demountable Structures guidance; Love Parade 2010 & Astroworld 2021 lessons

t: Sewer, Septic Tank & STP Sump Entry – Mechanised Cleaning First (PEMSR Act)
purpose: Eliminate deaths from manual cleaning of sewers, septic tanks, manholes and STP/ETP sumps by requiring mechanised cleaning, and control H2S, methane, oxygen deficiency, drowning and biological hazards when entry is unavoidable.
scope: Municipal and campus sewers, manholes, septic tanks, STP/ETP wet wells, sludge pits, grease traps, storm drains; cleaning by jetting/suction machines and robots; entry for inspection, repair and rescue; contractors and sanitation workers.
roles: Licensed mechanised cleaning agency / sanitation contractor
Entry supervisor, attendant, entrants (trained; not sanitation labourers)
hazards: H2S (10 ppm TLV; 100 ppm IDLH; > 500 ppm instant collapse), CH4 (explosive), CO2/O2 deficiency, ammonia; most deaths occur to rescuers following the first victim
Drowning/engulfment in sludge and sudden inflow (rain, upstream discharge); slips on ladders; falls through manholes; traffic at road manholes
Biological: hepatitis A/E, leptospirosis, gastro-enteritis, skin infections, needle-stick from sewage; chemical discharges (industrial effluent, solvents) in sewers
Illegal manual scavenging: contractors sending workers into tanks with no equipment — criminal offence under PEMSR Act 2013; Supreme Court 2023 directions (₹30 lakh compensation for deaths — verify)
pre: Policy: no person enters a sewer/septic tank/sump to clean it by hand; cleaning by jetting-cum-suction machines, desilting machines, bandicoot-type robots
Agency empanelled/licensed by ULB; contract clauses prohibit manual entry; principal employer liable
Entry (inspection/repair only) under permit-required confined-space programme: isolation of inflows (upstream penstock/valve, pump LOTO), ventilation ≥ 20 min with blower (verify)
Atmosphere testing at top/middle/bottom (O2 19.5–23.5%, H2S < 10 ppm, LEL < 10%, CO < 25 ppm), continuous monitoring, harness with lifeline on tripod/winch, attendant, communication
Rescue: SCBA sets and trained rescuers at the manhole for every entry; non-entry retrieval as first option; ambulance tie-up; never enter to rescue without SCBA
Health and hygiene: vaccination (hepatitis A/B, tetanus, typhoid advised), washing facilities, PPE decontamination, no eating at site; medical surveillance; leptospirosis awareness

Traffic management for road manholes (IRC:SP:55 signage, cones, barriers), lighting, weather check (no entry when rain forecast); equipment inspection (blowers, detectors calibrated, tripod/winch, SCBA)
steps: Request for cleaning: supervisor verifies machine availability and agency credentials; manual methods refused; schedule jetting/suction; record.
Mechanised cleaning: cordon area, open manhole with tools (hook/keys), stand upwind, operate jetting/suction from surface; handle hoses with gloves; dispose sludge to designated STP/ULB site.

If entry is unavoidable: written justification, permit, isolation of inflows and pumps (LOTO), ventilate, test atmosphere and record, assign attendant and rescue; entrant on lifeline with 4-gas monitor.
Entry: descend ladder with harness attached to retrieval line; continuous gas reading relayed; immediate exit on alarm, odour change or dizziness; work time limited; no hot work.
Attendant: never leaves, never enters; counts entrants; maintains communication; calls rescue and starts non-entry retrieval on alarm.
Emergency: raise alarm, winch victim out, SCBA team only if winch fails; CPR/oxygen; ambulance; notify police/ULB/labour department and DISH (fatal/dangerous occurrence) as required; preserve scene.
Post-work: close and secure manhole, decontaminate PPE and equipment, wash, dispose waste; record readings and permit closure.
STP/ETP sumps and digesters: biogas lines isolated, inert/ventilate, LEL and H2S tests, no entry during sludge transfer; chlorine/chemical dosing rooms separate controls.
Contractor audit: training certificates, equipment, insurance, wages, PPE; any manual entry observed → stop work, remove contractor, report under PEMSR Act.
Review every entry and near miss; annual drill with fire service; update inventory of sewers/tanks and cleaning schedule to reduce entries.
ppe: Full-body harness with retrieval line, 4-gas monitor, chemical/cut-resistant gloves, gumboots, coveralls, goggles/face shield, FFP3 (biological aerosols), SCBA for rescue; washing and disinfection facilities
stop: Any proposal for manual entry to clean a tank or sewer
Atmosphere outside limits or detector not calibrated
No attendant, retrieval system or SCBA rescue at manhole
Inflows/pumps not isolated; rain expected
Contractor not licensed/trained for confined-space entry
records: Mechanised cleaning records, entry permits with gas logs, isolation records, equipment calibration/inspection
Rescue drill records, vaccination/medical records, contractor credentials, incident/near-miss reports, PEMSR compliance file

india: Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 & Rules
Supreme Court Balram Singh v. Union of India (2023) directions; NAMASTE scheme & MoHUA SOP for cleaning of sewers and septic tanks (2018)
Factories Act s.36 via state rules / OSH Code s.6; IS 11972 (safety in sewers/confined spaces — verify title), IS 10245 (SCBA); Sch. II (H2S 10 ppm); BMW/HOWM Rules (sludge)
