t: Crushing & Screening Plants, Haul Roads & HEMM
purpose: Prevent crusher entanglement and blockage-clearing deaths, conveyor injuries, dumper/HEMM collisions and rollovers, dust disease and noise damage in quarries, aggregate plants, captive mines and crushing units.
scope: Jaw, cone, impact and VSI crushers; vibrating screens; feeders, hoppers and conveyors; stockpiles and tunnels; haul roads; dumpers/tippers, excavators, loaders, drills; weighbridge traffic; mobile crushing plants.
roles: Mine manager / plant in-charge (DGMS-recognised where mine)
hazards: Crusher blockage: workers entering jaw/cone or using bars while running — crushed or struck by ejected rock; stored energy in jammed material releasing when freed
Conveyors: nip points at head/tail/return rollers, cleaning spillage near running belts, riding belts, falling from elevated conveyors; stockpile tunnels (engulfment, dust)
HEMM: dumper over-edge at tips, rollovers on haul roads, reversing over pedestrians/light vehicles, brake failure on grades, fatigue; blasting interface
Respirable crystalline silica (TLV 0.025 mg/m³; India Sch. II 0.1 mg/m³ — verify) → silicosis (notifiable); noise 95–110 dB(A); vibration; heat; electrical on mobile plant
pre: Crushers: feed and discharge interlocks, hopper grids/rock breakers for oversize, blockage-clearing procedure with LOTO (crusher and feeder isolated
Stored energy released), no entry into crusher chamber without permit and isolation
Emergency stops at all stations; guarded flywheels/belts

Conveyors: nip guards on all pulleys and return idlers within reach, pull-wire stops full length, crossing bridges, cleaning only with belt stopped/isolated or using long-handled tools from outside guards
Stockpile tunnels as confined spaces with reclaim feeders isolated
Haul roads: design width ≥ 3× widest vehicle (two-way — verify), gradient ≤ 1 in 16 (verify DGMS norm)
Berms/bunds ≥ half wheel height at edges, drainage, dust suppression, signage, speed limits, light-vehicle segregation and radio protocol
Tip-edge bunds and stop blocks; run-off ramps on long grades
HEMM: pre-shift checks, brakes tested on grade, seat belts, reversing cameras/alarms, ROPS/FOPS, fire suppression
Operator competency (DGMS/state certificates where applicable), fatigue management (shift ≤ 8 h in mines), no overloading
Dust: wet suppression at crushers/screens/transfer points, enclosures and dust extraction, cab air-conditioning with filters, respirators (FFP3) for exposed tasks
Silica monitoring and medical surveillance (chest X-ray/PFT per Mines Rules/Factories Rules); hearing conservation
steps: Shift start: inspect guards, pull-wires, e-stops, interlocks, water sprays, haul-road condition (berms, surface, visibility), lighting; HEMM pre-use checks; brief crews.
Feeding crushers: oversize removed with rock breaker or excavator — never by hand or bar while running; operator at console with camera view; stop feeder on blockage.

Blockage clearing: stop and isolate crusher and feeder (LOTO), release stored energy (jack/rock breaker from outside), permit, exclusion zone, two persons, no one inside chamber unless isolated and material secured
Restart only after all clear.
Conveyor spillage: stop and isolate belt before shovelling near pulleys; use guards and bridges; never ride belts; maintain skirting to reduce spillage.
Screens/transfer points: isolate before changing meshes/liners; lifting with rated gear; dust sprays on during operation.
Stockpile tunnels/hoppers: entry only under confined-space permit with feeders isolated, lifeline, gas test, never walk on live stockpiles (engulfment).
Haul traffic: dumpers give way per site rules, light vehicles keep 50 m and call before overtaking, no reversing without camera/spotter, tipping only behind stop blocks with spotter at night
Speed ≤ 30 km/h (verify); wet weather restrictions.
Maintenance on HEMM: park on level, isolate, lower buckets/beds, prop raised bodies, tyre work by trained persons (inflation in cage).
Dust/noise/health: sprays maintained, respirators where > limit, audiometry yearly, silica surveillance per rules; notify silicosis cases.
Weekly: haul-road inspection record, guard audit, incident/near-miss review; monthly: DGMS/statutory returns and inspections, blasting-crusher interface review.
ppe: Helmet, hi-vis, safety boots, FFP3 respirator in dusty zones, hearing protection (SNR ≥ 30), gloves, safety glasses, harness for elevated conveyor work, seat belts in HEMM
stop: Blockage cleared or chamber entered without LOTO and permit
Conveyor guard or pull-wire missing/inoperative
Haul-road berms missing at edges/tips or road width/gradient out of limits
HEMM with defective brakes, seat belt or reversing aids
Dust suppression down with crushing in progress
records: Guard/interlock inspections, LOTO/permits for blockage and conveyor work, haul-road inspection log, HEMM pre-use and maintenance
Operator certificates, dust and noise monitoring, medical surveillance (silica), DGMS/state statutory registers and returns, incident log

india: Mines Act 1952 / Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961 (haul roads, machinery, dust, DGMS circulars incl. Tech. Circ. on dumpers & haul roads — verify) where a mine

Factories Act ss.21–22, 36 via state rules / OSH Code for standalone crushers; MV Act (tippers); Sch. II silica; Third Schedule (silicosis notifiable); IS 9474; CPCB/SPCB stone-crusher siting & dust norms; blasting-codes
ka: Karnataka Minor Mineral Concession Rules 1994 (quarries); KSPCB stone crusher regulations (Karnataka Regulation of Stone Crushers Act 2011); DGMS Bengaluru region
tn: TN Minor Mineral Concession Rules 1959; TNPCB stone crusher siting norms; DGMS Chennai region; TN Factories Rules 1950 for crushing units
osha: 30 CFR Part 56 (MSHA surface metal/non-metal — 56.14107 guarding, 56.9300 berms, 56.12016 LOTO); 1910.212/219; 1926.602; 1910.1053 (silica)
intl: UK Quarries Regulations 1999 & HSE QNJAC guidance (crusher blockages, haul roads, tipping); EN 620 (conveyors), EN 1009 (crushing machinery safety); ISO 19296 (mining machinery); ILO C176

t: Cement Kiln, Preheater & Coal Mill – Hot Meal, Blockage Clearing & Refractory Work
purpose: Prevent hot-meal burns (the leading fatal hazard in cement plants), CO and explosion incidents in coal mills and preheaters, falls and entrapment during kiln/preheater/cooler entry, and refractory and silica exposures.
scope: Preheater cyclones and risers, calciner, kiln inlet and hood, clinker cooler, coal/petcoke mills and bins, raw mills, kiln shutdown and refractory replacement, alternative fuels (AFR) feeding, cement mills and silos, bulk loading.
roles: Safety officer; fire crew; occupational health
hazards: Hot meal (800–1,000 °C powder behaving like fluid) released when clearing cyclone/riser blockages or opening poke holes/doors — engulfs and burns persons below; kiln inlet hot-meal flushes during restart
Coal/petcoke mills and bins: CO build-up and self-heating → fire/explosion; dust explosions; inerting failures; hot gas back-flow
Kiln/preheater/cooler entry during shutdown: residual heat, falling brick/coating, CO, oxygen deficiency, dust (silica from clinker/raw meal), falls at cooler grates, kiln rotation during work
AFR waste hazards (biological, chemical)
Cement/clinker silos and bulk loading: engulfment, dust, falls; hot clinker transport; chromium (VI) in cement (dermatitis); noise; heights on preheater tower (100 m)
pre: Blockage-clearing procedure: only trained crew with written method; poke holes with blast-proof covers; air cannons/CO2 blasters remote-operated; no one below or in line of discharge
Exclusion zones and barriers on all levels below work; aluminised PPE; escape routes clear; never open inspection doors with meal built up above

Coal mill/bin safety: CO and O2 monitoring with alarms and inerting (CO2/N2) on bins, temperature monitoring, explosion vents, inert operation when idle, no hot work near; housekeeping; DHA for coal/petcoke dust
Kiln/preheater/cooler entry: full shutdown, cooling to < 40 °C, isolation of fuel, air, feed and rotation (kiln drive LOTO plus mechanical block)
CO/O2 testing, confined-space permit, scaffold/platform for refractory with protection from falling coating (chipping from safe side), lighting, rescue
Coating removal by trained crews

Falls: guardrails and gratings on preheater tower, cooler, silo tops; WAH permits; dust control (sprays, extraction), silica surveillance; heat-stress plan for tower work; AFR handling with PPE and SDS
Emergency: burn first-aid stations (cool water, burn dressings) at each preheater level and kiln hood, hospital burn-unit tie-up, fire crew, evacuation routes marked
steps: Daily: CCR trends (cyclone pressures/temperatures) to detect build-ups early; poke-hole covers intact; CO levels in coal bins; housekeeping on tower levels.
Minor build-up: clear by air blaster from remote position
If manual poking needed — permit, crew in aluminised suits/face shields, barriers below, one person pokes from the side while second watches; never stand in front of poke hole.
Major blockage: stop feed, reduce temperature, plan with production head, isolate levels below, use remote tools; consider shutdown rather than manual clearing; brief all affected.
Restart after stop: expect hot-meal flushes at kiln inlet/cooler — clear personnel from inlet area and cooler before feed on; monitor.
Coal mill: inert before start/stop as per procedure; respond to CO alarm (> 100 ppm action — verify) by inerting and isolating; fire → CO2 flooding, no opening of doors.
Shutdown entry: cool, isolate (fuel, feed, fans, kiln drive with block), test atmosphere, remove loose coating from safe position, permit entry with attendant
Refractory demolition/installation with scaffold, dust control, heat limits.
Clinker cooler: isolate grate drive and hammers, cool, entry permit; hot clinker spills handled with machines; silo entry per silo procedure.
AFR: segregated reception, SDS, PPE, fire detection in storage, no entry into bunkers.
Burn injury: cool with running water 20 min, remove from hot zone, cover, hospital; report as dangerous occurrence where applicable.
Monthly: blockage-clearing drills and PPE audit, coal-mill safety-system tests, guard/guardrail audit, dust monitoring, incident review; annual: shutdown safety review with contractors.
ppe: Aluminised suit, hood with gold-coated visor, heat-resistant gloves and gaiters for hot-meal work; FFP3/PAPR for dust; helmet, harness on tower; CO monitor for coal/kiln areas; chemical gloves for cement (Cr VI)
stop: Person below or in discharge line of a blockage-clearing point
Coal bin CO/O2 monitoring or inerting out of service
Kiln/preheater entry without cooling, isolation and permit
Poke-hole or inspection door opened with meal above
Guardrail missing on tower/cooler platforms
records: Blockage-clearing permits and crew training, CO/O2 monitoring logs, coal-mill interlock tests, shutdown isolation and entry permits
Refractory contractor records, burn injuries and drills, dust/silica monitoring, WAH permits, incident reports

india: Factories Act ss.21, 31, 36, 37, 38 via state rules / OSH Code; Sch. II (cement dust, silica, CO 50 ppm); Third Schedule (silicosis); IS/IEC 60079-10-2 (coal dust zones)
HOWM Rules (AFR co-processing authorisations — CPCB guidelines); EC Act/CCTS (cement GEI targets); Mines Act for captive limestone mines
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (Rule 129 schedules; confined space); KSPCB (AFR, dust); Karnataka Safety Audit Rules 2024
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950; DISH TN; TNPCB (Ariyalur cement cluster)
osha: 1910.146, 1910.147, 1910.212, 1910.1053 (silica), 1910.1000 (CO); NFPA 85 (pulverised fuel systems), NFPA 652/654; MSHA 30 CFR 56 (quarry)
intl: Cement Sustainability Initiative/GCCA Safety Guidelines (hot meal, blockage clearing, contractor safety); UK HSE cement industry guidance; EN 1127-1; VDI 2263 (dust fires/explosions in coal mills); ISO 45001

t: Steel Plant Fuel Gases (BF/CO/BOF Gas) – CO Poisoning Prevention & Hot-Metal Areas
purpose: Prevent carbon-monoxide poisoning from blast-furnace, coke-oven, converter and producer gases, gas explosions during purging and hot work, and molten-metal/slag incidents at integrated and secondary steel plants, DRI and foundries using gas.
scope: BF gas, COG, BOF/LD gas, producer and mixed gas networks; gas holders, cleaning plants, mains and valves; purging, isolation (water seals, goggle valves, blinds) and hot work on gas lines; stoves and furnaces; cast house, converter, ladle and torpedo-car areas; DRI kilns.
roles: Gas safety officer / energy department head
Gas-line permit issuers and rescue squad
Operators of BF, SMS, coke ovens, rolling mill furnaces
Maintenance and contractors (hot work on gas lines)
hazards: CO: odourless; BF gas 20–30% CO, producer gas 20–25%, COG 5–10% (plus H2, benzene); leaks at valves, seals, bleeders, stoves, furnace doors, gas-holder tops; low-lying accumulation; deaths in groups when rescuers enter

Explosion: air ingress into gas mains during purging/shutdown, hot work without adequate purge (CO2/N2) and gas test, water-seal failure, gas back-flow; furnace light-off without purge; dust (BF flue dust) explosions
Hot metal/slag: ladle/torpedo-car breakouts, water–molten metal explosions, skull falls, converter slopping; burns from splash; hot-metal rail traffic; radiant heat
Confined spaces in gas cleaning plant, stoves, furnaces; H2S/benzene at coke ovens (benzene carcinogen); hydraulics; falls on gas mains walkways; nitrogen asphyxiation
pre: Gas safety organisation: designated gas safety officer, trained gas crew for isolation/purging/hot work, permit system specific to gas lines (IS 17893 plus plant gas permit)
Fixed CO monitoring at leak-prone points with alarms (25 ppm warning, 50 ppm evacuate — verify), wind socks, gas-area signage, restricted zones around bleeders and stoves
Personal CO monitors mandatory for everyone in gas areas; escape sets (CO filter self-rescuers) carried
SCBA sets and resuscitators at gas rescue stations; two-person rule; CO exposure limits (Sch. II 50 ppm TWA / ACGIH 25 ppm)
Isolation standards: positive isolation by goggle valve plus blind or water seal maintained at required head, purge with N2/CO2 (or steam) until CO < 1% and O2 criteria for hot work (verify)
Gas tests before and during work; no hot work on live gas mains; bleeder operation under permit

Hot-metal areas: dry charge/scrap, ladle and runner integrity, water-free pits, refractory inspection, breakout emergency plans, radiant-heat PPE, controlled access to cast house/converter aisle during tapping
Crane/ladle lifting under crane procedures

Furnaces/stoves: automatic purge and flame-failure, double block and bleed on gas trains, interlocks; confined-space entry after cooling and gas-freeing; health surveillance for CO and benzene-exposed workers
steps: Shift start: check fixed CO monitors, wind direction, water-seal levels, bleeder status, personal monitors calibrated, rescue station equipment; log.
Entering gas areas: monitor on, two persons, stay upwind of bleeders/stoves, no lying down/sitting in low areas; leave immediately on alarm, report.
Gas line isolation for maintenance: gas permit; close goggle valve, insert blind/raise water seal, purge with N2/CO2, verify CO/LEL/O2 at vents and work point
Display isolation tags; test again before hot work and every 2 h (verify).
Hot work on gas lines/holders: permit with fire watch, continuous gas monitoring, SCBA on standby, no work during gas pressure fluctuations; re-purge if readings rise.
Restoring gas: purge air from line with N2 until O2 < 1% (verify), then admit gas slowly; check for leaks with CO monitors; remove blinds under permit.
Furnace light-off: purge cycle complete, flame safeguard proven, operator at side of burner; never bypass; on flame failure, close gas and purge before relight.

Cast house/converter: during tapping only required crew in area, heat shields, dry tools/additives, no water lines leaking near runners; ladle/torpedo inspection before fill; breakout — alarm, evacuate, do not use water.
CO victim: do not enter without SCBA; rescue squad removes to fresh air, oxygen, CPR if needed, hospital (hyperbaric where available); treat as dangerous occurrence; investigate leak.
Coke ovens: door/lid emissions control, benzene monitoring, PPE, medical surveillance; gas cleaning plant and stove entries under confined-space permits.
Monthly: gas safety audit (monitors, seals, bleeders, permits), rescue drill, CO exposure review; annual: gas network integrity survey, valve/seal maintenance, training refresh.
ppe: Personal CO monitor and self-rescuer in gas areas; aluminised/FR clothing, face shields, heat gloves and spats in hot-metal areas; SCBA for rescue and gas crews; helmet, safety boots, hearing protection
stop: Person in gas area without CO monitor or alone
CO alarm active or fixed monitoring down in occupied area
Hot work on gas line without positive isolation, purge and gas test
Water seal below required head / goggle valve not closed
Water near molten-metal runners/ladles or wet charge
records: Gas permits and isolation records, purge/gas-test logs, fixed and personal CO monitor calibration, water-seal and bleeder logs
Rescue station checks and drills, CO exposure/medical surveillance, hot-metal breakout drills, incident and dangerous-occurrence reports

india: Factories Act ss.36, 37, 38, 41B–H via state rules / OSH Code Ch. XII; MSIHC Rules (CO/gas holder thresholds — verify); IS 17893 (permits); IS 11457; Sch. II (CO 50 ppm; benzene 1 ppm)
Third Schedule (CO poisoning notifiable); DGFASLI steel-plant safety guidelines; Steel Ministry Safety Guidelines (gas safety, hot metal) — MoS/SAIL safety codes; EC Act/CCTS (iron & steel)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (Rule 129 schedules); KSPCB; Ballari–Hospet steel cluster (JSW, Kirloskar) safety regimes; MAH Control (Karnataka) Rules 1994
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950; TN CIMAH Rules; DISH TN (Salem Steel, secondary steel units in Gummidipoondi)
osha: 1910.146, 1910.147, 1910.252 (hot work), 1910.1000 (CO 50 ppm), 1910.1028 (benzene), 1910.120; NFPA 86 (furnaces), NFPA 56 (fire and explosion prevention during cleaning and purging of flammable gas piping); ANSI Z49.1
intl: worldsteel Safety & Health guidance (gas safety, hot metal); EN 746-2 (industrial thermoprocessing — combustion & fuel handling safety)
UK HSE steel-industry gas-safety guidance (ISG), IGEM/SR/22 (purging); EIGA Doc 44 (nitrogen hazards); ISO 13577-2

t: Coal Handling Plants, Bunkers & Ash Handling
purpose: Prevent conveyor entanglement, coal-dust fires and explosions, bunker fires and CO, engulfment in bunkers/silos, and injuries in ash handling and ash-pond operations at thermal power plants and captive power units.
scope: Wagon tipplers and track hoppers, crushers, conveyors and transfer towers, stacker-reclaimers and stockyards, coal bunkers and feeders, coal mills (pulverisers), bottom-ash and fly-ash systems (ESP hoppers, silos, slurry/dense-phase), ash ponds/dykes, ash utilisation loading.
hazards: Conveyor nip points (the single largest injury source in CHP), belt cleaning and idler changes while running, falls from galleries, transfer-tower dust; wagon tippler/side-arm charger crush; track hopper engulfment
Coal dust explosions in crushers, transfer points, mills and bunker tops; spontaneous heating in stockpiles and bunkers (CO, fires); mill fires/puffs; hot work near dust

Bunker/silo entry: engulfment, CO/O2 deficiency, bridging, poking from inside; ash silos: hot fly ash (200 °C) flows like liquid — burns and engulfment; ESP hopper poking; compressed-air conveying ruptures
Ash ponds: dyke failure/breach (slurry flood), drowning, slurry pipeline bursts, dust storms from dry ponds; heat; noise; silica in ash (verify crystalline fraction)
pre: Conveyors: nip guards on head/tail/take-up/return idlers, pull-cords full length tested weekly, belt-sway and zero-speed switches, crossing bridges
Galleries with handrails and toe boards, no cleaning or idler change on running belt (LOTO), dust suppression/extraction at transfer points, housekeeping to prevent layers > 0.8 mm
Fire/explosion: DHA for coal dust (NFPA 652/85 benchmark), Ex-rated electricals in Zone 21/22 areas, CO and temperature monitoring in bunkers/silos
Inertisation (steam/CO2) for bunker fires, mill fire-fighting and inerting procedures, stockpile compaction and FIFO, thermal scanning, hot-work permit system covering CHP
Bunkers/silos: zero-entry policy; entry only with feed/discharge isolated (LOTO on feeders and conveyors), bridging assessment, atmosphere test (CO, O2, CH4), lifeline and retrieval, attendant
Poking from outside with air cannons/vibrators; ESP hoppers poked only with heater and isolation (hot ash)
Ash handling: fly-ash silo level/temperature monitoring, PRVs, dense-phase lines pressure-rated with blow-off protection, burns PPE; bottom-ash hopper quench
Ash pond dyke inspection (freeboard, seepage, piezometers), raised-dyke design per CEA/CPCB, emergency plan for breach; dust suppression on dry ponds/roads
Health: silica/coal-dust monitoring, respirators, audiometry, heat plan; training for all CHP staff and contractors; Form/registers per Factories Rules; EC/CCTS Scope 1 data from coal flow meters
steps: Shift start: walk conveyors — guards, pull-cords, spillage, hot spots (smell/thermal camera), bunker CO/temperature trends; tippler and stacker-reclaimer checks; log.
Belt operation: pre-start alarm, no persons on galleries at start; spillage cleared only with belt stopped and isolated or from outside guards with tools; never cross belts except at bridges.
Idler/belt maintenance: LOTO at MCC and local isolator, belt clamped, counterweight secured; splicing with vulcaniser under hot-work rules; guards refitted.
Dust: sprays on at transfer points, extraction filters maintained, vacuum/wash-down housekeeping; no compressed-air blow-down; hot work only after cleaning and permit.
Bunker fire/heating (CO rising, temperature > limit): stop feed, inert with steam/CO2, run bunker down to mill under controlled conditions, no opening of doors, fire crew ready
Mill fire — follow OEM inerting/isolation, no water jets into mill.
Bunker/silo entry: only after all alternatives, permit, isolations verified, bridging checked from top with camera, lifeline/winch, attendant; never below hanging material.
Stockyard: compaction, temperature probing, reclaim hot spots first, keep stockpile slopes within machine limits; stacker-reclaimer exclusion zones; dust suppression.

Fly-ash: silo unloading to closed tankers with level/pressure watch, dust-free loading spouts, burns PPE; ESP hopper evacuation with heaters, poking only from outside with isolation; dense-phase line inspection.

Ash pond: daily dyke inspection (freeboard ≥ 1 m — verify, seepage, cracks), slurry pipeline patrol, no entry into pond area alone, lifebuoys at decant structures, rain-season emergency plan, dust control on dry areas.
Monthly: conveyor guard/pull-cord audit, Ex equipment check, bunker/silo entry review, fire-system tests, dust monitoring; annual: dyke stability review, DHA update, training refresh.
ppe: Helmet, safety boots, FFP3 respirators in dusty areas, safety glasses/goggles, gloves, hearing protection
Harness and lifeline for bunker/silo/gallery work, heat-resistant PPE for ash hoppers/silos, lifejacket at ash pond water edges
stop: Work on running conveyor near nip points
Pull-cord or guard missing on a running belt
Bunker CO/temperature alarm ignored or inerting unavailable
Bunker/silo entry without isolation, lifeline and attendant
Ash-pond dyke freeboard/seepage outside limits
records: Conveyor inspection and pull-cord tests, LOTO records, bunker CO/temperature logs, hot-work permits, confined-space entry permits
Ex equipment register, dust and silica monitoring, fire-system tests, ash pond inspection and piezometer records, incident log

india: Factories Act ss.21–22, 36, 37 via state rules / OSH Code; Electricity Act/CEA (Technical Standards for Construction & Safety of thermal plants) 2023 regs; CPCB fly-ash notification (utilisation
Ash pond norms) & EP Rules; Sch. II (coal dust, silica); IS/IEC 60079-10-2; IS 11592 (belt conveyors — verify); CEA guidelines on ash dyke design & safety; EC Act/CCTS (thermal power)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969; KSPCB (ash pond consents, fly-ash); KPCL (RTPS/BTPS) safety procedures
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950; TNPCB (NCTPS, MTPS ash ponds); TANGEDCO safety rules; DISH TN
osha: 1910.212, 1910.219, 1910.147, 1910.146, 1910.269 (generation), 1910.1053; NFPA 85 (boiler & combustion systems hazards, pulverised fuel), NFPA 652/654, NFPA 120 (coal mines — benchmark); EPA CCR rule (ash ponds — benchmark)
intl: EN 620 (conveyors), EN 1127-1; UK HSE conveyor guidance (nip points) & coal-handling fire guidance; VDI 2263; ICOLD tailings/ash dam guidance; ISO 45001

t: Loading Docks, Yard Traffic & Trailer Loading
purpose: Prevent forklift drive-offs, trailer creep, dock-edge falls, pedestrian strikes and manual-handling injuries at warehouse and factory loading docks, tail-lifts and yards.
scope: Dock doors, levellers and plates, vehicle restraints, trailer and container loading/unloading, tail-lifts, yard traffic (trucks, LCVs, forklifts, pedestrians), drivers' waiting areas, night and peak operations, reefer trailers, cross-docks and dark stores.
hazards: Forklift drives off dock edge or into gap when trailer creeps/pulls away during loading; trailer landing-gear collapse; dock leveller falls
Pedestrians (loaders, drivers) struck by forklifts/trucks in yard; drivers walking between vehicles; reversing trucks; poor lighting/rain
Falls from dock edge (1.2 m) and from trailer beds/tail-lifts; crush at tail-lift; loads falling from trailers (shifted cargo, container doors springing open)
Manual handling of cases/bags, awkward postures in trailers; heat in containers (50 °C+); CO from diesel forklifts in trailers; reefer unit noise; security/theft incidents
pre: Dock equipment: levellers with lip and maintenance props, dock plates rated and secured, vehicle restraints (wheel-lock/hook) with communication lights or wheel chocks plus 'keys-to-loader' rule
Dock bumpers, edge guards/barriers at unused doors, lighting ≥ 100 lux (verify) in trailers and docks

Yard traffic plan: one-way flow, marked truck lanes and pedestrian walkways, drivers' waiting room, speed limit ≤ 10 km/h, reversing with banksman or cameras, mirrors at blind corners, no pedestrians in reversing zones
Night lighting and hi-vis for all
Procedures: loading sequence (restrain → check trailer floor and landing gear → inspect load → load → release)
Container door opening from the side with door-restraint strap, tail-lift operation by trained persons only with exclusion area, forklift capacity vs trailer floor rating
Manual handling: pallet jacks, conveyors/extendable belts into trailers, lifting aids, two-person rule for > 25 kg (verify site limit), rotation
Heat plan for container unloading; CO limits — electric forklifts in enclosed trailers or ventilation
Security and welfare: driver check-in, ID, drivers stay in waiting area, toilets/water for drivers; first aid; incident reporting including visiting drivers
steps: Vehicle arrival: marshal directs to door, driver reverses with banksman/cameras, engine off, brake on; keys handed to dock office or restraint engaged and light turned green.
Before loading: check trailer floor condition, landing gear/stands (use trailer stand for dropped trailers), restraint/chocks in place, leveller lip on trailer bed
Open container doors from side with strap, check for shifted load.
Loading/unloading: forklift drives straight on/off at walking pace, horn at entry, forks low; loaders out of trailer while forklift inside; stack and strap loads per plan; no climbing on loads.
Tail-lift: operator trained, platform rated, load secured, nobody on platform except operator where permitted, exclusion area; stow before driving.
Pedestrians: use walkways, stay out of trailer path; drivers remain in waiting area until released; no walking in yard lanes.
Completion: forklift out, leveller stored, restraint released only after confirmation, keys returned, light red; driver checks load securing before departure.
Dock doors not in use: barrier/chain across edge; levellers in stored position; good housekeeping (no pallets/wrap on floor).
Weather: wet docks — non-slip surfaces, extra care at edges; wind — container doors secured; heat — rest/water for trailer work.
Maintenance: monthly leveller/restraint inspection, bumpers, lighting, floor condition; forklift daily checks; yard markings repainted.
Weekly: near-miss review (drive-offs, creep, pedestrian conflicts), driver feedback; quarterly yard traffic audit; training refresh for loaders and marshals.
ppe: Hi-vis, safety shoes, gloves, helmet where overhead risk, knee pads for container unloading, sun protection; hearing protection near reefers
stop: Trailer not restrained/chocked and keys not controlled before forklift entry
Pedestrian in yard lane or trailer with forklift moving
Dock leveller or plate damaged/unsecured
Container doors opened without restraint strap or from front
Trailer landing gear/floor unsafe
records: Vehicle restraint/chock logs or key register, dock equipment inspections, forklift checks and operator authorisations, yard traffic plan and audits, driver induction records, near-miss/incident log, manual-handling training

india: Factories Act s.7A (safe workplace), s.34 (weights) via state rules / OSH Code s.6; MV Act 1988 (vehicles in premises)
Shops & Establishments Acts (warehouses); IS 15298 (footwear); pit-racking (forklift codes); NBC Part 4 (storage occupancy)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969; Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act; RTO Karnataka
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950; TN Shops & Establishments Act; RTO TN
osha: 1910.178 (forklifts — dock boards, trailer restraints 1910.178(k)/(m)), 1910.26 (dockboards), 1910.176, 1910.28 (dock edges), 1910.1000 (CO); ANSI MH30.1 (dock levellers), ANSI/ITSDF B56.1
intl: UK HSE HSG136 (workplace transport), 'Delivering safely' guidance, Loading dock guidance (LOLER for tail-lifts), EN 1756 (tail-lifts), EN 1398 (dock levellers); ISO 45001

t: Heat Treatment – Furnaces, Quench Tanks, Salt Baths & Protective Atmospheres
purpose: Prevent burns, quench-oil fires, explosions of protective/endothermic atmospheres, salt-bath eruptions, CO poisoning and crane/charge incidents in heat-treatment shops and in-house hardening lines.
scope: Batch, continuous, sealed-quench and pit furnaces; carburising/nitriding with endothermic gas, ammonia or methanol; vacuum furnaces; induction hardening; oil/polymer/water quench tanks; salt baths (neutral, nitrate/nitrite, cyanide); tempering; washing lines.
hazards: Protective atmospheres (endothermic gas: 20% CO, 40% H2; dissociated ammonia
Methanol): explosion if air enters furnace below 760 °C (verify) or on power/gas failure without purge; CO leaks at doors/flame curtains; ammonia and methanol toxicity/fire

Quench: oil quench fires when load not fully submerged, water contamination of oil (steam explosion), low oil level, high oil temperature near flash point; polymer/water quench steam; hot load dropping from crane/manipulator
Salt baths: moisture/organics in nitrate–nitrite salts → eruptions/explosions; cyanide salts (HCN with acid/water, toxicity); hot salt splashes 500–900 °C; vapour/fume
Burns from furnace doors, charge baskets, radiant heat; falls into pit furnaces/quench tanks; induction HF/EMF and cooling-water leaks; vacuum furnace implosion/ nitrogen asphyxia; heat stress
pre: Furnaces per NFPA 86 benchmark: safety-ventilated or inert-purged atmospheres, burn-off pilots/flame curtains at doors, interlocks (low temperature, low gas/air pressure
Power failure) that purge with nitrogen before atmosphere admitted or removed, flame safeguards on burners and generators, gas-train double block-and-bleed, CO monitoring in shop with ventilation
Quench tanks: oil level and temperature interlocks (prevent quench when oil < minimum level or > set temperature
Flash point margin ≥ 50 °C — verify), agitation, cooling, covers/lids with CO2 or dry-powder fixed suppression, drain/ bund, water ingress prevention, no water lines above tanks
Load fully submerged by design; emergency hoist power
Salt baths: dry pre-heated work and tools, covered storage of salts, no cyanide and nitrate baths adjacent, fume extraction
PPE (face shield, aluminised apron/gloves), spill tools, cyanide antidote kit and trained first aiders where cyanide used
Salt disposal as hazardous waste
Charging: baskets and fixtures inspected (creep/cracks), crane/manipulator capacity, lifting gear rated for temperature, exclusion zones during transfer, pit-furnace and tank guardrails/covers
Ammonia/methanol storage per gas/petroleum rules; nitrogen with O2 monitors in enclosed areas
Training for atmosphere furnaces (start-up, shutdown, power failure), fire drills (quench fire), medical surveillance (CO, ammonia, cyanide)
steps: Start-up: verify interlocks, purge with N2 to O2 < 1% (verify) before admitting endothermic gas, light pilots/flame curtains, check generator; log.
Running: keep doors closed except loading; monitor CO in shop; respond to interlock alarms — never bypass; on power or gas failure follow emergency purge procedure and evacuate until atmosphere safe.
Loading/unloading: inspect baskets, position crane/manipulator, exclusion zone, transfer hot load directly to quench without delay; no one between furnace and tank.
Quench: confirm oil level/temperature and agitation before transfer; submerge fully; on fire — keep load submerged, close lid, operate suppression, isolate heaters, do not use water; evacuate smoke.
Salt baths: dry work and tools over bath before immersion, lower slowly, keep face away; skim with dry tools; add salt in small dry amounts; cyanide — PPE, no acid nearby, waste controlled.
Shutdown: purge atmosphere with N2, burn off, cool with doors closed; confirm CO low before opening; isolate gas and lock.
Maintenance/entry: furnace cooled, atmosphere purged, gas isolated and locked, confined-space permit for furnace interior, refractory dust (ceramic fibre — RCF) controls, hot-work permit
Induction units isolated and capacitors discharged.
Gas/chemical storage: ammonia cylinders/tanks per gas rules with leak detection; methanol per Petroleum Rules; nitrogen and endo gas lines labelled; LPG/PNG gas trains tested yearly.
Waste: quench oil, salts, washing-line effluent as hazardous waste under HOWM; cyanide waste detoxified before disposal.
Monthly: interlock and flame-safeguard tests, oil flash-point/water-content checks, suppression inspection, CO monitor calibration, PPE audit, drill
Annual: furnace safety audit (NFPA 86 style), lifting gear tests, medical surveillance.
ppe: Face shield with heat-resistant visor, aluminised apron/sleeves/gloves, FR clothing, safety boots (metatarsal)
Hearing protection, CO monitor in atmosphere-furnace area, respirator for salt fume/RCF dust, cyanide first-aid awareness
stop: Atmosphere admitted below safe temperature or interlock bypassed
Quench oil low/hot or water contamination suspected
Wet work or tools near salt bath
CO alarm in shop or flame curtain out
Basket/fixture cracked or crane gear not rated for hot loads
records: Furnace interlock/flame-safeguard tests, purge logs, CO monitor calibration, quench oil tests, suppression and extinguisher inspections
Basket/lifting gear inspections, salt bath logs, hot-work/confined-space permits, HW manifests, medical surveillance, drill records

india: Factories Act ss.21, 31, 36, 37, 38 via state rules / OSH Code; Gas Cylinders Rules 2016 (ammonia); Petroleum Rules 2002 (methanol, quench oil Class C); PNGRB/IS 6044 (gas supply)
Sch. II (CO 50 ppm, ammonia 25 ppm, cyanide 5 mg/m³, RCF); HOWM Rules; IS 9474; foundry-codes (state dangerous-operations schedules — heat treatment/cyanide)
ka: Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (Rule 129 schedules — cyanide/heat treatment — verify); DFBISH; KSPCB
tn: TN Factories Rules 1950 (Rule 95 schedules); DISH TN; TNPCB; Coimbatore/Hosur heat-treatment clusters
osha: 1910.1000 (CO, HCN), 1910.147, 1910.146, 1910.212; NFPA 86 (ovens & furnaces — Class A/B/C/D), NFPA 30 (quench oil), NFPA 12 (CO2 systems); ANSI Z49.1
intl: EN 746-1/-2/-3 (industrial thermoprocessing equipment — combustion, atmosphere gases), EN 1127-1; UK HSE heat-treatment guidance (salt baths, quench-oil fires), COSHH; ISO 13577 series

t: Retail Fuel Outlets & Site Fuel Dispensing – Tank-Lorry Decanting, Dispensers, CNG
purpose: Prevent fires, explosions, vapour exposure and vehicle incidents during tank-lorry decantation, dispensing of petrol/diesel/CNG/LPG-auto, tank gauging and maintenance at retail outlets, captive fuel stations and construction-site fuel points.
scope: Retail outlets (PSU/private), captive bunks in plants/mines/ports, construction-site skid tanks and bowsers, CNG compressor/dispensing stations, auto-LPG; underground/above-ground tanks, dispensers, vapour recovery, forecourt traffic, generators, hot work and tank maintenance.
hazards: Petrol (Class A) vapour ignition during decanting and dispensing: static from hose/nozzle, mobile phones, running engines, smoking, hot vehicle parts; vapour pooling in pits/drains; spills
Tank-lorry decantation: wrong-tank/wrong-product connections, overfill, hose rupture, lorry moving while connected, lightning
Tank-lorry fires; underground tank leaks contaminating groundwater; dip-pipe/manhole chamber confined space
CNG: 200–250 bar gas — cylinder/hose rupture, jet fire, compressor room explosion, cascades; auto-LPG BLEVE on tank fire; forecourt traffic strikes on attendants; robbery/violence at night
Site fuel points: bowser/skid tanks without bunds or earthing, refuelling hot machines, jerry-can filling, diesel exposure/dermatitis
pre: Licences and layout per Petroleum Rules 2002 (Form XIV/XV — verify) and OISD-STD-117/118 benchmarks (retail outlet safety distances
Electricals in Zone 1/2, earthing pits ≤ 1 Ω for lorry/tank earthing — verify), Gas Cylinders/SMPV Rules and PNGRB T4S for CNG
Vapour-recovery stage I/II where mandated (CPCB); CEIG for electricals

Equipment: dispensers with breakaway couplings and auto shut-off nozzles, emergency shut-off switch (ESD) for dispensers and CNG, flame arresters/vents, overfill prevention (level gauging/high-level alarm)
Earthing clamp and bonding point for lorries, Ex-rated lighting/pumps, extinguishers (DCP 9 kg ×4 at least per outlet — verify) and sand buckets, spill kits, 'no smoking/engine off/phone off' signage
Decantation SOP: two persons, lorry earthed and chocked, engine off, compartment seals/dip verified, correct product–tank identification (colour codes/labels)
Hose check, continuous watch, no dispensing from the tank being filled, weather (no decanting during lightning), night lighting
Staff trained (OMC safety training), uniforms antistatic cotton, first aid, fire drill quarterly
Forecourt traffic layout (one-way, speed ≤ 10 km/h, pedestrian paths); CNG compressor room ventilation, gas detection, PRVs, hose inspection/replacement schedule
Site fuel points (construction/mines): bunded skid tanks/bowsers with earthing, PESO licence above exemption, refuelling of cold engines only
No jerry cans except approved safety cans, spill kits, extinguishers, fire-safe distance from camps and hot work
steps: Lorry arrival: position at decant bay, engine off, chocks, earth clamp attached before any hatch/hose; verify invoice vs compartments, seals, dip/density; attendant and crew stay throughout.
Decanting: connect hose to correct tank fill point (verify label), open valves slowly, monitor level/overfill alarm, no vehicle refuelling at adjacent dispensers of that tank
Stop on spill/leak; disconnect and cap, record quantity and dip.

Dispensing: customer engine off, no phones/smoking, nozzle in contact with filler neck (bonding), no overfilling or topping-off, two-wheeler riders dismount; stop on spill; no filling of plastic containers unless approved.
Spill: stop pump, isolate ignition, absorb with sand/absorbent, dispose as hazardous waste; vapour cloud → evacuate forecourt, ESD, call fire service.

Fire: ESD, extinguishers on small fires, evacuate, call fire service (101/112), move vehicles away if safe; CNG/LPG jet fire — do not extinguish flame, isolate supply, cool surroundings, evacuate 100 m+.
Tank gauging/dip: by trained person with antistatic rope/tape, after settling time; manhole chambers entered only under confined-space permit (vapour).
CNG: pre-shift check of compressor room gas detection, hoses, nozzles, PRVs; fill with vehicle engine off and cylinder test date verified; stop on hissing/odour.

Maintenance/hot work: PTW, gas-free certificate for tanks/lines, Ex equipment reinstated; tank cleaning per tank-cleaning procedure; leak detection/tightness tests for USTs periodically (verify interval).
Night operations: lighting, two attendants, CCTV, cash control, panic alarm; women attendants' safety per state rules.
Monthly: extinguisher/earthing/ESD checks, dispenser calibration, vapour-recovery function, staff drill; annual: PESO/OMC inspection, electrical inspection, UST tightness test.

t: LPG Bottling Plants & Bulk LPG Installations
purpose: Prevent LPG releases, flash fires, BLEVE and vapour-cloud explosions at cylinder bottling plants, bulk storage (mounded/above-ground bullets), tank-lorry gantries and industrial bulk LPG installations.
scope: LPG receipt by tank-lorry/pipeline, mounded and above-ground bullets, pumps/compressors, carousel filling, cylinder evacuation and testing, valve change, leak testing, cylinder storage sheds, loading/unloading gantries, fire-water systems, industrial bulk tanks and vaporisers.
roles: Shift in-charge and operators (trained per OISD)
hazards: LPG vapour (heavier than air, flammable 1.8–9.5%) from hose/valve/flange leaks, cylinder valve leaks, overfilled cylinders (hydraulic rupture when warmed), pump seal failure
Ignition by static, non-Ex equipment, vehicles, phones
BLEVE of bullets or tank-lorries under fire impingement; vapour-cloud explosion in congested filling sheds; jet fires at gantries; frost burns from liquid LPG
Cylinder handling: manual lifting 30–50 kg, falling stacks, conveyor nips, carousel moving parts, valve-change tools; cylinder evacuation of defective cylinders; hydro-test pit
Tank-lorry movement with hose connected, brake failure in gantry; lightning; monsoon flooding of bunds; security/sabotage; MAH off-site consequences (Vizag 1997 HPCL, benchmark incidents)
pre: Licences/standards: PESO licence under Gas Cylinders Rules 2016 and SMPV(U) Rules 2016
Layout and safety distances per OISD-STD-144 (LPG bottling plants), OISD-STD-150 (mounded storage), OISD-STD-169 (small LPG installations)
MSIHC/Chemical Accidents Rules (MAH site: safety report, on-site/off-site plans, mock drills); CEIG electrical; hazardous-area classification with Ex equipment (IS 5572/60079)

Fixed protection: gas detectors (alarm 20% LEL, trip/ESD 40% — verify) across sheds, gantries and storage, ESD system isolating pumps/compressors and remote-operated valves (ROVs) on bullets and gantries
Excess-flow and back-check valves, water deluge/sprinklers on bullets, cylinder sheds and gantries (OISD-116/144 rates), fire-water storage/pumps, monitors, hydrants
Lightning/earthing; wind socks
Operations: SOPs for receipt, filling (electronic scales with check weighing, auto cut-off), leak testing (water bath/detector)
Valve change (cylinder evacuated), evacuation of defective cylinders to flare/recovery, hydro-test
Static bonding of lorries; two-person rule; no hot work without permit and gas-free; mobile phones/vehicles restricted to designated zones

Tank-lorries: PESO-approved vehicles, driver training (OISD-GDN-207 style — verify), wheel chocks, earthing, engine off, hose inspection (test date), excess-flow/breakaway, no parking of loaded lorries in plant
Night loading only where licensed
Emergency: on-site plan with ERT, SCBA, PPE, foam/DCP, mutual aid with OMC plants and fire service, off-site plan with District Crisis Group, siren and evacuation routes, drills 6-monthly
Medical for frost burns; security (CISF/private) per PESO
steps: Shift start: gas detector panel, ESD/ROV test (periodic), fire pumps auto-start, deluge valves, hydrant pressure, wind sock, housekeeping; log.
Lorry unloading: position, chock, earth, engine off, driver out; connect liquid/vapour hoses after inspection, open valves slowly, leak check with soap/detector
Operator present throughout; disconnect, cap, release earth, remove chocks; record quantity.
Filling: cylinders inspected (due date, valve, body damage) before carousel; fill by weight with auto cut-off
Check-weigh 100% (verify); overfilled → evacuate; leak test every cylinder at valve/bung; seal and stack ≤ height limit on pallets.

Leaking/defective cylinders: move to designated outdoor evacuation area, evacuate LPG via recovery system (no venting to atmosphere), valve change by trained person with evacuated cylinder, hydro-test per schedule.
Cylinder sheds and storage: upright, valve caps, segregation of full/empty, no ignition sources within distance, forklifts Ex-rated or outside, lighting Ex.
Leak response: gas alarm → stop operations, ESD, isolate source, disperse vapour with water curtains/monitors, no ignition, evacuate crosswind, ERT in PPE/SCBA
Do not extinguish a jet fire until gas isolated; cool exposed tanks.
Fire on tank-lorry/bullet: activate deluge, evacuate 500 m+ (BLEVE), fire service and District Crisis Group alert, off-site plan; do not approach impinged vessel.

Maintenance: PTW, isolation (double block, blind), depressurise and purge (N2) before opening; gas-free test; Ex equipment reinstated (IEC 60079-17 inspection); instrument/ESD function tests per schedule.
Manual handling: rollers/conveyors, lifting aids, two-person for stacking, gloves; carousel guards and e-stops.

Audits and drills: monthly safety audit (OISD-144 checklist), 6-monthly mock drill with district authorities, PESO/OMC inspections, safety report update, training refresh; incident investigation and MSIHC reporting.
ppe: Antistatic FR coveralls, conductive safety boots, cotton inner wear, leather gloves (cryogenic for liquid LPG), face shield/goggles, helmet; SCBA and fire suits for ERT; no synthetic clothing
stop: Gas detector alarm or ESD/deluge impairment without compensating measures
